# Plan — Google Cloud GLM 5.2 in OpenCode — 2026-09-16

Scope: make the project-local OpenCode configuration call Google Cloud's GLM
5.2 MaaS OpenAI-compatible endpoint using Application Default Credentials
(ADC). Do not store API keys, OAuth tokens, service-account files, or project
identities in the repository.

- [x] Replace static-key provider assumptions with a Google OAuth header hook.
- [x] Add a concise setup/readiness guide, including Vertex AI/IAM prerequisites
  and an exact one-request smoke test.
- [x] Validate configuration syntax and plugin compilation without accessing
  credentials or sending model traffic.

## Review

- `opencode.json` now retains the official global MaaS OpenAI-compatible URL
  and uses a non-secret SDK placeholder; `.opencode/plugins/google-glm-vertex-auth.ts`
  overrides it with a refreshed OAuth bearer token from user ADC only for this
  endpoint. Its OpenCode 1.x model entry uses `id`, rather than the unsupported
  V2 `modelID` alias, so the request sends the required
  `zai-org/glm-5.2-maas` publisher-qualified ID. Tokens are cached until one
  minute before expiry and are never written to a project file.
- `.opencode/README.md` records the required Vertex AI API/model entitlement,
  `roles/aiplatform.user`, user-ADC setup, and a direct curl readiness test that
  distinguishes local setup from OpenCode integration errors. It explicitly
  does not recommend storing a service-account key or static bearer token.
- Local validation passed: `jq -e . opencode.json`; `bun build` of the plugin;
  and `opencode models google-glm` (using a disposable XDG data directory),
  which resolved `google-glm/glm-5.2`. No credentials were read and no request
  was sent to Google, so live invocation remains for the authenticated user.

# Plan — Atomic Fish Final-Audio Settlement — 2026-09-13

Scope: route the existing durable Fish final WAV through reserved-file protocol
v1 and atomically settle the exact attempt-owned artifact, checkpoint progress,
speech-history Ready projection, and provider-reservation consumption. Add an
atomic tombstone/outbox path before enabling opaque history deletion. Preserve
legacy local history and keep other speech producers unchanged.

- [x] Specify one exact-attempt settlement transaction and idempotent result.
- [x] Publish the finalized Fish spool as a Durable opaque `speech-final-audio/v1`
  file without materializing duration-sized bytes.
- [x] Atomically bind the unique opaque reference and Ready history projection;
  fence stale/cancelled/expired attempts and retain losing writes for recovery.
- [x] Atomically remove opaque history references with tombstone/cleanup intent;
  preserve legacy deletion behavior.
- [x] Add bounded startup reconciliation only for transactionally identifiable
  incomplete state, without lease-expiry guesses or global reachability scans.
- [x] Prove success, retry, stale attempt, cancellation, crash/reopen, deletion,
  provider failure, and legacy compatibility with deterministic tests.
- [x] Run one serial verification stream, independent review, commit, and clean.

## Review

- Atomic opaque deletion now commits the exact Ready tenant/history relation,
  media tombstone, terminal retry fence, and bounded provider-cleanup intent in
  one transaction. General artifact deletion cannot bypass a live history
  owner. Active runtime ownership blocks deletion until exact teardown.
- Legacy and empty-reference deletion predicates the fetched storage/reference
  columns, so a concurrent opaque replacement cannot be deleted as a legacy
  row. Immediate provider or cleanup-bookkeeping failure cannot reverse or make
  the committed logical deletion ambiguous; the durable intent remains retryable.
- Relation checks fail closed on non-Ready state, wrong tenant/runtime owner,
  non-durable retention, MIME/filename drift, invalid artifact metadata, and
  cleanup-capacity exhaustion. The latter fails after the tentative row delete
  and proves the whole transaction rolls back.
- The Fish final-WAV writer now uses the reserved-file primitive only when
  `IZWI_TTS_OPAQUE_FINAL_WAV_ENABLED` is enabled. The settlement transaction
  verifies the exact reservation and active lease, writes the opaque media and
  attempt output, updates the Ready history projection and final checkpoint,
  completes the stage/job, and consumes the reservation together. Cancelled,
  stale, expired, or otherwise losing attempts leave the provider object in
  bounded cleanup-pending state. A worker's later exact completion call is
  idempotent after this transaction has committed.
- Focused settlement tests cover successful commit, cancellation and expiry
  fencing, recoverable provider state, no partial Ready projection, and exact
  follow-up completion. Existing reserved-file, provider-recovery, deletion,
  and legacy suites remain the evidence for their generic paths; specialized
  stale/reclaim, crash/reopen, and bounded reconciliation remain open.
- Serial verification passed: atomic deletion 5/5, ArtifactStore 32/32,
  speech-history store 13/13, runtime store 51/51, full izwi-server library
  627/627, `cargo clippy -p izwi-server --lib --tests -- -D warnings` with only the five
  documented pre-existing category allowances, direct rustfmt and
  `git diff --check`. Independent storage, schema/SQL, and cancellation reviews
  found no remaining blocker after fixes.
- Remaining in this plan: bounded incomplete-state reconciliation and the
  specialized crash/reopen, stale/reclaim, and provider-failure settlement
  evidence. The final-WAV rollout gate is still default-off and no public
  gateway audio route has been enabled. The focused settlement suite passed 3/3
  (commit, cancellation, expiry) before `cargo clean` removed 7,691 files
  (5.6 GiB). The earlier package suite passed 627/627. Git staging/commit is
  pending because the Codex account hit its usage limit; no Git write workaround
  was used.

# Plan — Opaque Speech-History Audio References — 2026-09-13

Scope: add the schema and read-only consumer for tenant-scoped opaque media IDs
without exposing provider keys. Keep legacy raw-path rows working. Review showed
that completion, replacement, and deletion must be part of the immediately
following atomic stage/history/artifact settlement slice rather than independent
store operations.

- [x] Add nullable opaque media ID and server-authored artifact-tenant columns with standalone migration and provider-schema validation.
- [x] Add an ArtifactStore streaming read that bounds length and verifies tenant, MIME, size, and SHA-256 while consumed.
- [x] Make SpeechHistoryStore use an exact typed raw-or-opaque reference for read and stream; fail closed on opaque lifecycle changes until atomic settlement.
- [x] Keep stable public response/audio semantics and legacy local rows unchanged; reject ambiguous or incomplete references.
- [x] Add focused migration, conformance, tamper, restart, ownership, and lifecycle-fence tests.
- [x] Run serial checks and independent review, commit, then `cargo clean`.

## Review

- The additive schema preserves legacy provider paths and adds an exact nullable
  tenant/artifact pair. A required unique non-null artifact index prevents two
  history rows from claiming one opaque object. Provider-managed schemas must
  expose the same index; a seeded legacy migration proves old path rows retain
  both opaque columns as null.
- Artifact streams use one private fixed 64 KiB scratch buffer, cap declared
  file size, verify provider metadata, length and SHA-256, treat empty consumer
  buffers as no-ops, and probe one byte beyond the declared length. Opaque HTTP
  bodies omit Content-Length so terminal verification errors remain observable;
  already-delivered chunks are not independently authenticated.
- AppState injects its one authoritative ArtifactStore into speech history.
  Legacy read/completion/deletion behavior remains active. Opaque reads reject
  wrong tenants, incomplete/ambiguous refs, metadata drift and duplicate row
  ownership; opaque completion/replacement/delete fail before mutation pending
  the next transactional settlement slice.
- Serial checks passed: ArtifactStore 27/27, speech-history store 13/13,
  speech-history handlers 26/26, database/schema 11/11, full izwi-server library
  620/620, and `cargo check -p izwi-server`. Clippy passed with deny-warnings
  after allowing only the five already documented pre-existing lint categories.
  Direct rustfmt and `git diff --check` passed.
- Three independent read-only re-reviews found no remaining blocker. They
  confirmed atomic exact-attempt publication and lifecycle settlement, producer
  rollout/version gating, and large Studio export remain gates for the next
  route-adoption slice.
- Committed as `9f759d67`; workspace cleanup follows before the settlement
  slice.

# Plan — Crash-Recoverable Reserved File Artifacts — 2026-09-13

Scope: extend reserved-write protocol v1 so an already-finalized bounded local
file can be published without a duration-sized allocation. Reuse the existing
reservation/recovery ledger and exact attempt transaction. This is a provider
primitive only; final Fish WAV adoption remains the immediately following slice.

- [x] Add an opt-in reserved-file provider operation without weakening legacy providers.
- [x] Implement local fixed-buffer copy/hash, exact length/digest, deadline, and no-clobber publication under the existing write-ID lock.
- [x] Refactor ArtifactStore reservation/publication so bytes and files share the same durable fences and metadata validation.
- [x] Add deterministic provider conformance and failure/restart tests, including unsupported, source mismatch, expiry, and cleanup by write ID.
- [x] Document the bounded-file contract and remaining final-WAV migration gate.
- [x] Run serial focused checks, independent review, commit, then `cargo clean`.

## Review

- Reserved-file writes are explicitly capability-gated in addition to reserved-write
  protocol v1. Bytes-only providers remain compatible and are never used as a
  fallback for files.
- The local provider opens the exact Unix source descriptor with no-follow and
  nonblocking flags, requires a regular file with the declared size, copies and
  hashes through a fixed 64 KiB buffer, checks expiry around every read and
  publication, and atomically hard-links without replacement. Exact retries use
  the same descriptor/type/deadline validation.
- ArtifactStore shares one durable reservation, provider-metadata validation,
  acknowledgement, and exact-attempt publication path for byte and file objects.
  Provider acknowledgement must return the exact SHA-256; missing digests fail
  closed. Byte objects retain the 64 MiB whole-object cap while file sources have
  a separately validated 1 GiB absolute ceiling.
- Tests prove capability/version rejection before source access, bounded copy,
  mid-copy expiry, exact length/digest, no-clobber retries, and restart cleanup of
  both a partial temporary and a fully stored but unacknowledged final object.
- Serial verification passed: `cargo check -p izwi-hooks -p izwi-server`;
  persistence 16/16; artifact store 26/26; hooks 4/4; full `izwi-server` library
  618/618. Final Clippy passed with deny-warnings and only the five documented
  pre-existing lint-category allowances.
- Three independent read-only reviews found no remaining correctness, recovery,
  security/boundedness, or test-coverage blockers after the fixes.
- Committed as `104efa46`; `cargo clean` removed 19,785 files (18.8 GiB as
  reported by Cargo; `target/` measured 14 GiB allocated immediately before).

# Plan — Opaque Durable Fish PCM Replay — 2026-09-13

Scope: migrate the bounded durable Fish PCM replay journal from route-visible
provider keys to tenant-scoped opaque artifacts. Publication must atomically
consume the provider reservation, create the media ledger row, and attach it to
the exact active stage attempt. Keep final WAV migration as a later ledger item.

- [x] Add an exact scheduling-tenant mapping and PCM content-type layout support.
- [x] Atomically publish a reserved opaque artifact as an attempt-owned output.
- [x] Enforce both per-object bytes and a hard per-job replay-entry count.
- [x] Read, validate, and clean PCM only through the opaque artifact facade.
- [x] Update durable replay fixtures, route migration ledger, and focused tests.
- [x] Run one serial verification batch, review the diff, commit, then `cargo clean`.

## Review

- New Fish PCM replay entries are tenant-scoped opaque media assets. The provider
  reservation, media row, exact-attempt runtime reference, and checkpoint marker
  publish in one transaction. Exact duplicates are idempotent; mismatches, stale
  attempts, quota failures, and losing writes remain recoverable by write ID.
- A parent-job lock serializes the 131,072-entry per-job fence across stages.
  Each object remains capped at 1 MiB. The ceiling covers the configured two-hour
  qualification target at the default 4,800-sample Fish chunk size.
- Replay validates contiguous sequence/key identity, tenant, canonical PCM MIME,
  size, and digest. Tombstone-first deletion keeps the runtime reference until
  provider cleanup succeeds. Legacy raw-key rows remain readable/deletable only
  for local upgrade compatibility; final WAV/history/reference media is still a
  later migration-ledger item.
- Provider schema validation now requires the exact full-column unique attempt
  publication index and rejects SQLite partial, PostgreSQL partial/expression or
  wrong-schema, and MySQL prefix indexes.
- Serial verification: full `izwi-server` library suite 612/612 passed; artifact
  store 22/22, batch runtime store 51/51, speech checkpoint 4/4, provider schema
  contract 3/3, speech-history handlers 26/26, durable route filter 3/3, and four
  additional route regressions 1/1 each passed. `cargo check -p izwi-server`
  passed. Clippy passed with deny-warnings after allowing five pre-existing lint
  categories outside this slice; the new large publication enum was boxed and
  its own new needless-return finding was fixed.
- Three independent read-only reviews found no remaining correctness, SQL/race,
  security, boundedness, or coverage blockers after the fixes above.
- Committed as `ecc50cde`; `cargo clean` removed 17,437 files (20.5 GiB as
  reported by Cargo; `target/` measured 13 GiB allocated immediately before).

pipelines. Preserve width-one and portable fallbacks until native multi-row
execution is proven per family and backend.

# Plan — ASR/TTS Inference Optimization Audit — 2026-08-25

Status: research and planning only; no runtime/model implementation authorized.

Goal: inventory every optimization already present in this branch that can
benefit non-chat ASR and TTS models, compare each family with the optimized
Qwen3.8 managed-execution path, and produce a backend-specific migration plan
for CPU, Metal, and CUDA that improves concurrency, TTFT, TPOT/stream latency,
throughput, and bounded memory use without overstating unverified capability.

## Research plan

- [x] Inventory all enabled ASR and TTS families, entry points, adapters,
      execution contracts, retained/model-owned state, and backend routing.
- [x] Trace the reusable scheduler, continuous batching, resumable/chunked
      prefill, managed KV/state, prefix reuse, sampling, streaming, and
      observability mechanisms already implemented in source.
- [x] Inventory active CPU, Metal, and CUDA attention, convolution, projection,
      sampling, graph, memory, and transfer optimizations with exact eligibility
      and fallback constraints.
- [x] Build per-family ASR and TTS gap matrices: already used, directly
      reusable, reusable after adapter/state work, architecture-specific, or
      inapplicable.
- [x] Identify semantic blockers unique to audio encoders, cross-attention,
      codec/audio-token generation, vocoders, streaming state, long-form ASR,
      and multi-speaker or conditioning inputs.
- [x] Produce a dependency-ordered rollout plan and correctness, concurrency,
      latency, quality, memory, fallback, and exact-hardware evidence gates for
      CPU, Metal, and CUDA.
- [x] Verify the audit against source wiring, manifests/features, tests,
      benchmarks, and repository status; add a review section with findings and
      clearly separate implemented capability from candidate reuse.

## Review

- Scope covered seven dedicated ASR families plus the LFM2.5 Audio ASR route,
  and five dedicated TTS families plus the LFM2.5 Audio TTS route. Chat,
  speech-to-speech, forced alignment, and diarization paths were excluded.
- Stateful audio families already publish exact physical state through ABI v2;
  most state is invocation-scoped. Qwen3 ASR/TTS have the closest retained
  sequence implementations, Nemotron has retained realtime tensor/ring state,
  and Kokoro is correctly stateless. A blanket paged-KV conversion would be
  wrong for Kokoro and transducer/recurrent ASR families.
- No audio family currently has certified production multi-row model execution.
  Loaded contracts remain width one and execution-group-exclusive. Qwen3 audio
  can yield at sequence boundaries but still uses full prefill and scalar
  decode; direct TTS and most ASR paths remain atomic invocations.
- The reusable foundation is already present: exact stage and batch contracts,
  fair scheduling, incremental-prefill commit semantics, retained/invocation
  paged/tensor/ring/static state, transactional rollback, ragged paged
  prefill/decode, streaming delivery, resource admission, telemetry, and
  evidence runners.
- Recommended order is common audio stage contracts and evidence first; Qwen3
  ASR/TTS pilots; Whisper/VibeVoice/Granite/Voxtral decoder staging; LFM,
  VibeVoice, Voxtral, and Fish multi-clock TTS work; Nemotron/Parakeet retained
  transducer batching; and Kokoro static/ragged request batching.
- CPU has native paged GQA and row/head parallelism; Metal has native paged
  attention plus family-specific convolution kernels; CUDA has native/FA2
  paged attention, partitioned decode, graph replay, workspace pooling, and
  lazy arena growth. Eligibility and exact-device evidence remain mandatory;
  FP8 KV and dormant/test-only helpers were not counted as active capability.
- Verification passed 34 loaded-adapter contract tests, 26 lifecycle/state
  publication tests, 41 scheduler tests, and 8 CPU paged-KV tests (109 total).
  `git diff --check` is recorded separately after this review update. No
  runtime or model code was changed, and no Metal/CUDA performance result is
  claimed without actual-device evidence.

  validator smoke tests plus checked-in manifest expansion tests pass.

### Scope and evidence

- Audited source at `60526aad` without changing product/runtime code. The text
  chat scope is Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8, Gemma3, and LFM2.5; LFM2.5 Audio is a
  separate audio-chat path.
- Verified adapter routing, scheduler chunk continuation, the Qwen3 true ragged
  batch path, and CPU paged GQA with five focused unit tests. All passed.
- CPU behavior has executable coverage on this host. Metal and CUDA conclusions
  are source/build/test-inventory findings, not new real-device performance
  certification. The committed Qwen3.8 and CUDA benchmark files are workload
  manifests; there is no checked-in exact-SHA result bundle proving chat
  throughput, TTFT, TPOT, or memory behavior on all three backends.

### Capability truth

| Family | Scheduler-resumable prefill | Continuous membership | True tensor-batched decode | Safe prefix reuse |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3 | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Qwen3.5 | No; internal memory chunks only | No | No | No |
| Qwen3.8 | Yes, opt-in | Yes | No; scalar row loop | No |
| Gemma3 | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| LFM2.5 | No | No | No; full generation is one invocation | No |

- Qwen3.8's continuous path improves admission, cancellation, fairness, and
  state lifecycle, but `decode_step_batch` loops scalar rows. Qwen3 and Gemma3
  already have the stronger implementation: batched projections/MLP plus one
  ragged paged-attention call per layer.
- Qwen3.8 is the only family wired to scheduler-level chunked prefill. Its own
  and Qwen3.5's internal 256-token chunk loops bound transient memory, but only
  the Qwen3.8 begin/continue protocol yields between chunks.
- The normal continuous-serving route caps every row to one token. Qwen3.8 MTP
  draft/verify requires a quantum greater than one, so the current route never
  reaches speculative execution. Multi-row participation also permanently
  disables MTP for that state. This is a P0 capability/integration defect, not
  an optimization to copy.
- The engine retains one physical batch per step and prioritizes decode over
  prefill. It does not currently form a mixed-phase batch. Incremental prefill
  progress under perpetual decode load needs an explicit fairness test/policy.

### Reusable optimization inventory

- Model-neutral engine: weighted-fair/deadline scheduling, token/workspace
  budgets, exact execution lanes, ragged/padded shape policies, one-token
  continuous membership boundaries, transactional batch rollback, managed KV
  capacity admission, conservative whole-request preemption/recompute, exact
  prepared-request/model leases, and bounded queues/retained states.
- Cache/state: page-major physical KV, exact slot/page mutation, paged
  prefill/decode, atomic multi-domain state groups, logical checkpoints,
  copy-on-write committed-prefix cache with salted namespaces, LRU eviction,
  and capacity/workspace telemetry. Qwen3/Gemma can use safe prefix reuse;
  hybrid Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 and LFM2 must snapshot every state domain first.
- CPU: direct F32/F16/BF16 page-walking online-softmax attention, ragged
  GQA/MQA/MHA, sliding-window/softcap semantics, and Rayon parallelism across
  row-head work. Dense/quantized GEMM remains Candle/QMatMul, optionally backed
  by Accelerate; the repository has no active CPU custom fused-transformer
  kernel provider.
- Metal: native F32/F16 paged prefill/decode with split-KV long-context paths;
  real SiLU-multiply, RMS/QK-RMS, RoPE, LFM ShortConv/ring, hybrid causal-conv,
  and selected tiled DeltaNet kernels. Scalar request dispatch is deliberately
  serialized, automatic tensor width is one, and BF16/custom-ineligible shapes
  fall back portably.
- CUDA: native F32/F16/BF16 paged prefill/decode, split-KV, optional constrained
  paged FlashAttention2, attention-plan/metadata caching, bounded scratch, and
  native paged-decode graph capture/replay. Generic device greedy/bounded
  top-k/top-p sampling avoids full-vocabulary host reads when eligible. Custom
  Qwen hybrid conv/DeltaNet/epilogue candidates exist; several Qwen3.8-specific
  candidates are opt-in and unvalidated.
- Shared model fast paths: Qwen3 projection grouping (including compatible
  quantized QMatMul groups), compact GQA, optional CUDA FlashAttention/Metal
  SDPA for stateless paths, fused-operation eligibility/fallback routing, and
  generic transactional speculative verification.
- Do not count as active chat wins: the legacy generic buffer pool (ASR-only),
  metadata-only v2 scratch pool, row-interleaved weight layout, runtime
  quantized/FP8 KV, Metal SIMD helper names that call ordinary Candle ops,
  unimplemented 3x1 DeltaNet block fusion, or whole-model CUDA graphs. Current
  CUDA graphs capture only an eligible native paged-attention launch. Several
  generic CUDA "fused" wrappers are Candle compositions, not one-launch CUDA
  kernels.

### Dependency-ordered implementation plan

1. Establish truthful telemetry and baselines. Separate scheduled/envelope
   width from actual tensor-forward width; expose forward count, batch width,
   TTFT, TPOT, aggregate goodput, fairness, queue delay, page/workspace high
   water, fallback reasons, and MTP proposal/acceptance counters. Run exact-SHA
   c1/c2/c4/c8 (and CUDA c16) short/long/mixed-prompt workloads.
2. Make resumable prefill a family-neutral begin/continue/finalize contract.
   Port Gemma3 first, then Qwen3; both already have position-aware paged state.
   Compute first-token logits only on the final span and preserve rollback,
   cancellation, prefix boundaries, and exact token progress.
3. Repair Qwen3.8 before using it as the batching template: reconcile solo MTP
   quanta with one-token membership boundaries, then replace the scalar row loop
   with batched projections, paged attention, recurrent/conv state collation,
   and per-row scatter/commit. Keep scalar execution as the oracle/fallback.
4. Promote Qwen3.5's internal text chunks to scheduler-visible spans. Its
   prepared artifact must retain image-embedding cursor and 3-D position state;
   checkpoint paged, recurrent, and convolution domains atomically. Then add a
   true hybrid tensor-batched decode path.
5. Migrate LFM2.5 from invocation-owned batch-one state to retained,
   checkpointable paged-KV plus ShortConv-ring state. Expose incremental
   prefill/decode only after ring rollback is exact; then batch attention and
   ring-state updates and join the continuous adapter.
6. Generalize proven kernels by compatibility, not family name. Reuse Qwen3
   projection packing and eligible Metal RMS/QK-RMS/RoPE/SiLU paths, preserving
   Gemma's weight-plus-one normalization, GELU, alternating sliding windows and
   attention/logit softcaps. Profile before adding new CUDA or CPU kernels.
7. Improve backend overhead after model batching works: cache Metal metadata and
   partial buffers; consider larger CUDA graph scopes only with stable ownership
   and fence contracts; add bounded CPU/Metal stochastic sampling if profiling
   shows vocabulary readback is material.
8. Enable prefix caching for Qwen3/Gemma only with an explicit namespace salt
   and measured benefit. Do not enable it for hybrid families until atomic
   prefix snapshots cover attention, recurrent, convolution, MTP/ring, position,
   and multimodal cursor state.

### Acceptance gates

- Differential logits/tokens: scalar versus batched and monolithic versus every
  legal chunk boundary; mixed lengths, GQA/MQA, sliding windows and softcaps.
- Transaction safety: cancel/failure before and after dispatch, partial prefill,
  row join/leave, capacity preemption, recompute, and no cross-request prefix or
  state leakage.
- Architecture coverage: Qwen3.5 image spans/3-D positions, Qwen3.8 MTP
  rollback/acceptance and solo-to-shared transition, LFM ShortConv ring wrap.
- Backend coverage: CPU F32/F16/BF16; Metal F32/F16 plus forced fallback; CUDA
  F16/BF16, native/FA2/split/graph on/off, ineligible fallback, long context and
  memory plateau. FP8 weights must not be conflated with unsupported FP8 KV.
- Promotion requires exact-SHA real-hardware evidence showing improved aggregate
  throughput without unacceptable p95 TTFT/TPOT, starvation, correctness drift,
  memory growth, or cancellation regressions. Capability/default claims remain
  fail-closed until that evidence exists.

# Plan — Production Full-Context CUDA Capacity — 2026-08-19

Status: implementation in progress; CUDA runtime verification remains a manual
deployment gate because this host has no NVIDIA device/toolkit.

Goal: explain why several requests near the advertised 32K Qwen3.8 context can
reach a raw CUDA OOM, compare Izwi's active/retained KV behavior with current
vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp policies, and produce a CUDA-generic implementation
and hardware-validation plan. Distinguish single-sequence context feasibility,
multi-sequence concurrency, reusable prefix retention, and active-sequence
eviction/recompute.

## Research and implementation plan

- [x] Trace context fitting, physical page materialization, per-request page
      reservation, retained session lifetime, prefix retention, admission,
      scheduler backpressure, and raw CUDA allocation escape paths.
- [x] Calculate Qwen3.8 target plus MTP KV bytes per token/page and reconcile
      them with the configured 32K reach, resident model/workspace headroom, and
      the number of simultaneous or retained OpenCode requests.
- [x] Compare current vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp behavior using primary docs
      and source: preallocated pools, block/page allocation, admission,
      preemption, recomputation/swap, prefix-cache eviction, sliding windows,
      and context overflow.
- [x] Determine whether any engine silently evicts tokens from an active
      full-attention sequence, and separate that from evicting reusable prefixes
      or preempting an entire request.
- [x] Produce a severity-ranked, CUDA-capability/resource-derived remediation
      plan with portable CPU/Metal invariants, observability, tests, and exact
      manual CUDA evidence gates.
- [x] Stream target and MTP prompt prefill without retaining prompt-length
      embeddings, hidden spans, or MTP activations.
- [x] Reserve and validate prompt-plus-output KV demand before CUDA execution;
      publish truthful capacity diagnostics.
- [x] Add whole-request pressure recovery/recomputation and typed terminal
      capacity failures without truncating active full-attention history.
- [x] Prove terminal cleanup and expose allocation/workspace high-water state.
- [x] Run portable verification, document the manual CUDA matrix, and commit
      each independently reviewable change.

## Review

### Findings

- Qwen3.8 has 16 full-attention target layers plus one full-attention MTP layer.
  At dense F16 with four KV heads and 256-wide K and V, its paged state is
  69,632 bytes/token. A 32,281-token sequence therefore consumes approximately
  2,247,790,592 bytes (2.09 GiB) of paged state, plus roughly 50 MiB of fixed
  hybrid recurrent/convolution state per active sequence. The fitted page pool
  is shared capacity, not 32K capacity for every configured request row.
- The CUDA context fitter prices resident paged and fixed tensor state, but not
  Qwen3.8's actual long-prefill activation peak. Target prefill uses 256-token
  compute chunks yet retains all hidden chunks and concatenates them. MTP then
  embeds the entire prompt and executes one unchunked prompt-length head pass.
  This defeats the intended transient-memory bound and can escape as a raw
  `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` despite valid managed-page admission.
- Qwen3.8 prefix publication is disabled for all of its hybrid retained-state
  domains. Completed request pages should be released; repeated OpenCode turns
  do not currently reuse a safe hybrid target+recurrent+convolution+MTP prefix.
  Sequential growth therefore indicates transient allocation retention,
  incomplete cleanup/fencing, or allocator fragmentation and needs evidence;
  it must not be assumed to be ordinary prefix-cache retention.
- Managed page exhaustion already defers a waiter rather than allocating beyond
  the pool. The current preemption flag only changes priority scheduling; it
  does not proactively choose a KV owner, atomically release all hybrid state,
  and enqueue that exact request for recomputation. Executor-triggered
  recompute machinery exists, but no complete page-pressure preemption policy
  connects the allocator to it.
- vLLM and SGLang do not silently delete arbitrary tokens from a live
  full-attention sequence. They first reclaim unreferenced reusable prefixes;
  under active pressure they preempt/retract whole requests, release their KV,
  and later recompute/resume. Sliding-window layers discard only model-defined
  history. llama.cpp normally allocates one total KV budget across slots; its
  optional context-shift mode explicitly discards old tokens and changes model
  semantics, so it is not equivalent to serving the advertised full context.

### Implementation review

- `f84c0e04` streams target and MTP prompt bootstrap in bounded chunks and
  retains only the final target row needed by the sampled anchor.
- `4e5ea565` adds logical full-request page claims, pre-dispatch single-request
  capacity rejection, and model/arena capacity diagnostics.
- `60b1bb08` classifies allocator OOM as typed capacity pressure and exposes
  workspace budget/current/high-water measurements.
- `cd3414eb` completes conservative priority preemption: only unpublished,
  lower-priority, recompute-safe owners can be atomically cleaned and replayed;
  post-output requests remain protected.
- `3a38bc13` publishes chunked-prefill execution truth and a generic CUDA
  long-context capacity/cleanup evidence matrix.
- Verification passed: `izwi-core` 1,931 passed / 7 ignored; `izwi-server` 378
  passed; Metal workspace tests 5/5 and Metal core check passed; all three
  Qwen3.8 CUDA/MTP evidence-runner smoke tests passed. CUDA numerical,
  allocator, VRAM, and soak evidence remains the documented manual gate.

### Recommended implementation plan

1. Make the published capacity contract two-dimensional. Fit and expose total
   KV-pool tokens, maximum single-request prompt+output tokens, maximum
   concurrency at that length, per-sequence fixed hybrid bytes, reserved
   transient/workspace bytes, and actual prefill chunk size. Reserve the full
   requested prompt+maximum-output page demand before admission, as current
   vLLM does, instead of admitting only the first chunk.
2. Stream Qwen3.8 MTP bootstrap with target prefill. For each target hidden
   chunk, feed all rows whose shifted next-token embedding is already known to
   a same-sized MTP append; retain only the final target row. Once final target
   logits produce the anchor, append the single last MTP pair. Never construct
   full-prompt embeddings, a concatenated full hidden span, or a prompt-length
   MTP activation graph.
3. Derive target and MTP chunk sizes from live transient headroom and a
   model-shaped peak estimator. Budget weights, resident KV/tensor pools,
   CUDA-graph buffers, reusable attention workspaces, sampling/logits, and
   allocator safety reserve together. Preallocate/reuse bounded scratch where
   possible and reject load if the model-authored minimum cannot leave one
   valid execution workspace.
4. Add a pressure hierarchy: evict only unreferenced prefix-cache pages; defer
   new prefills; then optionally preempt the lowest-cost/priority whole request,
   atomically release target KV, MTP KV, recurrent, convolution, and staged
   state, and requeue it for recomputation. If one request cannot fit by itself,
   fail it with a typed capacity error before CUDA dispatch. Never surface a raw
   driver OOM or silently truncate full-attention history.
5. Make terminal cleanup and CUDA fences observable. After success, error,
   cancellation, client disconnect, and preemption, prove registered sessions,
   allocated pages, tensor sequences, pending writes, workspace high-water,
   and live device bytes return to a stable plateau. Poison/recreate the worker
   only for an unrecoverable CUDA generation, not routine capacity pressure.
6. Add hybrid prefix reuse only after an atomic checkpoint can cover target
   full-attention pages, recurrent and convolution tensors, and MTP pages at the
   same token cursor. Use an evictable, bounded LRU/radix index; a session label
   is soft preference, not a permanent VRAM pin.
7. Treat FP8/other quantized KV as a later capacity multiplier, not the primary
   fix. It could roughly halve the 2.09-GiB 32K paged state, but promotion still
   requires calibrated per-layer K/V scales and fused paged prefill/decode
   kernels with quality and latency evidence.
8. Verification: portable arithmetic/property tests for heterogeneous target
   and MTP groups; simulated full-ISL admission/preemption/cleanup tests; CUDA
   fault-injection proving typed rollback; then exact-SHA hardware matrices at
   8K/16K/24K/32K, prompt+output boundary, MTP on/off, sequential 20-request
   soak, concurrency 1/2/4, cancellation, and forced preemption. Require no raw
   OOM, bounded workspace peak, stable post-request VRAM, exact output/context
   semantics, and truthful concurrency telemetry across representative CUDA
   capabilities. Preserve fixed CPU/Metal allocation and backpressure semantics.

# Plan — Qwen3.8 MTP, Speculative Decode, and Quantized KV — 2026-08-19

Status: implementation in progress; CUDA runtime evidence remains a deployment
gate because this host has no NVIDIA device/toolkit.

Goal: determine why default-on Qwen3.8 MTP is not improving measured CUDA
throughput, establish whether its deployed KV cache is actually quantized, and
implement the best checkpoint-compatible speculative-decoding design without
GPU-name assumptions. Preserve correct CPU/Metal fallbacks and require honest
runtime diagnostics when CUDA hardware evidence is unavailable locally.

## Investigation and implementation plan

- [x] Trace policy resolution, checkpoint-head loading, proposal generation,
      target verification, acceptance/replay, scheduler accounting, and emitted
      diagnostics for the deployed Qwen3.8 path.
- [x] Trace requested, resolved, and physical KV dtypes/providers through state
      planning and accelerator allocation; distinguish advertised eligibility
      from actual quantized storage.
- [x] Compare Qwen3.8's native MTP topology with current upstream research and
      production speculative decoding implementations using primary sources.
- [x] Convert findings into concrete correctness, throughput, memory, telemetry,
      fallback, and hardware-evidence acceptance criteria.
- [x] Make the default native policy MTP-1, retain explicit depths 1-3, and
      expose scalar-versus-speculative execution plus acceptance/replay evidence
      so an enabled but inactive/unprofitable path cannot look successful.
- [x] Replace stochastic one-hot drafting with proposal sampling from the MTP
      distribution and standard lossless p/q rejection sampling. Keep target
      and draft RNG streams independent and preserve greedy behavior.
- [x] Report the resolved KV cache truth explicitly: Qwen3.8 currently uses
      dense F16 CUDA/Metal or F32 CPU (optional BF16 CUDA candidate), not FP8.
      Keep FP8 unavailable until calibrated K/V scales and fused paged-attention
      read/write kernels have correctness and performance evidence.
- [x] Implement each independent repair/optimization as a logical commit with
      focused tests before moving to the next slice.
- [x] Run complete portable/Metal-enabled core and server verification, record
      unavailable CUDA runtime gates, and provide exact deployment validation.

## Review

- `449be0cf` changes the default from MTP-3 to the production-conservative
  MTP-1, adds a scalar-target counter, and reports dense/non-quantized KV truth.
- `7e2f5211` gives stochastic MTP proposals their own RNG stream, retains their
  transformed `q` distributions, and verifies with lossless p/q rejection
  sampling instead of pretending every sampled proposal is one-hot.
- `01f81d64` keeps the common temperature-zero, penalty-free target verification
  on device and transfers only selected token scalars instead of full vocabulary
  rows. Penalty/stochastic paths retain the distribution transfer they require.
- `36f65e5f` publishes observed scalar/speculative mode, acceptance, bonus, and
  replay ratios; it also updates generic CUDA evidence guidance and explicitly
  documents why FP8 KV is not selectable yet.
- Verification passed: `izwi-core` 1,924 passed / 7 ignored; `izwi-server` 378
  passed; Qwen3.8 portable CUDA evidence-runner and paired MTP certifier smoke
  tests passed; focused sampler/policy/telemetry tests and package checks passed.
- This host cannot earn CUDA runtime/performance evidence. Redeployment must
  compare MTP-disabled and depth-1 runs on the exact device/SHA, confirm
  speculative rounds are nonzero for concurrency-one requests, and inspect
  acceptance/replay before promoting any deeper depth.

## Findings that define the implementation

- The bundled one-layer Qwen3.8 MTP head is loaded by default, but the old
  default requested three draft tokens. The scheduler reduces that quantum to
  one whenever another decode is active, work is waiting, or a request is
  overdue, so MTP can be enabled yet execute only scalar target steps.
- The old stochastic path generated greedy proposals and verified them against
  a one-hot draft distribution. It was distribution-correct but needlessly
  lowered acceptance for nonzero temperature; standard speculative decoding
  retains the proposal distribution and accepts with `min(1, p(d)/q(d))`.
- Every rejected hybrid target block must currently replay its accepted prefix
  to reconstruct recurrent tensor state. A shallow default reduces that cost;
  removing it requires a separate per-token recurrent-state checkpoint design,
  not an unsafe KV-only cursor adjustment.
- The checkpoint's FP8 weight format does not imply an FP8 KV cache. The current
  physical cache is dense F16 on CUDA/Metal and F32 on CPU, with an opt-in BF16
  CUDA candidate. The lower accelerator FP8 selector intentionally resolves to
  dense because its K/V scale contract is incomplete.
- Upstream production guidance favors native MTP with a small starting depth
  (one for Qwen latency-oriented serving), measures acceptance/bonus/replay, and
  avoids speculation at high concurrency where it can reduce aggregate
  throughput. Quantized KV requires calibrated scales and fused backend support;
  dequantizing outside attention can erase its memory/throughput benefit.

# Plan — Implement Qwen3.8 MTP Default-On — 2026-08-17

Status: best-effort implementation complete. Full-model CUDA/Metal/CPU validation is
unavailable on this host; portable and synthetic verification is required.

Goal: implement the complete researched Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 MTP path in logical,
independently verified commits. For this model, a valid bundled MTP head is
loaded and used by default at draft depth 3. Preserve an explicit disable/kill
switch and a bounded depth override. Do not claim hardware performance evidence
that this machine cannot produce.

## Implementation decisions

- Default policy for `Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` is `Enabled { draft_tokens: 3 }`, not an
  evidence-gated scalar `Auto` resolution. `mtp_num_hidden_layers = 1` remains
  the physical recurrent head count, not the draft depth.
- `Disabled` must skip MTP weight/state allocation and preserve the existing
  scalar path. A process-level operator control must be resolved once at load.
- If default-enabled MTP checkpoint validation fails, fail model loading with a
  precise error rather than silently serving a different execution path.
- Correctness comes before a fused optimization: use canonical restore/rerun as
  the rejection oracle, then add bounded accepted-count replay only where it is
  independently testable.
- Full-model runtime/performance evidence is deferred, but implementation is
  not. Completion requires exact synthetic contracts, reference math, state and
  sampling property tests, production-feature compilation, strict linting, and
  fail-closed remote evidence tooling.

# Plan — Qwen3.8 MTP Default-On Research — 2026-08-17

Status: research, analysis, and implementation planning complete. No production
implementation was performed.

Goal: determine how Izwi can load and execute the bundled Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
multi-token-prediction (MTP) head, when it can safely be enabled by default,
and what correctness, quality, memory, and performance evidence must gate that
promotion.

## Research checklist

- [x] Verify the pinned checkpoint's exact MTP configuration, tensor layout,
      intended decoding semantics, and official support/performance guidance.
- [x] Compare current primary-source implementations in Transformers, vLLM,
      and SGLang, including their default policies and recent hybrid-GDN fixes.
- [x] Trace Izwi's Qwen3.8 loader, recurrent/full-attention state, paged KV,
      scheduler/batching, sampler, request contracts, capability publication,
      observability, and benchmark/certification paths.
- [x] Choose an architecture that preserves exact target-model sampling
      semantics and transactional state under rejection, cancellation, and
      mixed prompt/decode work.
- [x] Define capability gates, automatic/default policy, rollback controls,
      telemetry, tests, real-model benchmarks, and staged promotion criteria.
- [x] Add this Review with evidence, open uncertainties, rejected options, and
      an ordered implementation handoff.
- [x] Revise the implementation-completion boundary for a development host that
      cannot load the full checkpoint on CUDA, Metal, or CPU.

## Decision

Do not make MTP an unconditional boolean default. Make the operator default
`Auto` when Qwen3.8 is loaded, while leaving Izwi's product-default model
unchanged. `Auto` must resolve to MTP only for a checkpoint, backend, memory
plan, sampling path, and workload bucket that has passed paired MTP-off/on
certification; otherwise it must retain scalar decoding and expose the reason.

The public policy should have three states:

- `Auto` (default): load and use MTP only when every capability and evidence
  gate passes; otherwise fall back visibly to scalar decoding.
- `Disabled`: do not load the head or allocate its retained state. This is the
  immediate rollback/kill switch.
- `Required { draft_tokens }`: fail model loading or request admission instead
  of silently falling back if the requested MTP path cannot run.

`mtp_num_hidden_layers = 1` is the number of physical checkpoint layers, not
the speculative draft depth. Start implementation and correctness testing at
depth 1. Benchmark depths 1, 2, and 3, with depth 3 as the Qwen3.8-specific
starting candidate from the official vLLM recipe. Let each certified hardware
profile select the fastest passing depth rather than hard-coding 3 globally.

Until exact-hardware evidence exists, `Auto` must resolve off. The first
promotion target should be the existing CUDA/L40S Qwen3.8 evidence profile.
CPU and Metal remain off until independently shown to improve end-to-end
performance. Initial policy resolution should be session-static: switching a
request off and later back on would require keeping the MTP cache synchronized
and would erase much of the intended saving.

## Environment constraint and revised completion boundary

This development machine has no usable GPU and insufficient CPU/Metal memory
to load or run the complete Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 checkpoint. That changes what can
block the implementation handoff, but it does not change the state architecture
or make an unmeasured performance claim safe.

Split delivery into two explicit milestones:

1. **Best-effort implementation on this host.** Complete the loader, MTP math,
   transaction, sampler, executor/scheduler accounting, policy, diagnostics,
   and evidence-runner code. Verify them with exact manifest fixtures,
   small/synthetic tensor references, deterministic state-machine/property
   tests, failure injection, ordinary Rust tests/checks/Clippy, and any
   driverless CUDA compile/link CI available. A full-checkpoint load or local
   throughput result is not required to call this milestone implemented.
2. **Deferred hardware validation and promotion.** Run the delivered exact-SHA
   evidence bundle later on a machine that can load the model. Only that run can
   classify a route as runtime-validated/performance-certified and add a cell
   that makes `Auto` resolve on.

The implementation must preserve three distinct statuses in documentation and
evidence: `implemented_unvalidated`, `runtime_validated`, and
`performance_certified`. Local compilation or synthetic parity may establish
only the first. The hardware runner must fail closed when the expected provider,
model revision, memory telemetry, or paired MTP-off baseline is absent.

For remote/manual testing, `Required { draft_tokens }` provides an explicit way
to exercise the candidate. `Disabled` remains the rollback control. `Auto`
remains the configured default but resolves to scalar on uncertified cells;
best effort is not permission to silently label an untested path faster.

## Checkpoint and upstream findings

### Exact pinned contract

- Izwi pins Hugging Face revision
  `017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`.
- The text model has 64 layers: 48 Gated DeltaNet linear-attention layers and
  16 full-attention layers. Hidden size is 5,120; the MLP width is 17,408; full
  attention has 24 query heads, 4 KV heads, and head dimension 256.
- The checkpoint has one recurrently reused MTP full-attention decoder block,
  not three independent prediction heads. `mtp_use_dedicated_embeddings` is
  false, so it reuses the target embedding table and target LM head.
- The MTP computation is: independently normalize the next-token embedding and
  target final normalized hidden state; concatenate them; apply the BF16
  `10240 -> 5120` `mtp.fc`; run the one dense full-attention/MLP block; apply
  `mtp.norm`; project through the shared LM head. Reuse layer zero for each
  further draft step.
- The shard contains 22 MTP tensors. Important shapes include BF16
  `mtp.fc.weight [5120, 10240]`, FP8 Q `[12288, 5120]`, K/V
  `[1024, 5120]`, O `[5120, 6144]`, and the normal dense gated-MLP projections
  plus FP8 block scales and zero-centered RMSNorm weights.
- The MTP shard is about 455 MiB on disk. From the exact shapes, expected
  residency is roughly 0.47 GiB with Izwi's current CUDA Q8 packing or 0.79 GiB
  when FP8 projections are expanded to F16/BF16, before allocator overhead.
  Its F16/BF16 KV slope is another 4 KiB per committed token (1 GiB at the
  full 262,144-token context). These bytes must enter load and admission plans.
- MTP prefill is one-token shifted: pair each target hidden state with the next
  token embedding. Across prompt chunks, retain one hidden/token boundary so
  the pairs are neither skipped nor duplicated. The final prompt hidden pairs
  with the target-sampled anchor token.
- Official generation stops are both token 248046 (`<|im_end|>`) and token
  248044 (`<|endoftext|>`). Padding also uses 248044, so batch masks must use
  explicit lengths, not token equality. The model vocabulary is padded beyond
  assigned tokenizer IDs; reference parity must settle masking of IDs
  248077..248319.

### What upstream proves—and does not prove

- The Qwen model card says the model was trained with multi-step MTP but does
  not publish a Qwen3.8-specific speedup.
- The current official vLLM Qwen3.8 recipe uses three speculative tokens and
  reports short-prompt acceptance of 84.8% for FP8. It still classifies
  speculative decoding as opt-in, so acceptance is not evidence of universal
  end-to-end speedup.
- vLLM implements the recurrent head as an EAGLE-like proposer. Its defaults
  use standard lossless rejection sampling and a greedy/one-hot draft
  distribution; probabilistic drafting is optional and consumes more memory.
  It also supports draft-depth schedules by batch size.
- SGLang's Qwen recipe uses three autoregressive steps, top-k 1, and four
  verification slots. Its hybrid-model path explicitly needs accepted-count
  replay/rewind of GDN state instead of keeping a full recurrent-state snapshot
  for every draft position.
- Transformers' generic `use_mtp` path currently rejects stateful models and
  does not map Qwen3.8's config/weights; a Qwen support PR was closed without
  merging because GDN rollback was unresolved. It is not a usable Qwen3.8 MTP
  reference runtime today.
- llama.cpp has an independent, opt-in recurrent MTP path after GGUF conversion
  and defaults its maximum draft depth to 3. It does not execute the official
  Hugging Face block-FP8 checkpoint directly and therefore cannot certify
  Izwi's numerical or performance behavior.
- Recent vLLM work fixed mixed speculative/non-speculative GDN gate alignment
  and added accepted-count recurrent-state rewind. The latter fused Blackwell
  kernel requires a value/key-head ratio of 8, whereas Qwen3.8 uses 48/16 = 3;
  Izwi cannot assume that upstream fast path applies.
- A current vLLM performance report shows good Qwen-family MTP acceptance can
  still lose to a strong no-MTP baseline because draft, rejection sampling,
  metadata, and slot-update overhead dominate. This is why Izwi's default must
  be evidence-gated by end-to-end latency/throughput, not acceptance alone.

Primary sources:

- https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
- https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json
- https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/model.safetensors.index.json
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py
- https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/blob/main/models/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.yaml
- https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features/speculative_decoding/mtp/
- https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B
- https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/45638
- https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/speculative.md
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51812
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51674
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/47277

## Izwi gap analysis

- Artifact acquisition already follows the complete safetensor index closure;
  downloader tests explicitly include `mtp.safetensors`. No download-topology
  change is required.
- `qwen38/native.rs` parses and validates the two MTP config fields and indexes
  `mtp.*`, but `Qwen38NativeCheckpoint::open` intentionally validates only the
  text/LM-head slice. The 22 MTP tensors are never required or materialized.
- `Qwen38TextModel` owns only the target embeddings, 64 layers, output norm,
  and LM head. `Qwen38ChatModel` loads only that target model.
- Target prefill returns only last-position logits. Target decode returns one
  logits row and discards the final normalized hidden state needed by MTP.
  Multi-position verification therefore needs a new prepared-forward result.
- `forward_hidden_physical` can already execute a multi-token continuation, but
  it immediately commits the entire paged-KV span. `PhysicalPagedKvCache` has
  whole-span commit only; it has no abort or accepted-prefix commit.
- Qwen3.8 retained state is already modeled as one transaction group containing
  full-attention KV, 48 recurrent GDN states, and 48 convolution histories.
  MTP adds a fourth retained full-attention domain to that same group.
- A Qwen3.8 GDN state is very large (roughly 150 MB per sequence before smaller
  convolution state). Keeping one complete snapshot per candidate is not a
  viable rollback design.
- The managed cache transaction requires the scheduled work-unit end to match
  the committed end. Efficient depth greater than one therefore needs a
  model-neutral accepted-prefix/unused-suffix reconciliation path; changing
  only the model-local KV cursor is insufficient.
- Chat decode currently consumes and emits exactly one token per call, while
  the executor treats decode calls as processed-token counts. A speculative
  result must report target inputs consumed, output tokens generated, physical
  verification width, and target passes separately.
- Qwen3.8 advertises incremental scalar decode but explicitly does not advertise
  continuous inter-request decode batching. MTP is intra-request speculation;
  the first implementation must not falsely promote continuous batching.
- The global scheduler's multi-token decode quanta are off by default and are
  forced back to one under streaming/contention constraints. MTP should use a
  model-authored atomic-span capability, not flip the global default for every
  model.
- Qwen3.8 already has family-specific runtime diagnostics and exact-SHA CUDA
  evidence runners, but current certificates require only that throughput
  values exist. They do not prove paired MTP improvement.

## Proposed architecture

### 1. Capability, policy, and load resolution

- Add a model-neutral `SpeculativeDecodingPolicy { Auto, Disabled, Required }`
  plus a bounded operator draft-depth override. Implement only a Qwen3.8 MTP
  capability initially.
- Resolve policy before allocating model weights. In `Auto`, require the exact
  compatible config/tensor contract, supported backend representation,
  certified hardware/workload profile, and sufficient projected head/cache/
  workspace memory. In `Required`, surface a structured error on any failure.
- Publish requested policy, resolved mode/depth, head contract, backend,
  resident representation, estimated bytes, and fallback reason in admin model
  diagnostics. `Disabled` must skip head materialization entirely.
- Add `qwen38/mtp.rs`. Refactor the target's projection/norm/attention/MLP
  loaders only enough to share exact math. Share embedding and LM-head owners;
  do not duplicate their storage.

### 2. Prepared target and MTP forwards

- Replace the Qwen3.8 logits-only boundary with a prepared span containing all
  final normalized target hidden rows, all logits rows, prepared KV writes,
  hybrid-state transition data, and explicit start/end positions.
- Keep the existing scalar wrapper over this API so `Disabled` behavior remains
  byte-for-byte isolated and easy to compare.
- Implement prompt MTP prefill with one-token-shift alignment and a chunk carry.
  Retain only the boundary hidden needed by the next chunk; do not retain the
  entire prompt on host.
- Implement recurrent drafting by applying the one physical MTP block K times.
  The MTP full-attention KV is retained in the unified cache contract.

### 3. Speculative round and exact sampling

- Introduce `decode_quantum(max_output_tokens)` and a result that separates
  `target_inputs_consumed`, `output_tokens_generated`, `verification_width`,
  `target_passes`, accepted drafts, correction/bonus tokens, and terminal state.
  Existing models can preserve scalar behavior through a one-token adapter.
- Preserve Qwen3.8's current one-token-lag/pending-token convention. Bootstrap
  the first target-sampled anchor, use the pending token plus K MTP drafts as
  the verification span, and never emit beyond scheduler or `max_new_tokens`
  reservations.
- Greedy verification accepts the target-equal prefix exactly. Before MTP can
  be the normal Qwen3.8 default, implement standard lossless speculative
  sampling for stochastic requests: accept candidate `x` with
  `min(1, p(x)/q(x))`; on rejection, sample from normalized `[p-q]+`.
  Initially use greedy MTP drafts, so q is one-hot, matching vLLM's default.
- Refactor the sampler so logits transforms, target probabilities, RNG,
  history penalties, top-k/top-p, and state updates can be applied
  transactionally per candidate. Greedy MTP must be token-identical to scalar;
  stochastic MTP must be distribution-equivalent, not necessarily
  seed-for-seed identical because it consumes random values differently.
- Stop at the first model EOS, configured stop ID, custom stop, or max-token
  boundary. Decode and stream accepted tokens in order only after the state
  transaction commits.

### 4. Atomic accepted-prefix state

- Extend physical paged attention with prepared-span `commit_prefix(n)` and
  `abort()` semantics. Seal and drain all asynchronous writes before rejected
  slots can be overwritten; leave rejected suffix slots logically unreachable.
- Extend the managed transaction/scheduler protocol to reconcile the maximum
  reserved verification span with the actual committed prefix and release the
  unused suffix. Do not falsify `WorkUnit.input.end` or count speculative work
  as committed tokens.
- Add the MTP attention domain to Qwen3.8's existing full-attention/recurrent/
  convolution consistency group. Target and MTP state commit or abort together.
- Use a correctness-first rejection path: restore the transaction base and
  rerun only the canonical committed span (accepted prefix plus correction).
  This avoids candidate-sized recurrent snapshots and provides a scalar oracle.
- Then add an optimized GDN accepted-count replay path. Capture bounded
  per-token transition operands during verification, restore the pre-round
  state, and replay only accepted transitions; do not copy roughly 150 MB of
  recurrent state per draft position. The optimized result must match the
  rerun oracle before it can participate in `Auto`.
- Treat cancellation, backend error, OOM, stop/EOS, and injected commit failure
  as transaction outcomes. No draft token or state change becomes externally
  visible before an authenticated commit.

### 5. Scheduler, admission, and observability

- Let the loaded adapter advertise a preferred and maximum atomic verification
  span. Keep the global decode-quanta default and Qwen3.8 continuous-batch
  capability unchanged.
- Reserve target KV slots, the MTP KV domain, verification workspace, and the
  maximum output block before execution. Report actual committed input/output
  counts afterward so scheduler fairness, TPOT, cache cursors, and streaming
  sequence numbers remain correct.
- Include MTP head residency and load peak in Qwen3.8 lifecycle estimates.
  Include 4 KiB/token MTP KV and bounded rejection/replay workspace in capacity
  planning. Never lazily allocate these during request admission.
- Add counters/histograms for requested/resolved policy, fallback reason,
  rounds, proposals, per-position accepts, mean accepted length, corrections,
  bonus tokens, target passes, reruns/replays, verification/replay time, MTP
  resident/cache/workspace bytes, and context/concurrency buckets.

## Ordered implementation handoff

Each phase should be a separate, verified commit. Phases 1–7 form the
best-effort implementation milestone on this host; `Auto` continues to resolve
off afterward until a separate hardware-promotion commit imports qualifying
evidence.

1. **Contract and policy:** retain MTP config; validate the exact 22-tensor
   manifest and scale shapes; add `Auto/Disabled/Required`; add byte accounting,
   diagnostics, and negative loader tests. Do not execute MTP yet.
2. **Head math:** add `qwen38/mtp.rs`, shared embedding/LM-head ownership, the
   shifted prefill boundary, and depth-1/2/3 recurrent forward. Compare hidden
   states and logits with a pinned vLLM/Transformers-derived fixture.
3. **Prepared state:** expose per-position normalized hidden/logits; add
   prepared/abort/prefix-commit physical KV; extend the Qwen3.8 state contract
   with the MTP domain; prove async-write fencing and all accept lengths.
4. **Sampling:** add a model-neutral transactional speculative sampler. Land
   greedy exactness first, then standard rejection/residual sampling for every
   existing Qwen3.8 temperature/top-k/top-p/penalty combination.
5. **Decode integration:** add `decode_quantum`, Qwen3.8 speculative state,
   exact executor accounting, atomic streaming, managed accepted-prefix
   reconciliation, and scalar-rerun rejection recovery. Keep it explicit-only.
6. **Best-effort performance path:** implement bounded GDN/conv accepted-count
   replay against the canonical-rerun oracle and use existing device primitives
   for greedy draft selection/rejection sampling. Do not invent a bespoke fused
   kernel without compile coverage or profile evidence; leave any such kernel
   as a later hardware-guided optimization. Keep continuous inter-request
   batching out of scope.
7. **Evidence tooling:** extend the existing Qwen3.8 CUDA runner with paired
   off/auto/required and depth 1/2/3 cells; verify dry-run schemas, exact-SHA and
   real-provider rejection, missing-cell rejection, and certificate generation.
   Deliver the command and manifest without claiming that this host ran them.
8. **Deferred promotion (hardware host):** run the evidence bundle, review raw
   correctness/memory/performance samples, and add only passing cells to the
   `Auto` capability table in a separate commit. Preserve the off kill switch
   and document rollback.

## Verification and promotion gates

### Local best-effort completion gates

- Do not attempt to load the full Qwen3.8 checkpoint on this machine and do not
  create swap-heavy CPU/Metal smoke tests. Such a run would be unreliable and
  risks host instability without producing relevant accelerator evidence.
- Use a synthetic safetensor inventory with the exact 22 MTP names, dtypes,
  shapes, and FP8 scale relationships to exercise validation, accounting,
  shared ownership, negative cases, and policy resolution without allocating
  production-sized tensors.
- Use small deterministic weights/tensors to compare MTP math, shifted prefill,
  recurrent draft steps, accepted-prefix state, rollback, and next-step logits
  against an independent reference implementation.
- Exhaustively test the speculative sampler on tiny vocabularies and run
  statistical tests on bounded distributions. Exercise every accept length,
  stop/EOS boundary, cancellation point, and injected failure with small fake
  state/KV arenas.
- Run focused and crate-level Rust tests, production-feature `cargo check`,
  strict Clippy, scoped formatting, shell-runner tests, and diff hygiene. If the
  local host lacks a CUDA toolkit, record CUDA compilation as a separate CI gate
  rather than fabricating a successful local result.
- The evidence runner must support a dry run here and must reject missing GPU,
  provider fallback, dirty/wrong SHA, wrong checkpoint revision, incomplete
  matrices, and absent paired baselines. Its real execution remains deferred.

### Correctness tests

- Exact tensor names/shapes/dtypes/scales; missing/corrupt head; `Auto`
  fallback versus `Required` failure; no duplicate shared weights.
- Reference parity for zero-centered RMSNorm, Q/gate split, partial RoPE,
  gated attention output, MLP, final norm, and logits at draft steps 1..3.
- Prompt-shift parity across chunk boundaries, one-token prompts, resumed
  sessions, maximum positions, and padded-vocabulary handling.
- Forced accept counts 0..K, all-accept, rejection at every position, and
  correction/bonus behavior. After each case, compare target KV length, every
  GDN recurrent/conv state, MTP KV, next logits, and the following scalar token.
- Failure injection at proposal, verification, sampling, replay, KV drain,
  managed commit, cancellation, and OOM. Require no state/page/workspace leak.
- Greedy token equality on synthetic/reference fixtures for penalties, stops,
  both EOS IDs, Unicode streaming, and max-token boundaries.
- Tiny-vocabulary exhaustive rejection-sampling tests plus large-sample
  distribution tests for temperature/top-k/top-p and penalties.
- Scheduler tests for one-slot fallback, partial reservation release, exact
  input/output accounting, fairness, streaming order, and a fail-closed claim
  that Qwen3.8 still lacks continuous inter-request batching.

### Deferred real-model evidence matrix

- Exact model revision and Izwi SHA, clean tree, real provider (no fallback),
  warmup, machine-readable raw samples, and paired prompts/seeds.
- Full-checkpoint greedy token/logprob parity against MTP-off for thinking
  modes, tools, penalties, stops, both EOS IDs, Unicode streaming, session
  resume, and max-token boundaries.
- MTP off versus depths 1, 2, and 3 at input lengths 128, 2K, 8K, and 32K;
  output lengths 128 and 1K; concurrency/queue buckets 1, 2, 4, and 8; both
  greedy and the checkpoint's normal stochastic profile.
- Measure TTFT, median/p95 TPOT, end-to-end latency, output tokens/s, request
  throughput, acceptance by position, mean accepted tokens/target pass,
  target passes, rerun/replay cost, and peak/resident memory.

### Deferred default-on promotion criteria

- Zero correctness, state-parity, lifecycle, provider-fallback, or leak failures.
- For every cell where `Auto` resolves on, at least 10% median TPOT improvement
  over the same-SHA MTP-off baseline, no more than 5% p95 TPOT or TTFT
  regression, and no throughput regression in the profile's declared workload.
  These are proposed promotion thresholds and may be tightened before rollout.
- Observed memory must fit the admission estimate and safety reserve; no
  reduction of capacity may be hidden from model diagnostics.
- Cells that do not pass remain `Auto -> Disabled(reason)` even if acceptance is
  high. Exact hardware evidence, not a model name or upstream benchmark, is the
  authority for promotion.
- Failure to run this matrix on the current machine does not block the
  best-effort implementation milestone. It does block runtime/performance
  certification and any commit that makes an `Auto` cell resolve on.

## Rejected shortcuts

- Loading `mtp.safetensors` and flipping a flag: there is no execution or state
  transaction underneath it.
- Treating one physical MTP layer as draft depth one only, or as three separate
  heads: the layer is recurrently reusable and depth is an independent policy.
- Equality-based acceptance for sampled generation: it changes the target
  distribution.
- Copying the full GDN state for every draft position: the per-sequence state is
  too large; replay/rewind or canonical rerun is required.
- Keeping MTP KV in an opaque model-local cache: it would escape Izwi's unified
  state ownership, memory accounting, cleanup, and transaction guarantees.
- Globally enabling scheduler decode quanta or claiming continuous batching:
  MTP is an intra-request capability and Qwen3.8 continuous batching is still
  unsupported.
- Promoting depth 3 or CUDA/Metal/CPU by upstream reputation alone: upstream
  keeps MTP opt-in and documents workload-sensitive behavior.

## Open uncertainties

- The fastest Izwi depth and the actual speedup on L40S are unknown until the
  planned paired runner is executed on another machine; this host intentionally
  provides no full-model or qualifying GPU evidence.
- Q8-repacked CUDA MTP weights can have different acceptance from upstream FP8
  kernels. Acceptance and end-to-end performance must be measured on Izwi's
  actual resident representation.
- The best accepted-count replay kernel for Qwen3.8's GDN head ratio is not
  supplied by the recent ratio-8-only upstream CUDA kernel.
- CPU and Metal may not amortize the extra head/LM projections; neither should
  be promoted without separate evidence.
- Reference parity must decide whether padded, tokenizer-unassigned vocabulary
  IDs are masked by the official serving path.

## Review

- Research used the pinned Qwen checkpoint, current official vLLM/SGLang
  recipes and source, recent upstream fixes, and current-branch runtime source.
- Current-branch proof: Izwi already downloads the MTP shard; the Qwen3.8
  loader intentionally excludes it; target forward eagerly commits whole spans;
  retained hybrid state has three transactional domains; scalar decode emits
  one token; and Qwen3.8 continuous batching is fail-closed.
- The resulting recommendation is `Auto` by default for Qwen3.8, with no cell
  resolving on until its exact capability/evidence gates pass. The implementation
  starts at depth 1 for correctness and promotes the fastest certified depth,
  evaluating the official depth-3 candidate.
- The environment constraint now explicitly permits implementation completion
  from portable/synthetic verification plus evidence-runner delivery. Real-model
  validation and the `Auto` promotion are a separate exact-SHA hardware handoff,
  not a blocker that leaves the implementation indefinitely unfinished.
- No runtime code, model behavior, catalog default, or production setting was
  changed. This document is the only task artifact.

# Plan — Production Batching, Continuous Batching, and GQA Audit — 2026-08-16

Status: research and analysis complete; no production implementation performed.

Goal: determine whether batching, batch sizing, continuous batching, and
grouped-query attention are correct and production-ready on CPU, Metal, and
CUDA; recommend backend-appropriate defaults and a prioritized remediation
plan.

## Checklist

- [x] Map every capacity axis from server admission through scheduler,
      executor, adapter, tensor kernels, state, and KV allocation.
- [x] Audit CPU and Metal defaults and prove their physical tensor batch width
      defaults to one without disabling safe request/session scheduling.
- [x] Audit CUDA defaults and compare them with current official vLLM and
      SGLang policies, distinguishing sequence count from token budget.
- [x] Verify continuous batching semantics for admission, prefill/decode
      mixing, fairness, cancellation, commit/rollback, cache reuse, and
      heterogeneous sequence lengths.
- [x] Audit GQA configuration, geometry validation, projection layout, RoPE,
      KV storage, dense/paged/flash attention, and batched decode across all
      relevant model families and backends.
- [x] Inventory correctness, stress, conformance, memory-slope, and throughput
      evidence; run targeted read-only diagnostics/tests available on this host.
- [x] Deliver severity-ranked findings, explicit uncertainty, recommended
      defaults, and an ordered implementation/validation plan.

## Review

- The current global `max_batch_size = 8` is overloaded across tensor width,
  scheduled rows, admission, retained sessions, staged KV transactions, and
  queue capacity. A direct change to one would damage useful concurrency; the
  axes must be split first.
- Safe interim physical defaults are CPU `1`, Metal `1`, CUDA `8` only for a
  continuous-capable tensor path, and `1` for scalar paths. Disable the current
  implicit CUDA `8 -> 16/32` promotion until post-load, model-aware memory
  sizing and explicit-vs-auto provenance exist.
- Continuous Qwen3/Gemma decode is a real changing-membership tensor batch, but
  all prefills are full and indivisible, default decode-first FCFS can starve
  new prefills, serial physical work delays commit, and batch state handling is
  not demonstrably failure-atomic. Qwen3/Gemma incremental paths also ignore
  request sampling controls and use greedy selection.
- GQA head mapping and compact managed/paged KV addressing are correct for
  valid geometry on CPU, Metal, and CUDA. Remaining gaps are early family
  validation, materialized-KV fallback paths, batch-one family coverage, and
  production certification. The CUDA parity test uses unsupported
  `page_tokens = 2`, so it cannot certify the native kernel.
- Verification passed: CPU/default continuous `10/10`, GQA `6/6`, paged decode
  `13/13`, capability conformance `7/7`, focused request-parallelism/tensor-cap
  tests, Metal-feature GQA `10/10`, and Metal-feature continuous `10/10`.
  Hardware-gated tests may skip when a device is unavailable. This host has no
  CUDA toolchain/device, so no CUDA runtime or performance claim is made.
- The implementation plan is configuration-axis split and provenance first;
  then hard reservation-aware token admission, fair/chunked scheduling,
  failure-atomic row handling and correct per-row sampling; then GQA fallback
  cleanup and family expansion; finally real-model CPU/Metal/CUDA certification
  gates before wider defaults are promoted.

### Revised implementation handoff — no local GPU

The absence of usable GPU hardware changes sequencing and completion semantics,
not the target design. GPU-feature compilation, source/ABI checks, and CPU
oracles are supporting evidence only; they must not be reported as Metal or
CUDA runtime certification.

1. **Implement hardware-independent contracts first.**
   - Split physical width, scheduled rows, active sequences, batched tokens,
     retained/staged state, request parallelism, admission, and queue capacity.
   - Preserve `Auto` versus explicit values and reject invalid zero/overflowing
     configurations.
   - Resolve CPU and Metal physical defaults to `1`, CUDA continuous-capable
     width to the conservative candidate `8`, and scalar paths to `1`.
   - Keep CUDA `16/32` promotion and larger token tiers disabled.
2. **Prove portable correctness locally.**
   - Add CPU oracle/property tests for scheduler fairness, hard token admission,
     failure-atomic state rollback, row-local cancellation, heterogeneous
     sampling, GQA geometry, and compact KV memory growth.
   - Run normal and feature-gated checks that the host can execute, but record
     every hardware-gated skip and unavailable CUDA build/runtime gate.
3. **Make GPU evidence fail closed.**
   - Repair CUDA tests to use supported page sizes and require an actual
     provider instead of silently passing when hardware is absent.
   - Add equivalent forced-provider Metal/CUDA matrices and diagnostics for the
     resolved capacity axes, provider, fallback reason, batch width/fill, token
     budget, KV usage, and memory high-water.
   - Leave GPU-specific candidates behind explicit rollback switches until
     manual evidence exists.
4. **Deliver a self-contained manual verification bundle with the code.**
   - Pin the exact commit and capture GPU, driver/runtime, compute capability,
     memory, model/checkpoint, dtype, context, and all resolved settings.
   - Provide one-command correctness, concurrency, cancellation/failure,
     partition-boundary, memory-slope, latency/throughput, and soak runs.
   - Emit raw results plus a machine-readable certificate that cannot pass if a
     required device/provider/test was skipped.
5. **Run deferred hardware certification manually.**
   - Metal: representative Apple hardware, Qwen3/Gemma real-model widths
     `1/2`, ragged GQA, membership churn, long prefill plus active decode, and
     unified-memory high-water/soak evidence. Default remains `1`; width `2`
     is only an opt-in certified optimization.
   - CUDA: representative GPU/model profiles at widths `1/8`, followed by
     candidate `16/32`; page sizes `16/32/64`; realistic GQA ratios/head dims;
     contexts around the partition boundary; forced native/partitioned/Flash
     providers; cancellations, failures, KV exhaustion, and long soaks.
6. **Promote only from signed evidence.**
   - The implementation may be reported locally as complete but
     `GPU-unverified`; production readiness remains `pending-manual-hardware`.
   - CUDA `8` becomes production-certified only after the baseline matrix
     passes. Width `16/32`, token budget `2K+`, and chunk tiers remain disabled
     until their exact model/GPU profile passes correctness, memory, throughput,
     and tail-latency gates.
   - A failed or missing hardware run retains CPU/Metal width `1`, CUDA width
     `8` as an unpromoted candidate, and the scalar/eager rollback path.

Status: complete; updated 2026-08-16 for a GPU-less implementation host.
Research and planning only; no production implementation was performed for
this task.

Goal: explain the current single-user 18 tok/s CUDA result, establish a
defensible L40S performance target for Qwen3.8 27B, and produce an ordered,
Qwen3.8-only implementation plan whose commits remain independently measurable
and reversible.

Constraint: this workstation has no CUDA GPU. Implementation-time verification
must therefore be portable and build-oriented; runtime correctness, memory,
provider selection, and performance certification will be executed manually on
the L40S after the implementation task completes.

- [x] Trace current prefill and decode execution from request scheduling through
      Qwen3.8 projections, hybrid attention/DeltaNet kernels, state, and output.
- [x] Inventory existing CUDA kernels, Q8_0 paths, graph capture, paged KV,
      workspace reuse, profiling counters, and family-specific feature gates.
