      with L40S bandwidth, compute, and optimized implementation evidence.
- [x] Separate measured facts, source-proven constraints, inferred bottlenecks,
      and hypotheses that require Nsight/CUDA evidence.
- [x] Define a reproducible L40S benchmark/evidence matrix for batch-one decode,
      prompt prefill, time-to-first-token, concurrency, VRAM, and correctness.
- [x] Prioritize optimization slices by expected impact, risk, dependencies,
      fallback behavior, and Qwen3.8-family isolation.
- [x] Specify logical commits, acceptance gates, rollback switches, and the
      point at which native FP8 may replace the current Q8_0 fallback.
- [x] Record findings and deliver the plan without changing production code.
- [x] Split local no-GPU verification from deferred manual L40S certification,
      including candidate defaults, evidence artifacts, and promotion commits.

## No-GPU implementation and promotion contract

Evidence has five distinct states and must never be collapsed into one claim:

1. `source_reviewed`: dimensions, launch geometry, ownership, synchronization,
   bounds, and fallbacks have been reviewed against the pinned checkpoint.
2. `portable_verified`: CPU/reference math, serialization, accounting,
   transactional state, cancellation, and fallback tests pass locally.
3. `cuda_compiled`: CUDA-feature code and kernels compile in a toolkit/CI
   environment. This does not imply a driver, device, or successful launch.
4. `cuda_runtime_validated`: the pinned artifact loads and completes the golden
   prompt/decode/context matrix on the real L40S with the intended providers.
5. `cuda_performance_certified`: repeated warmed L40S evidence meets the stated
   p50/p95 throughput, TTFT, memory, graph, and correctness gates.

The implementation task may complete through states 1-3 only. Every new CUDA
kernel/provider must be Qwen3.8-only, have an explicit `off` kill switch, retain
the current Q8_0/eager fallback, and remain a non-default candidate until states
4-5 are supplied. Low-risk representation-independent refactors may ship only
when the same production path is fully covered by portable tests; no unexecuted
CUDA path may be described as validated or faster.

The first implementation commit must add a versioned evidence manifest and a
single manual L40S runner. It records the Git SHA, checkpoint revision, driver,
CUDA/runtime versions, clocks, power/thermal state, provider/fallback counters,
peak VRAM, golden outputs, and raw benchmark samples. The final implementation
commit must generate a handoff report listing every feature as untested, failed,
or ready for promotion; it must not synthesize performance results.

After manual execution, evidence is imported without hand-editing and reviewed
in separate promotion commits, for example
`promote(qwen38): enable packed projections from L40S evidence`. A candidate is
promoted to `auto` only when its exact SHA/configuration passes runtime and
performance gates. Failed candidates remain off and preserve their diagnostic
reason; later repair commits do not rewrite or hide the failed evidence.

## Review

- The observed 18 output tok/s is credible for the current Q8_0/BF16 path. A
  projection-only traffic estimate of about 28.4 GB/token against the L40S's
  864 GB/s gives a roughly 30.4 tok/s no-MTP ceiling; the observation consumes
  about 59% of peak bandwidth before recurrent, KV, launch, and allocation work.
- The leading verified costs are 497 projections/token (400 Q8 and 97 dense),
  at least 800 Q8 activation-quantize/MMVQ launches, a latency-poor 48-layer
  DeltaNet path, repeated RoPE construction, CUDA BF16/F16 attention casts,
  synchronous KV completion sealing, and per-quantum convolution-state stacking.
- Short-context single-user targets are 20–24 tok/s initially, 24–26 tok/s after
  deeper fusion, and 25–28 tok/s as a stretch. Ordinary autoregressive results
  above roughly 30–32 tok/s need scrutiny. Checkpoint-native MTP is the separate
  route to an experimental 30–45 tok/s range.
- Paged KV is already hybrid and growable. It is secondary for short contexts,
  but becomes important at long contexts; current contiguous growth and tensor
  authorization can prevent the advertised 262,144-token logical limit from
  fitting on a 48 GB L40S.
- The implementation sequence is: evidence/telemetry; Qwen3.8 projection packing;
  dedicated convolution and DeltaNet decode kernels; BF16 KV and shared RoPE;
  elementwise/state/synchronization cleanup; Q8 GEMV/prefill tuning; stable-buffer
  full-token CUDA graphs; evidence-gated native FP8; MTP; then continuous batching.
- Every optimization remains Qwen3.8-family-gated, retains a portable/current-path
  fallback, and requires deterministic logits/tokens, transactional state/KV,
  peak-memory, long-context, and L40S performance evidence before promotion.
- Because the implementation machine has no GPU, the 20-28 tok/s and MTP
  30-45 tok/s ranges remain planning hypotheses rather than in-task acceptance
  results. Local completion proves only source, portable behavior, and whatever
  CUDA compilation CI/tooling makes available; a manual L40S pass supplies the
  runtime and performance evidence afterward.
- The logical commit order is unchanged, but each CUDA optimization commit now
  lands as a disabled candidate plus fallback and evidence hooks. A final
  handoff commit packages the exact commands and expected artifact schema;
  evidence-backed `promote(qwen38)` commits occur only after the manual run.

# Previous Plan Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 Chat Support — 2026-08-14

Status: initial text-chat implementation complete in four logical commits.
Portable and compile-time verification is complete locally; real 27B CPU,
large-memory Metal, and CUDA runtime evidence remains pending on capable hosts.

Goal: add the official `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8` checkpoint as a usable,
single-device text-chat model on CPU, Metal, and CUDA, while preserving the
checkpoint's block-scaled FP8 semantics and reporting backend support only at
the level actually verified.

## Frozen upstream contract

- Pin the first implementation to model revision
  `017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a`. Update that revision only in a
  dedicated compatibility change after re-running config, tensor, prompt, and
  golden-logit checks.
- Use the revision-pinned Transformers Qwen3.5 implementation at commit
  `a597f974857b3d92939971296bc0deb93d33d780` as the executable numerical
  oracle. The checkpoint declares `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` and
  `model_type=qwen3_5`; it is not a standard Qwen3 decoder.
- Treat the text tower as 64 explicit layers: 48 Gated DeltaNet layers and 16
  gated full-attention layers at indices `3, 7, ..., 63`. Validate the complete
  `layer_types` array instead of inferring it only from an interval.
- Preserve the published geometry: hidden size 5,120; FFN 17,408; vocabulary
  248,320; full attention 24 Q heads / 4 KV heads / head dimension 256; linear
  attention 16 QK heads / 48 V heads / head dimensions 128; convolution kernel
  4; partial rotary dimension 64; interleaved MRoPE sections `[11, 11, 10]`;
  RoPE theta 10,000,000; native context 262,144.
- Treat large matrix weights as Safetensors `F8_E4M3` with a companion BF16
  `.weight_scale_inv`, dynamic activation quantization, and block size
  `[128,128]`. The dequantized value is
  `fp8_weight[row,col] * scale_inv[row/128,col/128]`; there is no zero point.
- Honor the unusual 66-shard index (`layers-0.safetensors` through
  `layers-63.safetensors`, `outside.safetensors`, and `mtp.safetensors`) rather
  than assuming `model-00001-of-*` names.
- Use the measured checkpoint inventory for planning: 24,699,207,680 FP8
  elements and 3,082,220,272 BF16 elements. The tensor payload is about 28.74
  GiB; fully expanded 16-bit and 32-bit representations are about 51.75 GiB
  and 103.49 GiB respectively, before cache, workspaces, and allocator
  headroom.

Primary upstream evidence:

- Model card: <https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/README.md>
- Model config: <https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/config.json>
- Tensor index: <https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/model.safetensors.index.json>
- Tokenizer config: <https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8/blob/017b9c7af6b5689d5dd426a76e0bc077eb5ca20a/tokenizer_config.json>
- Reference model: <https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/a597f974857b3d92939971296bc0deb93d33d780/src/transformers/models/qwen3_5/modeling_qwen3_5.py>
- Reference FP8 integration: <https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/a597f974857b3d92939971296bc0deb93d33d780/src/transformers/integrations/finegrained_fp8.py>

## Initial support contract

- The first release is text chat, one model on one device. It includes cached
  prefill/decode, streaming, thinking on/off, `reasoning_effort`, historical
  thinking preservation, and the existing XML tool-call flow.
- Publish 262,144 as the checkpoint's native logical maximum, but select and
  expose a smaller effective context when memory requires it. Never allocate
  the full logical context at model load. Do not claim the documented 1M YaRN
  extension until a separate RoPE-scaling implementation and validation pass.
- Do not load `mtp.*` for ordinary one-token generation. Keep MTP speculative
  decoding explicitly deferred.
- Make the vision tower optional in the shared Qwen3.5 wrapper and keep
  Qwen3.8 image/video capability disabled for the initial text release. Add
  image chat as a later, separately tested slice; keep video deferred until the
  media pipeline supports it end to end.
- Superseded by the dedicated-family plan above: reuse
  `ModelFamily::Qwen35Chat`, `NativeChatModel::Qwen35`, its hybrid
  scheduler state, and the current prefill/decode dispatch. Add a new
  `ModelVariant::Qwen3827BFp8`; do not create a parallel model family or route
  this checkpoint through the standard Qwen3 graph.
- Keep checkpoint storage format, resident weight representation, activation
  compute dtype, KV dtype, and recurrent-state dtype as separate concepts.
  `F8_E4M3` is a weight-storage format, not a valid generic compute-dtype
  override.

## Backend execution policy

| Backend | Correctness path required for first support | Optimized path | Initial hardware expectation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CPU | Stream each shard, apply 128x128 scales, materialize persistent F32 projections, and use existing CPU matmul. Keep recurrence/state math F32. | Add a packed block-FP8 GEMV/GEMM after the correct vertical slice if CPU memory or throughput requires it. | Plan for a 128 GB-class host; exact admission is derived, not hard-coded. |
| Metal | Stream/dequantize projections to F16, upload a layer at a time, and keep DeltaNet decay/recurrent math F32. Use F16 KV and F32 softmax/accumulation where required. | A packed Metal weight kernel can later retain FP8 bytes and dequantize in the GEMM, behind parity tests. | 64 GB is likely marginal; validate first on 96/128 GB unified-memory Apple Silicon with a fitted context. |
| CUDA | First provide a forced BF16/F16 dequantized fallback on a sufficiently large GPU. | Retain FP8 plus block scales and dynamically quantize activations in a native kernel. Target SM90 first; validate SM89 independently rather than inferring support. | Use an 80 GB device for the expanded fallback and 40/48 GB+ for native FP8 with a restricted context, subject to measured headroom. |

The ordinary Candle 0.11 CPU, Metal, and CUDA matmuls do not consume these FP8
weights, and `VarBuilder` casts the raw values without applying
`weight_scale_inv`. Therefore, using the existing Qwen3 Safetensors loader is a
hard correctness failure, not an acceptable fallback.

Runtime-state budgeting must include, per active sequence:

- F16/BF16 full-attention KV: 65,536 bytes/token across 16 layers, or exactly
  16 GiB at 262,144 tokens. F32 KV doubles that to 32 GiB.
- FP32 DeltaNet recurrent state: 144 MiB across 48 layers.
- The current three-token convolution-history representation: about 5.625 MiB
  across 48 layers.
- Live and staged/transactional state rows separately; do not multiply either
  fixed state by the logical context or page count.

## Verification and release gates

- [ ] Portable fixture gate: config/index parsing, exact required-tensor
      coverage, missing/partial shard rejection, FP8 scale math, native/GGUF
      norm and head-order distinctions, prompt token snapshots, state sizing,
      context fitting, catalog/API/UI exposure, and unload accounting.
- [ ] Tiny-model oracle gate: export deterministic fixtures from the pinned
      Transformers revision and compare prefill plus at least three cached
      decode steps, thinking modes/efforts, preserved history, and tool turns.
- [ ] Repository gate: focused model/downloader/runtime/server/UI tests, full
      serial core/server suites, strict Clippy, UI type/test/build checks,
      default/Metal/CUDA feature compilation, and backend-truth scripts.
- [ ] CPU real-model gate: revision-verified download, load, multi-token chat,
      cache equivalence, fitted-context rejection, peak RSS, and reclamation on
      a capable host.
- [ ] Metal real-model gate: the same behavioral checks plus 48-head recurrence,
      command-buffer synchronization, unified-memory peak, and oracle logits on
      a capable Apple Silicon host.
- [ ] CUDA real-model gate: forced-expanded evidence on a large GPU and native
      FP8 evidence on each claimed capability class, bound to the exact commit,
      model revision, driver/toolkit, device, and selected execution mode.
- [ ] Documentation gate: user model/chat pages and the support matrix state
      text-only scope, backend memory expectations, native versus expanded FP8,
      effective-context fitting, deferred features, and the exact evidence
      level without calling best-effort paths certified.

## Main risks and stop conditions

- Silent numerical corruption is most likely at FP8 scale orientation,
  zero-centered norms, `A_log`, native head repetition, or prompt rendering.
  Any golden-logit mismatch stops backend work until the first divergent layer
  is identified.
- A raw 28.74 GiB checkpoint-size estimate is unsafe for expanded CPU/Metal or

# KV Architecture Comparison with vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp — 2026-07-21

Goal: compare the proposed Izwi physical KV-cache and paged-attention plan with
current upstream serving engines, then identify which patterns Izwi should copy,
adapt, or deliberately avoid across CPU, Metal, and CUDA.

Constraints:
- [x] Research and planning only; do not modify product code.
- [x] Use current upstream primary documentation and source because these
      projects change rapidly.
- [x] Compare physical ownership, layouts, batching, prefix reuse, eviction,
      quantization, kernels, extensibility, and non-CUDA behavior.

Investigation plan:
- [x] Re-state the current Izwi proposal as explicit comparison criteria.
- [x] Audit vLLM's block manager, KV connector/cache API, paged attention,
      prefix caching, and backend abstractions.
- [x] Audit SGLang's token/page pools, radix cache, memory manager, attention
      backends, scheduling, and disaggregation contracts.
- [x] Audit llama.cpp's unified KV cache, sequence-cell allocation, context
      shifting, recurrent state, batching, and accelerator kernels.
- [x] Compare at least one additional production engine where it changes the
      recommendation materially.
- [x] Produce an Izwi-specific borrow/adapt/avoid matrix and revised priorities.

Review:
- The target is a convergence with current vLLM V1 and SGLang, not an unusual
  architecture: scheduler-owned logical block/slot identities address physical
  worker-owned arenas, and attention kernels consume those mappings directly.
  A metadata-only scheduler is valid; Izwi's current defect is that its IDs do
  not identify the model-owned tensors used by production forwards.
- vLLM provides the strongest precedent for model-produced typed cache specs,
  per-layer cache groups, explicit worker tensor layouts, persistent block
  tables, slot mappings, COW copies, hybrid managers, quantized layouts, and KV
  transfer connectors. Izwi should retain stronger generation-tagged
  prepare/write/commit/abort semantics and avoid vLLM's global block-shape
  compromises where independent cache domains are cleaner.
- SGLang most clearly separates request-to-token mappings, physical token/KV
  pools, page-aligned radix reuse, and backend-specific attention metadata. Its
  capability matrix shows that page size and layout must be negotiated by model,
  device, cache domain, and kernel (and potentially by prefill versus decode),
  rather than fixed engine-wide. Izwi should not expose SGLang's dense mutable
  request table or schedule-time mutation as its public ABI.
- llama.cpp master remains a unified dense/cell cache with indexed in-place
  writes and dense attention up to a high-water mark, not merged production
  paged attention. It is the best precedent here for CPU/CUDA/Metal portability,
  transactional batch preparation, quantized KV writes, context operations, and
  composing attention KV with recurrent state. Its separate paged-cache
  prototype independently demonstrates the concurrency benefit and the small
  low-concurrency scheduling/indirection cost.
- TensorRT-LLM validates separate physical pools for layers with different KV
  heads or attention windows, GQA-native storage, radix reuse, rolling windows,
  prioritized eviction, and host tiers. Its acknowledged static multi-pool
  memory partitioning weakness argues for borrowable domain budgets in Izwi.
- Revised design: a model adapter publishes typed cache-domain requirements; a
  backend negotiates physical page size/layout/dtype and produces arenas; the
  scheduler owns generation-safe request tables and transactional deltas; direct
  CPU/Metal/CUDA operations write, copy, zero, and attend over those pages. Keep
  full-attention, sliding-window, recurrent/SSM, convolutional, cross-attention,
  and opaque state as distinct capabilities under one composite memory contract.
- Revised order: physical arena and resource truth; versioned transactional table
  ABI; CPU reference and native Qwen3 batched migration; Metal/CUDA direct-page
  kernels; page-aligned prefix reuse and eviction; quantized/hybrid domains;
  genuine host offload; distributed/disaggregated transfer last. Preserve opaque
  width-one compatibility, but require typed cache specs for new paged adapters.

  model-state byte leases are a valuable newer source of physical truth.

  softmax avoids full-history concatenation. Partial-page append nevertheless
  materializes, concatenates, and rebuilds the page; decode still materializes

  and MLPs, but cache append and attention still run row by row. Qwen3 chat also
  constructs its cache with dense decode disabled, so the priority batched path

  physical arenas, not one homogeneous global pool. It must support multiple
  cache domains and auxiliary state: Qwen3.5 combines full-attention KV with
  recurrent and convolution tensors.

  generation-safe arena/table/slot contract; implement transactional in-place

  opaque fallbacks for Candle/internal and non-decoder state.

  unbounded staging vector that is drained only after physical execution,
  report reconciliation, and engine commit. LFM2.5 still generates token
  callbacks, but its whole decode is one atomic executor call, so no delta is
  externally visible until that call finishes.

  chat variants. Native Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 sequence execution still reaches a
  commit boundary per decode quantum. Atomic callback ASR and audio-chat paths

  rendering forward deltas immediately and are not the buffering layer.

  transaction validation. The selected design activates the existing
  `OutputVisibility::IncrementalCommitted` contract for non-tensor atomic
  producers and adds bounded, exact-session in-flight output checkpoints. Core
  validates and commits each monotonic checkpoint before publication; final
  success remains gated on the authoritative physical report and state commit.

  peer isolation. They have no temporal assertion that a delta arrives while
  atomic generation is still running, which is why the regression escaped.
  No server or real model was started.

# Continuous Tensor Batching Implementation Audit — 2026-07-20

Goal: independently review the completed implementation against the current
source and tests, identify any correctness, lifecycle, coverage, resource, or
production-readiness gaps, and make no production-code changes.

- [x] Map the complete branch diff and re-derive the implementation invariants.
- [x] Audit engine scheduling, physical dispatch, keyed commit, and failure semantics.

Review:
- The exact model-generation/stage fences, keyed physical-batch reconciliation,
  model-forward lock split, and fail-closed rollout controls are sound.
- Continuous Qwen decode never reaches width greater than one: the adapter sets
  an aggregate `max_work_units` budget of one, and every decode row costs one.
- Static Qwen TTS can form mixed-length padded physical batches, but the model
  internally splits by exact prefill length and reports only the largest
  subgroup width. Core then rejects all successfully generated rows. Late
  scalar fallback inside a planned static batch has the same contract break.
- Continuous stream chunks escape before physical-report validation and core
  commit. One row's full or closed channel can drop every peer decoder state
  and terminalize the whole tensor cohort.
- Prepared steps have no cancellation/rollback guard. Dropping a step between
  prepare and commit can strand scheduler quanta and active plans; ordinary
  preparation errors are recovered by aborting every runtime request.
- Production adapters advertise zero transient workspace, so resource
  admission and workspace telemetry are no-ops for real tensor execution.
- Width-one compatibility execution serializes all non-tensor models and makes
  the existing CPU/CUDA request-parallel executor path unreachable, regressing
  fallback throughput relative to `main`.
- The loaded adapter is a descriptive identity/contract object rather than the
  owner of planning and execution, so optimized model additions still require
  coordinated central executor, registry, and handler edits.
- Focused serialized validation passed: execution (21), execution-group (4),
  engine-core (28), adapter registry (14), loaded adapters (6), rollout (8),
  Qwen continuous parity, and the engine lock-release test. Metal core,
  server, and CLI all-target checks passed with one Cargo job. No server or
  real model was started. These suites do not cover the cross-layer failures
  above, which are established directly by the production control flow.

# Qwen3.5 Resource Regression Investigation — 2026-07-19

Goal: identify why the current Qwen3.5 branch freezes a memory-limited laptop
during decode and after repeated turns, then define a Candle-native repair and
verification plan without changing product code or starting risky model runs.

- [x] Diff the branch against its pre-change base and map new work in decode,
  prefill, state persistence, KV storage, and prefix reuse.
- [x] Quantify per-token and per-turn allocation, copy, command-buffer, and
  residency costs for the distinct 0.8B/2B and 4B/9B layouts.
- [x] Inspect Candle 0.11 Metal allocation and residency lifecycles directly.
- [x] Separate the primary decode freeze from secondary prefix and sequence-
  prefill amplification.
- [x] Produce a staged repair design and serialized performance/memory gates.

Review:
- The exact-storage changes put full recurrent-state, convolution-slot, logits,
  and growing dense-KV copies directly in token decode. On Metal each copy uses
  a new unpooled private buffer and blit encoder; this adds about 49 such
  operations per 0.8B/2B token and 65 per 4B/9B token.
- Candle registers those private allocations with its residency set but the
  path does not participate in pooled-buffer reclamation or visible drop-time
  deregistration. This makes the resource slope unbounded and adds heavy Metal
  allocation, residency-commit, encoder, fence, and copy pressure.
- The 4B fixed branch-added copy volume is roughly 50 MiB before its growing KV
  term, explaining why it stalls within only a few output tokens. Dense KV also
  re-copies the whole context, making total decode work quadratic.
- The prefix cache is a secondary multiplier for requests whose configured
  session bound allows capture. The standard chat UI's omitted max-token value
  becomes 4096 and normally makes the 256 MiB preauthorization reject snapshots,
  so the reported default-UI freeze does not require a prefix-cache hit.
- No server or model was started because direct source/lifecycle evidence is
  sufficient and the failing path risks another laptop-wide resource stall.

# Qwen3.5 Multi-Turn Chat Review — 2026-07-17

Goal: independently review the current Rust/Candle Qwen3.5 chat implementation,
including the distinct 0.8B/2B and 4B/9B architectures, diagnose the reported
second-turn `No valid Qwen3.5 logits to sample` failure, and produce a
source-backed implementation and verification plan without changing product code.

- [x] Inventory the current Qwen3.5 architecture, loader, prompt, executor, and session paths.
- [x] Establish authoritative 0.8B/2B versus 4B/9B architecture and chat-template behavior.
- [x] Trace first-turn and second-turn state, positions, masks, logits, and sampling.
- [x] Rank root causes and secondary correctness/performance gaps with code evidence.
- [x] Define a Candle-native implementation sequence and multi-turn regression matrix.

Review:
- The model-family split is broadly correct: 0.8B/2B use 24 layers and equal
  QK/V DeltaNet head counts, while 4B/9B use 32 layers and GGUF-reordered
  QK=16/V=32 tensors. The current tiled repeat is required for llama.cpp GGUF
  conversion and must not be replaced with Transformers' native head order.
- The reported sampler error means all in-vocabulary logits are non-finite. A
  new HTTP turn creates fresh hybrid state and re-prefills the full history, so
  this is not stale turn-one KV/DeltaNet state. The leading numerical suspects
  are overflow-unsafe DeltaNet softplus and Metal's implicit F32-to-F16 SDPA
  prefill; diagnostic finite checks are required to identify the first bad
  layer on the user's failing transcript.
- Independent correctness defects were confirmed: the unfused full-attention
  prefill has no causal mask; dense KV is ignored when detecting a cached
  prefix; GGUF `qwen35` preprocessing and token types are not honored; streamed
  output decodes isolated token IDs and can corrupt Unicode before the next
  turn; persistent small-model recurrent tensors can escape the scratch pool
  after their lease is released; and conv-ring views retain whole prefill
  projection buffers, invalidating physical cache estimates for longer prompts.
- A local 4B Metal smoke produced valid outputs for a 25-token first request and
  a 50-token two-turn replay. A roughly 1k-token replay was rejected earlier by
  physical cache reconciliation, confirming that the failure is length/path
  sensitive and that cache accounting is a separate blocker. Eight Qwen3.5 text
  unit tests and three renderer tests pass, but none cover numerical finiteness,
  prefill/decode parity, or a real multi-turn transcript.
- Recommended order: add diagnostics and a correctness reference path; fix
  tokenizer/decoder, stable F32 DeltaNet math, causal attention, dense-prefix
  continuation, owned persistent state, and compact conv history; then add the
  four-model multi-turn/parity matrix; finally implement real Candle custom
  kernels and optional exact-prefix state snapshots. No product code was changed.

Goal: reuse a successful Qwen3.5 turn's longest exact rendered-token prefix on
the next turn without changing chat-template, thinking, media, or position
semantics and without allowing mutable runtime state to alias across sessions.

  convolution slot/index, DeltaNet recurrent tensor, full-attention dense/paged
  KV tensor/count, and exact next position. Boundary logits are intentionally
  omitted because restoration is accepted only when at least one exact suffix
  token follows the checkpoint; suffix prefill produces the required logits.
- [x] Match the exact loaded model instance, variant, backend, activation/KV
  policy, rendered token IDs, and position triplets; fail closed for multimodal
  prompts until encoded media has a deterministic identity.
- [x] Publish a reusable pre-generation boundary only after successful request
  completion, so cancelled/failed turns cannot seed cache state.
- [x] Bound retained physical storage by conservatively deduplicated backing
  bytes, skip oversized entries, evict least-recently-used entries, and never
  hold the cache lock during Candle copies or inference.

Implementation plan:
- [x] Add a small concurrency-safe exact-prefix LRU module with model-lifetime
  fencing, longest-prefix selection, byte accounting, and deterministic tests.
- [x] Add opaque Qwen3.5 prompt/snapshot APIs that can checkpoint the stable
  assistant-header boundary and independently fork all Candle storage.
- [x] Wire executor prefill to restore a matching snapshot, prefill only the
  suffix, and publish the next checkpoint only after clean completion.
- [x] Cover exact token/position hit, mismatch, LRU eviction, stale model scope,
  and independent cloned-session evolution.
- [x] Run exact-file rustfmt, focused cache/chat/executor tests, a core compile
  check, real 4B two-turn cache-hit acceptance, and final diff/ownership review.

Review:
- Added a 256 MiB default, environment-bounded exact-prefix LRU scoped to the
  exact loaded model instance, variant, backend, activation/KV policy, token
  IDs, and position triplets. Multimodal requests remain deliberate misses.
- Stable checkpoints are taken immediately after the current assistant header,

## Source-Backed Current State

Core engine and scheduler:
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/config.rs` already exposes the main knobs:
  batch size, tokens per step, chunked prefill thresholds, adaptive batching,
  TTFT/TPOT targets, deadlines, decode quanta, KV tiering, and backend
  selection.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/core.rs` already separates scheduled prefill and
  decode batches, records queue/prefill/decode/TTFT breakdowns, groups
  compatible subbatches by task/model, and serializes Metal prefill/decode work.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/scheduler/mod.rs` already has adaptive prefill
  reservation, KV pressure backoff, priority aging, deadline scoring, paused
  prefill handling, and bounded multi-token decode quanta. The missing P1 piece
  is not "add a scheduler"; it is class-aware admission, policy tuning,
  stronger tests, and better attribution.

Executor and model dispatch:
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/executor.rs` keeps backend-specific request
  parallelism conservative: CPU and Metal default to one concurrent request,
  CUDA can use configured parallelism, and long model calls are wrapped through
  `run_blocking` plus panic handling.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/executor/dispatch.rs` dispatches by task type to
  TTS, ASR, chat, and audio-chat handlers, with backend-specific request
  parallelization gated through executor policy.
- ASR, chat, Qwen TTS, and audio-chat handlers mix incremental paths with full
  direct generation paths. Some full paths can occupy an engine step for a long
  call, so P1 should add explicit phase timing and move CPU preprocessing or
  full direct work to bounded lanes rather than blindly increasing fan-out.

KV cache, attention, and backend policy:
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/cache/kv.rs` is a logical block manager with
  prefix reuse, soft caps, COW, residency hints, and telemetry.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/cache/metal.rs` wraps the logical manager with
  Metal memory pressure handling and dynamic soft limits.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/models/shared/attention/paged.rs` implements the
  model-level paged KV cache, page sizing, KV quantization gates, and grouped
  paged decode attention.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/models/architectures/qwen3/core.rs` already has dense
  decode cache paths, bounded growth, page migration, fused attention gates, and
  Qwen-specific profiling. P1 should align and measure these two cache layers
  before adding new cache mechanisms.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/backends/router.rs`, `capabilities.rs`, and
  `models/registry.rs` centralize backend/device selection, but runtime
  diagnostics still do not expose a consistent actual loaded dtype/device/kernel
  policy for every loaded model.

Runtime and telemetry:
- `crates/izwi-core/src/runtime/service.rs` owns the background engine step
  driver, request completion waiters, model residency leases, and runtime
  telemetry snapshots.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/runtime/telemetry/metrics.rs` already captures stage
  observations, queue wait, prefill, decode, TTFT, pipeline counters, route
  decisions, broker validation, and benchmark-facing samples. P1 should reuse
  this rather than inventing a parallel metrics surface.
- Direct TTS and ASR runtime methods can bypass the generic incremental engine
  for some families, so P1 admission and observability must cover direct model
  calls as well as `EngineCoreRequest` paths.

Server, batch, media, and realtime:
- `crates/izwi-server/src/state.rs` has a global request semaphore but not
  route-specific or resource-class-specific admission.
- `crates/izwi-server/src/batch_runtime/store.rs` claims the next queued stage
  by priority and sequence, but does not filter by worker queue names,
  capabilities, backend, model, or resource hints.
- `crates/izwi-server/src/batch_runtime/worker.rs` records batch stage
  lifecycle events and supports lease recovery, but lacks drain semantics and
  richer resource-aware scheduling.
- Batch ASR in `crates/izwi-server/src/api/transcription/handlers.rs` enqueues
  a single ASR stage whose executor starts the existing route processor and then
  polls the transcription projection. Batch TTS in
  `crates/izwi-server/src/api/speech_history/handlers.rs` uses a similar
  single-stage shape.
- `crates/izwi-server/src/api/media/handlers.rs` already builds canonical
  16 kHz mono WAV derivatives for uploaded media, but batch ASR and realtime
  paths do not consistently reuse this canonical asset flow.
- `crates/izwi-server/src/app/voice_realtime.rs` and
  `transcription_realtime.rs` already have bounded websocket output queues and
  backpressure counters. Voice turns still acquire the global request semaphore,
  while transcription realtime runs one in-flight inference at a time from a
  rolling buffer or native streaming ASR.

## Implementation Sequence

### Phase 0: Baseline and Guardrails

Goal: lock down current behavior and measurements before changing hot paths.

- [ ] Define the P1 benchmark matrix:
  - interactive voice turn, modular pipeline, short input;
  - unified speech-to-speech turn, short input;
  - chat/text streaming, short and long prompts;
  - Qwen TTS short and medium text;
  - ASR short, long, and chunked audio;
  - batch ASR/TTS mixed queue;
  - concurrent realtime websocket plus batch load.
- [ ] For each benchmark, record current p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, queue wait,
  prefill, decode, tokens/sec, real-time factor, audio duration, output quality
  pass/fail, backend, device, loaded model, and memory pressure.
- [ ] Create fixture-level quality gates so faster output cannot pass with empty
  text, bad transcript coverage, broken speaker attribution, missing audio, or
  malformed streaming events.
- [ ] Add a small benchmark manifest or script per workload if one does not
  already exist, reusing the CLI benchmark report and stage observation parser.
- [ ] Save baseline artifacts under the existing benchmark/report convention.
- [ ] Verification:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core runtime::telemetry::metrics::tests`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-cli commands::bench::tests`
  - run at least one local smoke benchmark on the available backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- The baseline can distinguish queueing, prefill, decode, sampling, codec,
  media, postprocess, and artifact time for the workloads P1 will touch.
- The benchmark report refuses performance wins that regress output quality.
- The backlog markdown remains untracked/uncommitted.

### Phase 1: Admission, Latency Classes, and Backpressure

Goal: make work admission explicit before tuning scheduling.

- [ ] Introduce a small `LatencyClass` or `WorkloadClass` model in the runtime
  layer, then map it from routes and task types:
  - realtime interactive voice;
  - websocket realtime transcription;
  - streaming chat;
  - streaming TTS;
  - regular online API request;
  - batch stage;
  - background observation/extraction.
- [ ] Add an `AdmissionDecision` surface that can accept, queue, shed, or retry
  with a reason and retry hint.
- [ ] Apply admission before expensive model loading, media decode, and route
  processing where possible.
- [ ] Replace or wrap the global server semaphore with class-aware limits:
  preserve the current global cap, but add smaller per-class caps and queue
  depth accounting.
- [ ] Thread class and admission outcome into runtime stage observations,
  Prometheus output, and benchmark reports.
- [ ] Keep realtime websocket outbound backpressure separate from inference
  admission, but correlate both in telemetry by session/route.
- [ ] Tests:
  - unit tests for class mapping and admission decisions;
  - route tests proving batch work cannot starve realtime work;
  - websocket tests proving backpressure counters still increment on full
    outbound queues;
  - server tests proving rejected or retried work returns a stable error
    contract.

Acceptance criteria:
- A realtime request can be admitted or protected independently of batch work.
- Queue wait samples can be grouped by class and route.
- Existing request limits still apply when class limits are disabled.

### Phase 2: Scheduler Policy Tuning

Goal: tune the existing scheduler using the new class signal instead of adding a
second scheduling system.

- [ ] Extend `EngineCoreRequest` metadata with the latency/workload class.
- [ ] Make adaptive prefill reservation class-aware:
  protect realtime/chat TTFT while still allowing batch prefill throughput when
  the system is under low interactive load.
- [ ] Make decode quanta class-aware:
  keep one-token decode for latency-sensitive streams, and allow bounded
  multi-token decode for isolated batch/offline requests.
- [ ] Add explicit starvation guards for paused prefill and low-priority batch
  requests.
- [ ] Improve scheduler telemetry with selected class, reason, queued age,
  skipped reason, KV pressure decision, prefill reservation, and decode quantum.
- [ ] Add scheduler tests for:
  - realtime request arriving while batch prefill is waiting;
  - KV pressure reducing admission without deadlocking;
  - paused prefill resume ordering;
  - deadline aging;
  - decode quantum collapse when an interactive request appears;
  - CPU/Metal behavior matching current serial expectations.
- [ ] Run benchmark diff against Phase 0 baselines.

Acceptance criteria:
- Interactive p95 TTFT improves or stays flat under mixed batch load.
- Batch throughput improves only when quality and interactive latency gates pass.
- No scheduler behavior depends on CUDA-only assumptions unless gated.

### Phase 3: Executor Concurrency and Phase Separation

Goal: make executor concurrency intentional and measurable.

- [ ] Add a small executor phase timing contract for media decode, prompt build,
  tokenizer, model prefill, model decode, sampling, codec, and postprocess.
- [ ] Wire handler-level phase timings from ASR, chat, Qwen TTS, and audio-chat
  into `RuntimeTelemetryCollector` instead of relying on total executor time.
- [ ] Split CPU preprocessing from GPU-bound model work where the code already
  makes the boundary clear:
  - audio decode and chunk planning;
  - text normalization/tokenization;
  - prompt/history assembly;
  - codec encode/decode.
- [ ] Use bounded blocking lanes for CPU preprocessing. Do not increase Metal
  or CPU model request parallelism by default.
- [ ] For CUDA, evaluate request parallelism and subbatch dispatch with
  benchmark proof before changing defaults.
- [ ] Isolate full direct generation paths that currently occupy an engine step
  so they cannot hide queueing or block incremental work without attribution.
- [ ] Preserve panic handling and cancellation semantics from the current
  executor wrapper.
- [ ] Tests:
  - executor policy tests per backend;
  - cancellation and panic tests;
  - telemetry tests for phase timing propagation;
  - integration tests showing direct and incremental paths report comparable
    timing fields.

Acceptance criteria:
- Executor reports where time is spent for every P1 workload.
- CPU preprocessing can overlap safely with model work where backend policy

### Phase 4: KV Cache and Attention Alignment

Goal: align logical engine KV policy with model-level cache behavior before
adding more cache features.

  - Qwen dense decode cache in `qwen3/core.rs`.
- [ ] Add model-level cache telemetry:
  page size, quantization mode, dense decode enabled, dense-to-paged migration

  gates, dense decode enablement, and soft-cap behavior.
- [ ] Benchmark cache policy matrix:
  - Qwen chat decode;

- [ ] Only after the telemetry confirms the bottleneck, tune block/page sizes,
  dense decode thresholds, and KV quantization defaults per backend/model.
- [ ] Keep Q4/int8 KV cache behavior opt-in where the current code warns about

Acceptance criteria:
- P1 can explain KV memory use and cache hit/miss behavior at both logical and
  model levels.
- Cache tuning improves decode throughput or memory pressure without hidden
  quality regressions.
- No full theoretical KV cache preallocation is introduced.

configuration alone.

### Phase 7: Server Runtime, Batch, Media, and Realtime Integration

Goal: make server-side orchestration match the optimized core engine.

Batch runtime:

Goal: prove the P1 implementation is correct, faster, and safer to operate.

Acceptance criteria:

# Voice Realtime Connection Close Fix

Goal: find and fix the issue where starting a voice realtime connection appears
to connect and then immediately surfaces `Voice realtime connection closed`.

Plan:
- [x] Inspect the UI websocket lifecycle and error handling around voice
  realtime startup.
- [x] Inspect the server `/v1/voice/realtime/ws` handler for startup errors,
  protocol mismatches, and immediate close paths.
- [x] Reproduce or isolate the failing behavior with focused tests or a local
  websocket probe.
- [x] Patch the smallest responsible UI/server contract so startup failures are
  surfaced correctly and valid sessions remain open.
- [x] Add or update regression tests for the broken contract.
- [x] Run focused UI/Rust verification, plus a smoke/probe if practical.
- [x] Add review notes with root cause, changed files, and verification output.

Review:
- Root cause: the voice websocket handshake was healthy, but the first browser
  microphone frame (`2048` samples at `48 kHz`) entered `VadScorer` and
  panicked inside `StreamingLinearResampler::push`. For an exact 3:1 resample
  ratio, `next_src_pos` advanced to `2049` after reading a `2048` sample
  buffer, then attempted `drain(0..2049)`, killing the websocket task and
  surfacing as `Voice realtime connection closed` in the UI.
- Fix: cap the streaming resampler drain range to the current input buffer
  length. This preserves the next source offset while preventing out-of-range
  drains for common browser audio callback sizes.
- Changed file: `crates/izwi-vad/src/lib.rs`.
- Verification: reproduced the original websocket close (`1006`, server panic)
  with a one-frame Bun websocket probe; after the fix, the same probe sent 25
  `48 kHz` / `2048`-sample frames and the socket stayed open until the probe
  intentionally closed it.
- Tests: `cargo test -p izwi-vad` passed; `cargo test -p izwi-server
  voice_realtime` passed.

# Fish Audio S2 Pro Full Synthesis Implementation Plan

## Fish S2 CPU/Metal Performance Investigation

Goal: research Candle/Rust-only CPU and Metal performance opportunities for
`FishAudio-S2-Pro`, without changing product code in this task.

Plan:
- [x] Review prior Fish S2 notes and lessons for backend-specific constraints.
- [x] Map the current Fish S2 synthesis path from request through reference
  encode, slow semantic prefill/decode, fast codebook decode, and DAC decode.
- [x] Inventory existing Izwi custom kernels and Candle backend coverage that
  could apply to Fish S2 on CPU/Metal.
- [x] Identify high-impact missing Metal kernels or Candle dispatch changes,
  with expected blast radius and verification gates.
- [x] Identify high-impact CPU improvements, especially Accelerate/vecmat,
  thread use, and avoidable host/device synchronization.
- [x] Define benchmark goals and acceptance thresholds for short, medium, and
  diagnostic Fish S2 runs.
- [x] Add investigation review findings with source-backed recommendations.

Review:
- Observability is the first blocker. Fish S2 generation exposes flat
  diagnostics (`reference_encode_ms`, `prompt_build_ms`, `slow_prefill_ms`,
  `ar_decode_ms`, `dac_decode_ms`, `total_model_ms`) from
  `fish_s2/mod.rs`, while the benchmark stage parser expects nested
  `timings_ms`. The runtime telemetry snapshot is also zero because Fish S2
  bypasses the generic incremental executor. Add Fish S2 stage counters,
  `frames_generated`, `stop_reason`, and audio duration to the CLI/server
  output before treating RTF or tokens/sec as reliable optimization signals.
- Saved-voice reference encode is the highest-confidence request-level win.
  The speech path resolves saved/direct reference audio, then
  `generate_with_reference` DAC-encodes that reference on every request before
  prompt construction. Cache `FishS2VqCodes` by model id, saved voice/audio
  hash, reference text, codec version, device, and dtype. Target a warm saved
  voice cache hit that skips DAC encode and host code download entirely.
- The slow and fast AR caches are the main Metal decode bottleneck. Slow and
  fast attention append K/V using `Tensor::cat` on every step; Candle `cat`
  allocates a new output and copies old cache contents. Replace this with a
  preallocated or chunk-grown dense KV cache with a valid length, then use the
  existing Metal single-token GQA decode kernel for slow/fast `seq_len = 1`.
- Fish S2 should reuse existing Izwi Metal transformer kernels before adding
  new transformer kernels. Drop-in candidates are fused `silu(gate) * up`,
  q/k RMSNorm, BSHD RoPE pair, RMSNorm, and decode GQA attention. LFM/Qwen
  call sites already show the expected fallback pattern. Prefill/full-sequence
  attention should try Candle Metal SDPA where the mask and shape constraints
  fit.
- Host sampling readback is a major synchronization risk. Semantic sampling
  currently copies the full slow logits row to CPU every generated frame even
  though only the semantic token range plus EOS are valid. Fast codebook
  sampling copies one full codebook row per residual step. Use device argmax
  for deterministic/greedy cases, slice semantic logits before host top-p, and
  defer a full GPU top-p/argsort kernel until after the cheaper wins land.
- DAC needs codec-specific kernels, not just transformer reuse. Fish DAC uses
  depthwise/grouped Conv1d in ConvNeXt blocks; Candle grouped Conv1d chunks
  per group and concatenates outputs, which is poor for depthwise. Add Metal
  and CPU specialized depthwise causal Conv1d for the DAC shapes, and fuse
  Snake activation (`x + sin(alpha*x)^2 / alpha`) to avoid multiple elementwise
  launches and temporaries. Reuse Parakeet/Kokoro Metal conv patterns as
  references, not direct copies.
- Quantizer encode/decode can avoid repeated normalization and large
  intermediate distance tensors. Cache normalized codebooks once per
  quantizer/device/dtype, and consider a fused nearest-code kernel that returns
  argmin directly without materializing the full distance matrix. This mostly
  helps reference-cache misses and direct-reference requests.
- CPU should stay F32. Candle Accelerate matmul supports F32/F64 and rejects
  F16, while Fish S2 already forces CPU F32 and Metal F16. CPU work should
  focus on Accelerate-enabled release builds, avoiding extra host copies,
  depthwise Conv1d/Snake kernels, cached normalized codebooks, and thread
  tuning to avoid Rayon/Accelerate oversubscription.
- RoPE cache construction is repeated in slow, fast, and DAC attention. Preload
  or lazily cache RoPE tables on the target device and narrow by position,
  matching the pattern used by other architectures.

Recommended work order:
1. Add Fish S2 benchmark observability and a stage-timing parser.
2. Add saved-voice VQ-code caching.
3. Replace slow/fast KV `Tensor::cat` with preallocated/chunk-grown KV.
4. Wire existing Metal fused MLP, RoPE, q/k norm, RMSNorm, and decode GQA into
   Fish S2 with exact fallback tests.
5. Add greedy/device argmax and semantic-logit slicing before host top-p.
6. Add DAC depthwise Conv1d and Snake kernels for Metal and CPU.
7. Cache quantizer normalized codebooks and only then consider fused nearest
   code/top-p kernels if stage timings still justify them.

Benchmark goals:
- Required benchmark fields: backend, build profile, model dtype, text length,
  saved voice cache state, frames generated, stop reason, audio duration,
  reference encode, prompt build, slow prefill, AR decode, DAC decode, total,
  P50/P95, and RTF. Reject performance comparisons where the short-text run
  produces less than 0.5 seconds of audio unless it is explicitly the
  one-frame diagnostic benchmark.
- Diagnostic one-frame target for the current benchmark shape: Metal release
  P50 under 30 s after observability/reference caching, under 12 s after KV
  and fused transformer work, and under 8 s as a stretch target. CPU release
  P50 under 90 s initially, under 45 s after CPU cache/sampling/DAC cleanup.
- Short saved-voice target with meaningful output (`max_frames` at least 16 or
  audio at least 0.5 s): Metal P50 under 60 s after reference caching, under
  30 s after KV/fused transformer work, and under 20 s as a stretch target.
  CPU P50 under 120 s after reference caching, under 75 s after CPU cleanup,
  and under 60 s as a stretch target.
- Medium saved-voice target, 2-3 s generated audio: Metal RTF under 50 after
  reference caching, under 20 after KV/fused transformer work, and under 10 as
  a stretch target. CPU RTF under 150 initially, under 80 after CPU cleanup,
  and under 50 as a stretch target.
- Stage targets: warm saved-voice `reference_encode_ms` under 50 ms; slow
  prefill under 8 s on Metal and under 25 s on CPU for the short prompt;
  AR decode under 500 ms/frame on Metal initially and under 200 ms/frame after
  fused decode; DAC decode under 2 s on Metal and under 5 s on CPU for up to
  one second of generated audio.
- Benchmark matrix: run warm saved-voice cache, cold saved-voice cache miss,
  direct reference audio, one-frame diagnostic, short 16/32-frame output, and
  medium 2-3 s output on both Metal release and CPU release with Accelerate.

  for greedy Fish S2 residual codebook selection; avoiding full fast-output

Review:
- Phase 1 exposed Fish S2 benchmark diagnostics without loading a real model:
  Fish S2 generation now emits nested `timings_ms`, `prompt`, `decode`, and
  `audio` sections while preserving the legacy flat fields.
- The CLI TTS stage parser now recognizes Fish S2 `reference`, `ar_decode`, and
  `dac_decode` stages and can parse both nested and old flat Fish payloads.

  - `cargo test -p izwi-core generation_diagnostics_include_benchmark_stage_shape`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-cli fish_s2_tts_stage_timing_collection`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core -p izwi-cli`
- Phase 2 added a small bounded Fish S2 reference-code cache keyed by reference
  sample rate, audio sample count, bitwise audio hash, and reference text. Warm
  saved voices and repeated direct references now reuse VQ codes instead of
  rerunning DAC reference encode, and diagnostics include `reference_cache_hit`.
- Phase 2 verification:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core 'models::architectures::fish_s2::tests::'`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core`
- Phase 3 replaced slow/fast AR K/V concatenation with a shared chunk-grown
  `FishS2KvCache` that uses contiguous storage plus `slice_set` and returns a
  valid-prefix view for attention. Cache length now reports valid tokens rather
  than allocated capacity.
- Phase 3 verification:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core`
- Phase 4 wired the safe reusable kernel subset:
  - slow/fast one-token decode now tries the existing Metal fused GQA decode
    kernel against full contiguous KV backing storage plus valid length,
  - slow/fast/DAC feed-forward blocks now try fused `silu(gate) * up`,
  - CPU and unsupported Metal shapes keep exact Candle fallbacks.
- Phase 4 intentionally did not add q/k RMSNorm or RoPE pair fusion yet:
  q/k fusion needs packed norm weights, and RoPE pair needs cached packed
  cos/sin tables to avoid rebuilding packing per layer/step.
- Phase 4 verification:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core`
- Phase 5 changed semantic sampling to read back only compact candidates
  (semantic token range plus optional EOS) instead of the full vocabulary row,
  preserving top-p and RAS behavior. Fast codebook greedy sampling now uses
  device argmax on Metal/CUDA and keeps host top-p for stochastic sampling.
- Phase 5 verification:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core`
- Phase 6 added codec-side acceleration:
  - Fish S2 depthwise causal Conv1d now opportunistically reuses the existing
    Parakeet Metal depthwise Conv1d kernel for true depthwise F32 shapes,
    including bias add, and falls back to Candle otherwise.
  - Fish S2 Snake activation now has a CPU F32 custom op that fuses the
    elementwise expression into one pass; unsupported shapes use the existing
    Candle expression.
- Phase 6 verification:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core`
- Phase 7 caches each Fish S2 vector quantizer's L2-normalized codebook at
  load time and reuses it during nearest-code encode. A fused nearest-code
  kernel remains a possible later Metal optimization, but the repeated
  normalization cost is now removed from reference-cache misses/direct refs.
- Phase 7 verification:

  - `cargo check -p izwi-core`
- Phase 8 corrected the compact semantic sampler with the old full-mask
  fallback, then added three bounded one-frame optimizations discovered during
  signoff:
  - greedy fast-codebook IDs stay as tensors through the next embedding and are
    materialized after the frame,
  - greedy first-frame semantic code selection feeds the fast decoder on device
    before materializing the generated frame,
  - `max_frames == 1` skips slow KV-cache construction and skips the unused
    post-frame slow decode step.

## Goal
Implement complete Fish Audio S2 Pro synthesis in Rust/Candle with logical phase
commits. The target is reference-voice TTS from audio+text input to generated
waveform output, using the public `fishaudio/s2-pro` checkpoint artifacts:
sharded safetensors for `DualARTransformer` plus `codec.pth` for the DAC codec.

Hard constraints:
- Rust/Candle only; no Python sidecar or alternate inference runtime.
- Commit each completed phase separately.
- Allow `FishAudioS2Pro` to be downloadable/inferable once native synthesis is
  wired, while keeping the ignored real-model smoke as the post-download proof
  gate.
- Verify against upstream Fish Speech source contracts before enabling.

## Implementation Phases
- [x] Existing scaffold: catalog/downloader/API/UI metadata, artifact/config
  validation, tokenizer shell, registry/runtime dispatch, and disabled safety
  gate are committed.
- [x] Phase 1: add source-backed parity contracts for upstream Fish Speech S2.
  Capture exact tensor remaps, prompt tensor construction, sampling rules, DAC
  config constants, and codec state-dict key expectations in executable Rust
  tests/fixtures.
- [x] Phase 2: implement Fish S2 weight loading. Add a sharded safetensor
  resolver with upstream key remapping (`text_model.model.*` -> slow path,
  `audio_decoder.*` -> fast path), dtype/device selection, required tensor
  shape checks, and tiny synthetic VarBuilder tests.
- [x] Phase 3: implement prompt/reference conditioning. Replace the simple
  ChatML text helper with upstream-compatible `ContentSequence` behavior:
  modality token, speaker/reference text, VQ semantic token mapping, `(1 +
  num_codebooks, seq)` prompt tensors, and audio/VQ masks.
- [x] Phase 4: implement the slow `DualARTransformer` text/semantic path:
  embeddings, codebook embedding merge, scaled codebook embeddings, packed QKV

  - Prompt input is shaped `(num_codebooks + 1, seq)`.
  - The first row is text/semantic token IDs; VQ rows hold codebook IDs at
    semantic-token positions.
  - Semantic tokens are contiguous and map as `semantic_token = codebook0 +
    semantic_begin_id`.
  - Generation samples semantic/im-end tokens from the slow LM, then generates
    each frame's codebooks through the fast transformer.
  - Codec config is DAC at 44.1 kHz with encoder rates `[2,4,8,8]`,
    decoder rates `[8,8,4,2]`, one 4096-entry semantic RVQ codebook, and nine
    1024-entry residual RVQ codebooks.

  - `model_type = "fish_qwen3_omni"`
  - `architectures = ["DualARTransformer"]`
  - `torch_dtype = "bfloat16"`
  - `vocab_size = 155776`
  - `bos_token_id = 151643`, `eos_token_id = 151645`,
    `pad_token_id = 151643`
  - `audio_pad_token_id = 151677`, `semantic_start_token_id = 151678`,
    `semantic_end_token_id = 155773`
  - `num_codebooks = 10`, `codebook_size = 4096`
  - top-level `max_seq_len = 4096`
- Slow text/semantic path:
  - Nested `text_config` is Qwen3-shaped.
  - 36 decoder layers, hidden size 2560, intermediate size 9728.
  - 32 attention heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 128.
  - RoPE theta 1,000,000, RMS norm eps 1e-6.
  - The safetensor index uses `text_model.model.*` and
    `text_model.lm_head.weight` keys.
- Fast audio path:
  - Nested `audio_decoder_config` is a compact autoregressive decoder.
  - 6 layers, hidden size 5120, 32 attention heads, 8 KV heads.
  - The safetensor index uses `audio_decoder.*` keys such as
    `layers.*.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight`, codebook embeddings, classifier
    weights, and speaker/prosody adapters.
- Prompt/tokenization:
  - `chat_template.jinja` is ChatML-like and emits `<|im_start|>role` /
    `<|im_end|>` messages with an optional assistant generation prompt.
  - Use the Hugging Face tokenizer JSON and special-token map, not a hand-coded
    tokenizer.
- Model behavior from card/upstream code:
  - S2 Pro is a multilingual TTS model based on Fish Audio's S2 architecture.
  - The architecture uses dual autoregressive generation: a slower semantic
    token stream and a faster acoustic/codebook decoder.
  - The model card describes inline contextual emotion/speed/volume control and
    a token rate around 21.5 tokens/sec.
- The current card mentions streaming/incremental generation support in the
  architecture, but Izwi should start with final-only synthesis until parity
  is proven.

# Fish Audio S2 Pro Voice Selection Investigation and Plan

## Goal
Determine whether Fish Audio S2 Pro ships selectable built-in voices and plan
the product/API work needed for users to select compatible voice behavior in
the desktop app and API.

## Investigation Findings
- [x] Inspect the current Hugging Face model card and artifact tree.
- [x] Inspect local downloaded artifacts under the Izwi model directory.
- [x] Inspect upstream Fish Speech inference/server code and docs.
- [x] Inspect Izwi backend, desktop, and Studio voice workflow contracts.

Findings:
- The `fishaudio/s2-pro` artifact bundle does not include a named voice
  catalog, voice manifest, speaker list, reference-audio presets, or paired
  reference transcript assets. The shipped assets are model weights,
  tokenizer/config/template files, license/readme, overview image, and
  `codec.pth`.
- The model card advertises inline natural-language control, multi-speaker /
  multi-turn capability, and reference-voice workflows, but it does not expose
  a list of model-shipped built-in voices.
- Upstream Fish Speech allows reference-free generation by skipping the
  reference-audio step, which lets the model randomly choose a voice timbre.
- Upstream `reference_id` resolves a saved reference folder under
  `references/<id>`; it is a user/server-managed reference voice, not a
  built-in S2 Pro speaker identifier.
- Izwi currently models voice workflows as `built_in`, `saved`, and
  description-driven variants. Fish S2 Pro is correctly marked
  `supports_builtin_voices = false` and `supports_reference_voice = true`.

Conclusion:
- Fish S2 Pro does not appear to have model-shipped named built-in voices.
  Users can select saved/reference voices, and Izwi can expose a random
  no-reference voice workflow. Selectable preset voices would need to be Izwi
  curated reference presets with explicit audio/text assets and license review,
  not "built-in voices" from the model.

## Implementation Plan
- [ ] Phase 1: Add a first-class random/no-reference voice capability.
  - Extend `SpeechModelCapabilities` with `supports_random_voice` or replace
    the current booleans with an explicit `voice_workflows` list while keeping
    backward-compatible fields for existing UI/API clients.
  - Mark `FishAudioS2Pro` as `supports_reference_voice = true`,
    `supports_random_voice = true`, and `supports_builtin_voices = false`.
  - Surface the new capability through `/v1/admin/models`, OpenAPI schemas, and
    `ui/src/shared/api/models.ts`.
  - Add catalog/server/UI tests proving Fish S2 advertises saved/reference plus
    random voice support without reporting built-in voices.

- [ ] Phase 2: Implement Fish S2 no-reference synthesis in Rust/Candle.
  - Add a tokenizer prompt builder for the upstream no-reference conversation:

  - Add `FishS2TtsModel::generate_random_voice` or a
    `FishS2VoiceCondition::Random` path that skips DAC reference encoding and
    uses the same slow/fast AR decode and DAC decode pipeline.
  - Keep reference-voice generation unchanged for saved voices and direct
    reference audio/text requests.
  - Add unit tests for prompt shape, audio masks/parts, max-frame accounting,

  - Add an ignored real-model smoke for reference-free Fish S2 generation using

  - Accept `voice_mode = random` with no `saved_voice_id`,

# Fish S2 Saved-Voice No-Frames Bug Fix Plan

## Goal
Fix the terminal/server failure where FishAudio-S2-Pro saved-voice TTS can
sample `<|im_end|>` before producing any audio frame and return:
`Fish S2 generation produced no audio frames`.

## Implementation Plan
- [x] Record the active bug-fix plan before editing product code.
- [x] Inspect Fish S2 saved-voice request resolution and the semantic sampling
  loop.
- [x] Implement a minimal runtime fix that prevents frame-zero end-of-audio for
  non-empty Fish S2 TTS requests while preserving normal EOS handling after at
  least one generated frame.
- [x] Add a regression test around the semantic sampler so EOS is masked only
  before the first frame.
- [x] Run focused Fish S2 tests plus a compile check for the touched crates.
- [x] Commit the fix separately from local task notes.

## Verification
- [x] `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
- [x] `cargo check -p izwi-core -p izwi-server`

## Review
- Fixed the Fish S2 semantic sampler so `<|im_end|>` is masked only until the
  first acoustic frame has been generated. This prevents a valid saved-voice
  request from terminating with zero frames, while preserving normal end-token
  handling after audible output exists.
- Added regression tests for both pre-first-frame EOS masking and post-frame EOS
  acceptance.
- Commit: `d2f99ec7` (`Prevent Fish S2 zero-frame EOS`).
- Could not reproduce against saved voice
  `3795c07b-9d2a-44b5-a28b-d1d8450dc71d` via HTTP because no local server was
  listening on `127.0.0.1:3000` during verification.

## Repository Fit
- Add S2 Pro as a new native TTS family, not as a Qwen3 TTS variant. The text
  backbone is Qwen3-shaped, but the model has different artifact layout, tensor
  prefixes, packed QKV modules, a fast audio decoder, and a separate codec.
- Backend/catalog surfaces to update in a future implementation:
  - `crates/izwi-core/src/catalog/metadata.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-core/src/catalog/variant.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-core/src/models/families/mod.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-core/src/models/architectures/mod.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-core/src/models/registry.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-core/src/runtime/tts.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-core/src/artifacts/downloader.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-server/src/api/openai/audio/speech.rs`
  - `crates/izwi-server/src/api/admin/models.rs` if API shape needs new flags
  - `ui/src/types.ts`
  - `ui/src/features/models/catalog/modelMetadata.ts`
  - `ui/src/features/models/catalog/routeModelCatalog.ts`
- The existing `SpeechModelCapabilities` model can represent first-pass S2:
  reference voice supported, built-in voices unsupported, voice description
  unsupported at API level unless instructions are intentionally mapped to
  Fish inline control text, streaming unsupported initially, speed control
  unsupported initially, long-form support deferred until chunking is tested.
- The OpenAI speech request path already supports `reference_audio`,
  `reference_text`, and `saved_voice_id`. S2 should follow the VibeVoice
  contract at first: require a saved/direct reference voice for cloning unless
  an upstream default-speaker prompt is explicitly validated.
- The UI should place S2 under voice cloning, not built-in TTS voices. It needs
  a Fish Audio provider label and route catalog entry or it will be hard to
  discover even after backend support exists.

## Proposed Architecture
- Create `crates/izwi-core/src/models/architectures/fish_s2/`.
- Suggested module split:
  - `mod.rs`: public `FishS2TtsModel`, generation structs, exports.
  - `config.rs`: deserialize and validate `config.json`, nested text/audio
    config, token ids, codebook dimensions, and model limits.
  - `weights.rs`: resolve sharded safetensors with `model.safetensors.index`.
  - `text.rs`: Qwen3-style slow decoder with S2 tensor prefixes and packed QKV.
  - `audio_decoder.rs`: fast AR codebook decoder with injection layers.
  - `tokenizer.rs`: ChatML prompt builder plus tokenizer/special token lookup.
  - `codec.rs`: Fish codec encoder/decoder backed by Candle tensors.
  - `voice.rs`: reference audio/text preparation and prompt-code construction.
  - `sampling.rs`: constrained semantic sampling and codebook sampling.
- Reuse existing Qwen3 primitives only after checking tensor names and shapes.
  The S2 slow path should share concepts with `qwen3/core.rs`, but copying a
  small, name-compatible decoder may be simpler than forcing a generic Qwen
  refactor through packed QKV and `text_model.*` prefixes.
- Generation flow for first pass:
  1. Decode base64 reference audio and resample to the codec's required sample
     rate after the codec config is confirmed.
  2. Encode reference audio with the Fish codec to 10-codebook RVQ tokens.
  3. Tokenize reference text and target text through the HF tokenizer/chat
     template.
  4. Build the multimodal prompt with semantic placeholders and codebook input
     tensors matching the upstream `DualARTransformer` contract.
  5. Prefill the slow transformer with text tokens and reference codebook
     embeddings.
  6. For each output frame, sample the semantic token only from
     `[semantic_begin_id, semantic_end_id)` plus EOS handling.
  7. Feed the semantic hidden state to the fast audio decoder and generate the
     remaining codebooks autoregressively.
  8. Stop on EOS or max frame budget, then decode generated codebook frames to
     waveform samples with the Fish codec.
  9. Return final-only `GenerationResult`; streaming wrapper can send one final
     chunk until incremental codec decode is validated.

## Hard Gates and Risks
- `codec.pth` is the largest implementation risk. Izwi currently has a minimal
  PyTorch zip helper for reading a single logical tensor, not a full codec
  state-dict loader. Before implementing model forward, inspect `codec.pth`
  format and either:
  - extend the Rust PyTorch archive/pickle loader enough to load the codec
    state dict directly; or
  - define a reproducible safetensors codec packaging path and make downloader
    support that artifact explicitly.
- Do not hardcode sample rate from memory. The current S2 config has
  `sample_rate: null`; derive sample rate/hop length from the codec artifact or
  upstream codec config before setting API metadata.
- Verify exact tensor names and transposition needs from
  `model.safetensors.index.json` before writing loaders. The current index
  confirms `text_model.*` and `audio_decoder.*` namespaces, but the loader
  should assert every required tensor.
- The model is BF16 and large. First pass should load with the repo's
  `DeviceProfile` dtype policy, with explicit fallback/error messages for
  unsupported BF16 devices. Expect memory requirements substantially above the
  11 GB artifact size.
- Fish inline control syntax is a product/API decision. Do not silently map
  OpenAI `speed` or `instructions` until verified with examples and tests.
- Long-form/chunked synthesis should be a second phase. The model has a
  `max_seq_len` of 4096 and an advertised token rate around 21.5/sec, so time
  budgets and request timeouts need S2-specific heuristics.

# LFM2.5 Long-Audio ASR Fix Implementation

## Goal
Fix long-audio transcription repetition for `LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF` while
preserving its ASR, TTS, and voice-to-voice capabilities and avoiding a large
short-audio performance regression.

## Plan
- [x] Reconfirm the implementation surface from current source, treating prior
  research notes as context rather than authority.
- [x] Thread ASR options through the LFM audio-chat ASR adapter so `max_tokens`
  is not hardcoded to `1024`.
- [x] Add long-form chunking for LFM audio-chat ASR using the shared
  `AsrLongFormConfig`, `plan_audio_chunks`, and `TranscriptAssembler`, while
  preserving the single-pass path for audio that fits one chunk.
- [x] Reuse the fixed ASR helper from voice-to-voice input transcription so V2V
  receives the same long-audio protection without changing TTS generation.
- [x] Add LFM ASR stop reasons, phrase-loop detection, and diagnostics so caps
  and recovery are observable.
- [x] Add focused unit tests for option propagation, chunk/budget policy, and
  phrase-loop trimming.
- [x] Run cargo tests/checks plus a real LFM long-audio smoke where practical.
- [x] Commit the fix in logical commits, excluding `tasks/*` notes.

## Review
- Implemented LFM audio-chat ASR long-form routing in the registry wrapper. The
  short/single-chunk path keeps the legacy `1024` default token cap, while
  multi-chunk ASR uses shared duration chunk planning, transcript assembly, and

- Threaded API `max_tokens` through the audio-chat ASR runtime shortcut for
  base64/bytes and streaming/non-streaming requests.

  leaving TTS/audio generation on the existing audio-chat path.
- Added LFM ASR stop-reason diagnostics and a cheap trailing phrase-loop trim
  that runs only when host tokens are already decoded.
- Verification passed:
  `cargo test -p izwi-core lfm_audio_asr`,
  `cargo test -p izwi-core lfm25_audio`, `cargo check -p izwi-core`, and
  `cargo build -p izwi-server -p izwi-cli`.
- Real smoke passed on
  `data/diarization-2.mp3` via patched debug server on port `18080`:
  `116.58449s` input, `6` chunks, transcript length `1946`, RTF `0.228`, all
  chunks stopped on `stop_token`, and all repetition-loop diagnostics were

- Logical commits:
  `58eb7002 Route LFM audio ASR through long-form chunks` and

# LFM2.5 Long-Audio ASR Repetition Investigation

## Goal
Analyze why `izwi transcribe ... --model LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF` repeats
"It's very expensive" on longer audio after the LFM2.5 updates, and produce a
low-regression fix plan. This task is research, analysis, and planning only; do
not edit product code in this pass.

## Plan
- [x] Review existing lessons and current task notes for relevant ASR/long-form
  constraints.
- [x] Trace the CLI transcription route into the LFM2.5 model path, including
  audio loading, chunking, prompting, decode limits, stop-token handling, and
  fallback/recovery behavior.
- [x] Inspect the recent LFM2.5 performance update surface for changes that
  could affect long-audio correctness, especially stop-check intervals,
  streaming/chunk boundaries, and device-side greedy decoding.
- [x] Reproduce or collect read-only runtime evidence on the supplied long audio
  where practical without changing product code.
- [x] Compare short-audio and long-audio behavior to isolate whether the loop is
  chunking, prompt carryover, token-budget, EOS detection, or decode-state
  related.
- [x] Propose the simplest fix that preserves most of the recent performance
  gains, with focused verification commands and acceptance criteria.
- [x] Add review findings and verification limits here before reporting back.

## Review
- Reproduced the supplied failure against the already-running desktop server,
  without starting another server:
  `izwi transcribe data/diarization-2.mp3 --model LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF --format json --output /private/tmp/lfm-long-transcribe.json`.
  The source MP3 is `116.540952s`. The response JSON contained only `text`; it
  was `4306` characters and contained `204` matches for `very expensive`, with
  no `asr_diagnostics` exposed by the endpoint for this model path.
- Root cause candidate 1: LFM2.5 Audio ASR bypasses the generic ASR long-form
  executor path. `/v1/audio/transcriptions` accepts `prompt` and `max_tokens`,
  but `RuntimeService` returns early for `variant.is_audio_chat()` and calls
  `asr_transcribe_audio_chat_bytes`, which decodes the whole file and calls
  `NativeAudioChatModel::transcribe`. That path does not use
  `NativeExecutor::asr_chunk_plan`, `TranscriptAssembler`, prompt replay, or
  the request max-token option.
- Root cause candidate 2: `NativeAudioChatModel::transcribe` hardcodes `1024`
  LFM ASR decode tokens. The repeated output shape is consistent with the model
  running to this cap after falling into a short phrase loop. User
  `--max-tokens` cannot mitigate the issue today because it is ignored on the
  audio-chat ASR shortcut.
- Root cause candidate 3: the recent performance path defers Metal/CUDA ASR
  token readback and stop/repetition checks. Current default stop-check interval
  is `92`, after commits `34f1ab71`, `470d6c3d`, `d1d2b158`, `f07f048a`, and
  `85d01382`. This is good for the short benchmark's host-sync cost, but it
  means stop tokens and repetition guards are observed only after speculative
  device forwards. The existing token repetition detector also only checks
  token spans `(24,3), (16,3), (12,3), (8,4), (6,5)`, so a short phrase like
  `It's very expensive` can evade it until the hard token cap.
- Recommended implementation plan:
  1. Add an LFM audio-chat ASR long-form branch before the current whole-file
     transcribe call. Use `AsrLongFormConfig::default`, `plan_audio_chunks`,
     and `TranscriptAssembler`; keep the current single-pass path for files
     that fit in one chunk to preserve short-audio benchmark performance.
  2. Thread `max_tokens` through the LFM audio-chat ASR runtime/registry methods
     instead of hardcoding `1024`. For chunked LFM ASR, use a duration-aware
     per-chunk cap, with a conservative floor for short clips and a ceiling
     well below `1024` for default 24-30s chunks.
  3. Add a cheap text-level trailing phrase-loop detector/trim for LFM ASR in
     addition to the existing token-pattern guard. This is low performance risk
     because it runs only when host tokens are already read back, and it reduces
     the blast radius if a chunk still falls into a phrase loop.
  4. Preserve the high `92` stop-check interval for successful short ASR unless
     verification shows it is still needed to lower it. Prefer chunking,
     duration budgets, and phrase-loop detection before globally increasing
     host readbacks.
  5. Expose diagnostics for LFM audio-chat ASR on transcription responses:
     chunk boundaries, per-chunk generated/max tokens, stop reason,
     `repetition_loop`, and whether `max_new_tokens` was reached.
- Verification plan for the implementation pass:
  - Unit tests for audio-chat ASR request option propagation, chunk planning
    threshold, duration-aware LFM token budgets, and short phrase-loop
    detection/trimming.
  - Real audio smoke on `data/diarization-2.mp3` asserting no repeated-phrase
    tail, no `generated_tokens == max_new_tokens` chunk unless explicitly
    marked/recovered, and non-empty coverage beyond the first sentence.
  - Short-audio regression benchmark with LFM2.5 ASR to confirm the single-pass
    path still meets the recent performance band and preserves generated-token
    invariants.
  - Optional interval sweep only after the above: compare default `92` versus
    `32`/dynamic checks on the failing long file and the short benchmark, and
    keep the high interval if correctness is solved without extra readbacks.

  `<=50-70 ms`.

Only one Izwi server may run at a time while benchmarking.

## Implementation Plan

  no behavior change; verify no more than +/-2% movement; commit.

  tensors on device and adding chunked/final host reads for EOS/text; verify ASR

  device-side where possible and reducing per-frame allocations; verify audio

- [ ] Phase 3: split and optimize detokenizer backbone/copy/ISTFT stages;
  verify waveform sanity and detokenizer target; commit.
- [ ] Phase 3b: optimize Conformer encoder low-risk pieces first
  (relative-position cache, reusable depthwise conv patterns), then deeper

- [ ] Stretch verification: run final TTS and ASR benchmark commands, record

  token/frame invariants, so the kernel complexity was restored out.

  LFM Conformer conv modules by folding each depthwise conv's affine scale/bias
  into precomputed per-channel weight/bias tensors, with the original

  dense mirror for the tiny codebook projections on this hardware.

  `KvCache::current_data()` for the depthformer single-token Metal fused
