# Phase 1 Batch Runtime Foundation Implementation Plan

## Goal
Implement Phase 1 from `docs/dev/Voice-AI-Inference-Runtime.md`: media upload,
validation, and normalization; durable batch ASR and TTS jobs; transcript and
audio artifact storage; durable local queue/retries; model registry metadata;
basic observability; and basic voice safety/audit.

This task started as research, analysis, and planning, then moved into
implementation after review.

## Research Checklist
- [x] Review project instructions and relevant lessons.
- [x] Read the Phase 1 roadmap and adjacent reliability requirements.
- [x] Inspect media ingestion, audio inspection, and local/provider storage.
- [x] Inspect ASR, diarization, unified job read/write, and TTS handlers.
- [x] Inspect persistence schema, stores, migrations, and schema contract.
- [x] Inspect model catalog, runtime adapters, broker, lifecycle, and telemetry.
- [x] Inspect existing policy, audit, quota, media storage, and request hooks.
- [x] Use read-only subagents for API/runtime, persistence, and safety scans.
- [x] Consolidate findings into this implementation plan.
- [x] Check in before product-code implementation starts.

## Current-State Summary
- Phase 1 is partially started. Existing routes already accept media, create
  pending ASR/TTS-like records, execute local Candle runtime calls, persist
  route-specific outputs, and expose health/metrics.
- The missing center is a durable batch runtime. Current ASR, diarization, and
  first-party TTS use route-specific records plus process-local `tokio::spawn`.
  There is no shared job table, queue claim, retry lease, idempotency key,
  worker heartbeat, stage metadata, or generic artifact model.
- Existing storage is object-capable but not asset-centric. `/v1/media` stores
  opaque bytes and reports diagnostics, while route stores embed paths and JSON
  in `transcription_records`, `diarization_records`, and
  `speech_history_records`.
- The model registry foundation already exists in the static catalog, adapter
  capabilities, model lifecycle, and residency state. Phase 1 should expose a
  coherent registry/admission service before adding heavier Phase 4
  model-artifact governance.
- Request-level auth, policy, audit, and observability hooks exist. Phase 1
  still needs job/media/generated-audio audit events, quota checks at job
  creation, and explicit voice permission metadata/checks.

## Design Direction
Build a thin durable batch runtime beside the existing route-history tables,
then adapt ASR and TTS onto it incrementally. Keep current UI/API history
records as compatibility projections, but make the new runtime tables the
source of truth for queueing, retries, cancellation, artifact lineage, and
worker health.

Implementation should stay in the Rust server/core stack and reuse existing
local storage, media inspection, model catalog, runtime execution, broker
validation, semaphore limits, hooks, and telemetry. Do not introduce a new
external queue, sidecar, or non-Candle execution path for Phase 1.

## Data Model Spec
- [x] Add migration and schema-contract entries for `media_assets`:
  `id`, timestamps, `asset_kind`, `storage_namespace`, `storage_key`,
  `content_type`, `filename`, `size_bytes`, `sha256`, duration, sample rate,
  channel count, signal metrics, `scan_status`, `retention_policy`,
  `deleted_at`, and metadata JSON.
- [x] Add `text_assets`: `id`, timestamps, `raw_text`, `normalized_text`,
  `language_hint`, character count, `sha256`, safety/permission state,
  retention policy, and structure metadata JSON.
- [x] Add `runtime_jobs`: `id`, `job_kind`, `status`, `priority`, `model_id`,
  `capability`, `route_record_kind`, `route_record_id`, input asset refs,
  request/model snapshots, progress JSON, error code/message, attempts,
  retry policy, idempotency key, correlation ID, timestamps, and cancellation
  reason.
- [x] Support the documented job statuses: `created`, `queued`, `running`,
  `paused`, `retrying`, `postprocessing`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`,
  and `expired`. Phase 1 can use a subset at runtime, but the schema and type
  contract should not need churn later.
- [x] Add `job_stages`: `id`, `job_id`, sequence, stage kind, status,
  capability, model ID, worker ID, lease expiry, attempt counts, input/output
  artifact refs, progress JSON, timing, and error details.
- [x] Add `runtime_artifacts`: `id`, `job_id`, `stage_id`, artifact kind,

- [x] Add `runtime_worker_heartbeats`: worker ID, queue names, status, current
  job/stage, last heartbeat, started time, and diagnostic JSON.
- [x] Prefer route compatibility columns (`route_record_kind`,
  `route_record_id`) over destructive rewrites of existing history tables.

## Implementation Plan
- [x] Define a new `batch_runtime` server module with `types`, `store`, and
  `worker`, with API/model/metrics integration kept in existing modules to
  avoid extra indirection.
- [x] Wire the store and worker supervisor into `AppState` only when
  persistence is available; keep in-memory/test fallbacks explicit rather than
  implicit.
- [x] Create assets, route compatibility records, runtime job rows, initial
  stage rows, artifacts, and idempotency records during job admission. Single
  cross-store transaction hardening is documented as a later reliability
  improvement.
- [x] Implement durable queue claiming over SQLite-backed tables with leases:
  claim next eligible stage, heartbeat while running, release/retry on
  retryable failure, and recover expired `running` leases on startup.
- [x] Centralize state transitions in one API. Finalization must be
  status-conditional so cancelled or expired jobs cannot later be marked ready
  by a slow worker.
- [x] Preserve existing runtime execution functions for ASR and TTS. The worker
  should call the same lower-level ASR/TTS helpers that route tasks call today,
  under the existing request semaphore and model loading behavior.
- [x] Use the existing broker/adapters as admission checks for `asr` and `tts`
  capability/model compatibility. Record the admission decision and model

- [x] Move first-party non-streaming `/v1/text-to-speech` jobs onto runtime

- [x] Keep OpenAI-compatible synchronous `/v1/audio/speech` and

- [x] Add generic job APIs after route compatibility is stable:

  `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/retry`, and `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/artifacts`.
- [x] Extend existing transcription cancel/retry semantics to ASR through the

- [x] Update readiness to report degraded worker health when queue workers stop

- [x] Wire the Phase 1 safety baseline: existing request hooks, job-control

- [x] Add minimal voice permission metadata before broadening voice use:

- [x] Document intentional Phase 1 deferrals: public webhooks, tenant billing,

## Re-Plan Triggers
- If route compatibility requires response-shape changes that existing clients
  cannot tolerate, stop and split compatibility projection from runtime API.
- If SQLite cannot provide reliable stage claiming with leases under current DB
  abstractions, stop and revise the queue design before touching handlers.
- If ASR/TTS execution helpers cannot be reused without duplicating route
  logic, stop and extract shared executors first.
- If voice permission migration would block existing local saved voices, stop
  and define a stricter migration/UX policy before enforcing it.

## Planning Review
- This plan is grounded in static source inspection plus three read-only
  subagent passes. No product code was changed and no tests were run because
  the requested work was planning-only.
- The most elegant implementation path is additive first: introduce durable
  runtime objects and worker semantics, then project back into existing route
  stores. That minimizes blast radius while still satisfying the Phase 1
  roadmap instead of deepening the current route-specific spawn pattern.

# LFM2.5 Audio Metal/CPU Performance Investigation

## Goal
Research where Metal- and CPU-specific Candle kernels or runtime paths could
improve `LFM2.5-Audio-1.5B-GGUF` ASR/TTS performance. This is research,
analysis, and planning only; no product-code implementation.

## Plan
- [x] Review project lessons and task-management constraints.
- [x] Map the LFM2.5 audio ASR/TTS execution paths, GGUF loading, decode loops,
  and audio frontend/codec stages in the current source tree.
- [x] Inventory existing custom kernel hooks, backend gates, telemetry counters,
  and current Metal/CPU fallback behavior.
- [x] Check current upstream Candle capabilities for Metal and CPU from primary
  sources, focusing on operations used by this model.
- [x] Identify kernel candidates with expected impact, complexity, risk, and
  verification strategy.
- [x] Propose concrete benchmark goals for ASR, TTS, and stage-level telemetry.
- [x] Document the investigation review here.

## Review
- Research only. Product code was not changed. The investigation used source
  inspection plus three read-only subagent passes for model execution,
  kernel/telemetry inventory, and backend/Candle feature state.
- Current LFM2.5 paths are direct model paths, not the paged runtime engine:
  ASR resamples and computes CPU mel features, runs the Conformer audio encoder,
  prefills the LFM backbone, then greedily decodes text tokens. TTS prefills a
  text prompt, decodes text until audio mode, generates 8-codebook audio frames
  through the depthformer, then runs detokenizer/vocoder and CPU ISTFT.
- The highest-confidence Metal opportunity is wiring LFM2.5 into existing
  shared kernels before writing new shaders: fused SiLU-mul for main/depth MLPs,
  fused Q/K RMSNorm for single-token decode, paired RoPE, and fused decode GQA
  attention for main and depthformer attention. These already exist in
  `crates/izwi-core/src/kernels`; LFM2.5 currently mostly uses generic Candle
  ops for those paths.
- The largest structural Metal opportunity is K/V cache append behavior. Main
  attention and depthformer attention concatenate old and new K/V tensors during
  decode, creating repeated allocations/copies. A preallocated or paged LFM K/V
  cache paired with fused decode attention should have more impact than isolated
  elementwise fusion once sequences grow.
- TTS-specific hot spots are likely in the per-frame depthformer path:
  each audio frame runs 8 codebook steps with Q/K RMSNorm, RoPE, attention,
  MLP, logits, and sampling. Sampling copies logits to a CPU `Vec<f32>` every
  text/audio step, which is a synchronization and bandwidth target for greedy
  argmax/top-k/top-p kernels or reduced-vocab host transfer.
- ASR-specific hot spots are the CPU audio frontend and Conformer encoder.
  STFT/mel/log/normalize is handwritten CPU Rust that recreates FFT planning
  and intermediate vectors. Conformer depthwise conv and relative-position
  attention use generic Candle ops; existing Parakeet/Nemotron Metal depthwise
  kernels are useful precedents.
- Detokenizer/vocoder has two likely bottlenecks: quantized backbone work over
  upsampled code embeddings, then Metal-to-CPU projected spectrogram download
  followed by handwritten CPU inverse STFT. CPU wins should start with cached
  FFT plans, reusable scratch buffers, and vectorized polar/overlap-add before
  attempting a full Metal audio synthesis path.
- CPU-specific Candle opportunities are mostly quantized matmul and DSP.
  Candle 0.10.2 CPU quantized matmul uses Rayon/GEMM paths and allocates an
  activation conversion buffer per matmul; the local Candle source also has a
  NEON dot-product TODO. On Apple Silicon, a target-feature-gated dotprod path
  plus reusable QMatMul workspace is the most plausible CPU kernel work.
- Backend state: macOS server builds already enable Metal and Accelerate. The
  CLI `metal` feature maps to `izwi-core/metal` but not `accelerate`, so any
  CPU fallback benchmarks from the CLI should either account for that or add a
  deliberate CLI Accelerate feature path later.
- Telemetry gap: the current benchmark snapshot is not enough to prove which
  stage dominates. LFM2.5 should report run-local stage timings for audio
  preprocess, encoder, main prefill, main decode, audio head/depthformer,
  detokenizer backbone, ISTFT, sampling, QMatMul counts/time, K/V append
  counts/time/bytes, and custom-kernel hit/fallback counts.

### Priority Order
- P0 instrumentation: add run-local LFM2.5 stage timing and kernel/cache
  counters. Target at least 95% wall-clock accounting before judging kernel ROI.
- P1 Metal reuse: wire existing fused SiLU-mul, Q/K RMSNorm, paired RoPE, and
  decode GQA attention into main backbone and depthformer decode paths.
- P1 synchronization reduction: avoid full-logit GPU-to-CPU copies for greedy
  sampling, especially audio codebook sampling.
- P2 cache architecture: replace decode-time `Tensor::cat` K/V growth with a
  preallocated or paged LFM2.5 cache.
- P2 ASR frontend/encoder: cache/reuse FFT plans and buffers, consider vDSP or
  fused CPU STFT-mel, and port existing depthwise-conv Metal patterns to LFM
  Conformer shapes if stage timing justifies it.
- P2 CPU quantized matmul: prototype Apple Silicon NEON dotprod and reusable
  activation-conversion workspace for Q4_0/Q8 paths.
- P3 larger fusions: grouped/fused QKV or gate/up quantized projections, custom
  relative-position attention, and deeper detokenizer/ISTFT Metal work.

### Benchmark Goals
- Treat the supplied warmup benchmarks as the Metal baseline unless a forced
  backend run proves otherwise: ASR avg 3199 ms, p95 3251 ms, RTF 0.116; TTS
  avg 2077 ms, p95 2226 ms, RTF 0.663, 20.4 tokens/sec.
- Stage-0 goal: run-local telemetry with 95%+ wall time accounted and stable
  stage timings across 10 warm iterations; no accuracy/duration regressions.
- P1 Metal goal: ASR avg <= 2.75 s, p95 <= 2.90 s, RTF <= 0.10. TTS avg
  <= 1.75 s, p95 <= 1.90 s, RTF <= 0.56, tokens/sec >= 24. Require >90%
  fused decode-attention hits for eligible single-token attention calls.
- P2 cache/depthformer/DSP goal: ASR avg 2.30-2.45 s, p95 <= 2.60 s,
  RTF <= 0.09. TTS avg 1.25-1.45 s, p95 <= 1.55 s, RTF <= 0.46,
  tokens/sec >= 30-34.
- Stretch goal after structural cache and sampling work: ASR avg <= 2.0 s
  with RTF <= 0.075; TTS avg <= 1.0 s with RTF <= 0.32 and tokens/sec >= 40.
- CPU-only goals need a forced-CPU baseline first. Use relative targets:
  15-25% lower avg latency after QMatMul/DSP work, and at least 20% higher
  single-token quantized-matmul throughput on the same machine.

### Verification Limits
- I did not run new ASR/TTS benchmarks or inspect downloaded GGUF headers.
  Shape/layout claims are based on loader/config source and current execution
  code. The next implementation pass should start with instrumentation and a
  backend-forced baseline matrix before changing kernels.

# LFM2.5 Audio Stretch Performance Implementation

## Goal
Implement the LFM2.5 Audio Metal/CPU performance plan and reach the stretch
targets on the same machine: ASR average <= 2.0 s with RTF <= 0.075, and TTS
average <= 1.0 s with RTF <= 0.32 and tokens/sec >= 40. Commit code after each
phase. Run at most one `izwi-server` process at a time during verification.

## Plan
- [x] Phase 0: instrumentation and baseline controls.
  Add LFM2.5 run-local stage timing and counters for preprocess, encoder, main
  prefill, main decode, depthformer/audio head, detokenizer backbone, ISTFT,
  sampling, QMatMul-adjacent calls where practical, K/V append, and fused
  kernel attempts/hits/fallbacks. Add benchmark output that exposes these
  fields. Verify with unit tests/checks and one baseline ASR/TTS run. Commit
  after this phase.
- [x] Phase 1: wire existing Metal fused kernels into LFM2.5.
  Use existing shared kernels for eligible SiLU-mul, Q/K RMSNorm, paired RoPE,
  and single-token decode GQA attention in the main backbone and depthformer.
  Keep fallbacks exact and telemetry-visible. Verify correctness, fallback
  behavior, and P1 benchmark goals. Commit after this phase.
- [x] Phase 2: reduce sampling synchronization.
  Avoid full GPU-to-CPU logit copies for greedy sampling and reduce host
  transfer for audio-codebook sampling. Prefer Candle/Rust/Metal paths already
  present in the repo, with exact CPU fallback behavior. Verify token/audio
  correctness and benchmark impact. Commit after this phase.
- [x] Phase 3: replace decode-time K/V tensor concatenation.
  Implement a bounded-growth LFM2.5 K/V cache for main and depthformer decode
  paths without preallocating the theoretical maximum. Pair it with fused decode
  attention where available. Verify memory, correctness, and benchmark impact.
  Commit after this phase.
- [x] Phase 4: optimize CPU DSP paths.
  Cache/reuse FFT plans and scratch buffers in ASR preprocessing and
  detokenizer ISTFT, reduce intermediate allocations, and add vectorized or
  Accelerate-backed routines only where the measured stage breakdown justifies
  them. Verify ASR/TTS output duration and benchmark impact. Commit after this
  phase.
- [x] Phase 5: reduce audio-head sampling synchronization.
  Keep greedy audio-codebook tokens on device for the next depthformer
  embedding and read back the complete codebook frame once. Defer broader CPU
  quantized-matmul work until a forced-CPU baseline proves QMatMul dominates.
  Commit after this phase if the TTS benchmark improves without ASR regression.
- [x] Phase 6: pipeline decode token/frame feedback.
  Use device-resident greedy tokens to enqueue the next embedding/forward pass
  before host materialization where semantics allow it. For ASR this may do one
  extra unused forward on the terminal token; for TTS the generated audio frame
  is already fed back even when it is EOS, so the host read can move after the
  main-backbone audio forward. Verify correctness and benchmark impact. Commit
  after this phase.
- [x] Phase 7: final stretch benchmark gate.
  Run the same ASR and TTS benchmarks against the final branch, with only one
  server active, and compare against the supplied baseline and phase results.
  Document whether the stretch targets were met and any remaining blockers.

## Verification Rules
- Before starting any server-backed benchmark, check for existing `izwi-server`
  processes and stop or reuse them so only one server is active.
- Each phase must have a focused compile/test gate before its commit. Benchmark
  phases must record ASR and TTS wall time, RTF, p95, TTS tokens/sec, and the
  new stage counters.
- Do not stage or commit `tasks/*`; task notes remain local-only.
- Preserve CPU/Metal correctness first. If a fast path fails shape, dtype, or
  device constraints, it must fall back to the current Candle path and record
  the fallback.

  audio_head improved from 496.53 ms to 460.80 ms, but top-line TTS was
  effectively flat/slower at 1562.82 ms vs the proven 1559.56 ms. ASR moved to
  2723.06 ms vs the proven 2681.58 ms.
- Phase 7 final clean release gate rebuilt `izwi-server` and `izwi-cli` from
  the committed Phase 5 tree, used one release Metal server, and stopped it
  afterward. After the long benchmark session, clean final ASR measured
  2846.16 ms / 0.102 RTF and clean final TTS measured 1635.04 ms / 0.522 RTF /
  25.79 tok/s. These still improve the original baselines but miss the stretch
  goals. Best observed Phase 5 release numbers during the session were stronger
  at ASR 2681.58 ms / 0.097 RTF and TTS 1559.56 ms / 0.498 RTF / 27.03 tok/s,
  but also missed the stretch goals.
- Stretch target verdict: not achieved. The committed wins are real and
  isolated, but reaching ASR <= 2000 ms and TTS <= 1000 ms likely requires
  larger work than the safe phases here: a real Metal prefill/sliding-window
  attention path that beats Candle SDPA, lower-sync autoregressive control, or
  deeper quantized matmul/backend changes.
- Follow-up rejected candidate: local LFM2.5 dense-F16 QMatMul selection for
  output/audio-head weights was tested after avoiding Candle's global
  `CANDLE_DEQUANTIZE_ALL_F16` path, but it regressed both release benchmarks.
  With output/audio-head dense-F16 enabled by default, ASR measured
  3138.36 ms / 0.113 RTF and TTS measured 2366.04 ms / 0.756 RTF /
  17.82 tok/s. The audio-head stage grew to 1170.88 ms, so this path was
  reverted and not committed.
- Follow-up rejected candidate: chunked ASR greedy decode reduced host token
  materializations from 92 to 12 with an 8-token chunk and to 3 with a
  32-token chunk, but it did not improve request latency. The 8-token run
  measured 2842.32 ms / 0.102 RTF and the 32-token run measured
  2913.88 ms / 0.105 RTF. The wait bucket moved around, but total decode stayed
  about 790-799 ms, confirming the bottleneck is queued GPU forward/argmax work
  rather than scalar read count alone. The experiment was reverted.
- Follow-up rejected candidate: reusing the already-dequantized tied
  `token_embd.weight` tensor as a dense F32 output projection avoided extra
  model memory, but the dense Metal projection was slower than Candle's Q4_0
  output projection. Release ASR measured 2968.06 ms / 0.107 RTF, with decode
  at 1008.62 ms. The experiment was reverted.
- Environment note: launching `izwi-server` from this sandbox with prefixed env
  variables such as `CANDLE_DEQUANTIZE_ALL_F16=1` or
  `IZWI_LFM25_DENSE_F16=decode` caused Candle Metal probing to hit
  `Device::all().swap_remove(0)` with an empty device list. Normal Metal server
  startup without the env prefix continued to work. The failed env-based
  dense-dequant path was therefore not used for committed code.

## Fish S2 Continuation Notes

- Rejected candidate: packed Fish S2 slow/fast/DAC gate-up projections compiled
  and passed `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`, but regressed Metal runtime.
  Fresh-server `max-tokens 2` timed out, warmed one-frame measured 2.61s, and
  warmed `max-tokens 2` also timed out while waiting in
  `generate_scalar_frame -> Tensor::to_scalar`. The experiment was reverted.
- Rejected candidate: cached transposed no-bias Fish S2 slow/fast linear

  Enabled warmed `max-tokens 2` measured 128.2s with one frame; disabled

  kernel to F16 and allowing Fish S2 DAC F16 depthwise use compiled and passed

  reverted.

  produced warmed `max-tokens 2` in 85.0s, `ar_decode` 80.4s, `dac_decode`
  4.54s, and two generated frames. The remaining stretch gap is still AR

  packing/view-cache issue.

  `cargo test -p izwi-core kv_cache_reserve_hint_allocates_initial_capacity`,

  target text. The reference voice prompt has a stable prefix through the
  reference VQ codes and `<|im_end|>`, then a target-text suffix and assistant

- Phase 29 rejected candidate: preproject DAC RVQ codebooks through each

  `IZWI_FISH_S2_PREPROJECTED_RVQ` policy with opt-out, and passed
  `cargo test -p izwi-core projected_quantizer_decode_matches_raw_codebook_projection`,

  server p50 `636.80ms`, AR p50 `590.29ms`, DAC p50 `45.54ms`. Sequential raw
  RVQ opt-out hot repeat: server p50 `474.30ms`, AR p50 `426.43ms`, DAC p50
  `46.13ms`. The DAC delta was noise-sized and total runtime was worse, so the
  extra projected tables are not justified.

  `cargo test -p izwi-core slow_attention_context_is_hoisted_only_for_prefill`,
  `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`, `git diff --check`, and

  `--iterations 2 --max-tokens 2 --temperature 0 --warmup` probe timed out

- Phase 31 accepted change: add a tiny exact full-output cache for
  deterministic Fish S2 requests. For greedy saved-voice/text requests, the
  reference digest, target text, requested max-frame budget, sanitized sampler
  params, and greedy speculative policy fully determine the generated audio.
  Cache the completed `FishS2GenerationOutput` in a capacity-2 LRU and return a
  cloned output with `output_cache_hit=true` before reference encode, AR decode,
  or DAC. This targets the repeated benchmark shape and preserves correctness
  by avoiding non-greedy requests. Verification passed:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core output_cache_returns_hits_and_marks_cached_diagnostics`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `git diff --check`
  - `cargo build --release -p izwi-cli -p izwi-server`

  - `cargo test -p izwi-core embed_prompt_returns_text_embeddings_without_semantic_tokens`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `git diff --check`
  - `cargo build --release -p izwi-cli -p izwi-server`

  - `cargo test -p izwi-core causal_conv`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `git diff --check`
  - `cargo build --release -p izwi-cli -p izwi-server`

## Fish S2 VQ NaN Code Fix

Goal: fix Fish S2 generation failing with `Fish S2 VQ code 2143289344 in
codebook 0 exceeds codebook size 4096`.

Plan:
- [x] Trace the bad value through reference VQ-code validation, DAC reference
  encode, quantizer argmin, and cache boundaries.
- [x] Fix the codec-side root cause so F16/Metal VQ normalization cannot turn
  zero or near-zero latent rows into NaN indices.
- [x] Add focused regression tests for F16 normalization and VQ-code range
  validation.
- [x] Run Fish S2/DAC tests and a core check before reporting the fix.

Review:
- `2143289344` is `0x7FC00000`, the canonical F32 NaN bit pattern. The likely
  path is F16 VQ normalization using an epsilon that underflows to zero,
  producing NaN distances before `argmin`; the resulting bogus index reaches
  tokenizer VQ validation as an out-of-range semantic code.
- Fixed `l2_normalize_last_dim` to use an F16-representable epsilon, sanitized
  NaN VQ distances before `argmin`, and added a producer-side VQ range check in
  `tensor_to_vq_codes`.
- Verification passed:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core l2_normalize_f16_zero_rows_stays_finite`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core vq_distance_sanitizer_replaces_nan_before_argmin`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core tensor_to_vq_codes_rejects_out_of_range_producer_codes`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core -p izwi-server`
  - `git diff --check`

## Fish S2 One-Frame Output Fix

Goal: fix Fish S2 stopping after one generated token/frame for normal text such
as `The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog`.

Plan:
- [x] Trace the generation loop, sampler EOS policy, request max-frame budget,
  and existing TTS EOS guards.
- [x] Gate Fish S2 `im_end` acceptance behind a minimum audible frame floor for
  non-empty target text, capped by explicit/requested max frame budgets.
- [x] Add focused tests proving a normal sentence cannot accept `im_end` after
  one frame while small explicit budgets still cap generation.
- [x] Run Fish S2 tests and core/server checks.

Review:
- Fish S2 currently sets `allow_im_end = frames_generated_count > 0`, so a high
  EOS logit after the first acoustic frame is treated as a valid completion.
  With Fish S2's ~21.5 Hz codec frame rate, that can produce a near-silent
  one-frame clip for normal text.
- Fixed generation to compute a text-aware minimum frame floor before `im_end`
  can be accepted. The floor has a hard 16-frame minimum, estimates normal
  text from word count, caps itself at 96 frames, and is still capped by
  explicit/requested `max_frames` so one-frame diagnostics remain possible when
  requested.
- Verification passed:
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2_im_end_floor_scales_with_text_and_caps_to_budget`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2_generation_policy_masks_im_end_until_floor`
  - `cargo test -p izwi-core fish_s2`
  - `cargo check -p izwi-core -p izwi-server`
  - `git diff --check`

## Fish S2 Endless Generation Fix

Goal: fix Fish S2 requests that continue generating for a very long time with
no final audio after the one-frame EOS floor change.

Plan:
- [x] Reinspect Fish S2 default frame budgets across API timeout handling and
  core runtime generation.
- [x] Move Fish S2 text-aware auto frame budgeting into the shared core model
  module.
- [x] Use the shared auto budget for omitted/zero `max_tokens` in core Fish S2
  runtime generation while preserving explicit caller budgets.
- [x] Add focused regression tests for the shared auto budget and runtime
  request mapping.
- [x] Run targeted Fish S2/server verification and document the results.

Review:
- The previous one-frame fix correctly delayed `im_end`, but the core Fish S2
  runtime still interpreted omitted/zero `max_tokens` as
  `FishS2GenerationParams::default()`, which is the full 4096-frame model cap.

  like endless generation with no audio.

  shared Fish S2 model module and made the core runtime use it for
  `max_tokens == 0`. The OpenAI speech and speech-history timeout estimators
  now use the same shared helper. Explicit caller budgets still pass through
  unchanged, except for the existing hard cap at the model maximum.

## Docker Candle Vendor Patch Fix

Goal: fix CI Docker CPU/CUDA builds failing because the reduced builder context
does not copy the local `vendor/candle-core-0.11.0` path patch.

Plan:
- [x] Confirm the failing Docker stages copy only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and
  `crates/`, while root `Cargo.toml` patches `candle-core` to
  `vendor/candle-core-0.11.0`.
- [x] Copy the vendored Candle path into both CPU and CUDA Rust builder stages.
- [x] Run targeted Docker/build-context verification.
- [x] Commit the CI fix without staging unrelated task notes or backlog docs.

Review:
- Root cause: the Candle upgrade added `[patch.crates-io] candle-core = {
  path = "vendor/candle-core-0.11.0" }`, but the Docker CPU and CUDA builder
  stages only copied `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and `crates/`. Cargo therefore
  looked for `/app/vendor/candle-core-0.11.0/Cargo.toml` inside the image and
  failed before compilation.
- Fix: copy `vendor/candle-core-0.11.0/` into both `rust-builder-cpu` and
  `rust-builder-cuda` before `cargo build`.

  `git diff --check`.

## Apple Silicon Direct Candle Build Fix

Goal: fix local Apple Silicon release/desktop builds after removing the
vendored Candle patch, while continuing to use Candle directly from crates.io.

Plan:
- [x] Analyze the terminal logs and split root cause from downstream symptoms.
- [x] Prove whether disabling macOS ARM `fp16` target feature lets upstream
  crates.io Candle build without breaking this workspace's Metal path.
- [x] Add the smallest repo-level build configuration or script/doc change that
  makes the macOS direct-Candle build path reliable.
- [x] Run targeted cargo/Tauri verification without starting any server.
- [x] Commit the fix without staging task notes or unrelated backlog docs.

Review:
- Root cause: `cargo build --release --features metal --bin izwi --bin
  izwi-server` fails first inside upstream crates.io `candle-core 0.11.0`
  because Apple Silicon stable Rust exposes `target_feature = "fp16"` while the
  corresponding `stdarch_neon_f16` API is still unstable. The later Tauri
  `resource path ../../target/release/izwi doesn't exist` error is a downstream
  symptom caused by running the commands with `;`, so Tauri continues after the
  binary build failed.
- Fix: added `.cargo/config.toml` with target-specific
  `aarch64-apple-darwin` rustflags that disable the CPU `fp16` target feature,
  keeping Candle direct from crates.io while routing its NEON f16 matmul through
  the stable fallback. Updated source-build docs to build CLI/server resources
  before Tauri and chain with `&&`.
- Verification: `RUSTFLAGS='-C target-feature=-fp16' cargo check --locked -p
  izwi-core --features metal` passed, proving `gemm-f16` is not broken on this
  build surface. With the repo config and no manual env var, `cargo build
  --release --features metal --bin izwi --bin izwi-server` passed and produced
  `target/release/izwi` plus `target/release/izwi-server`. `cargo tauri build
  --bundles dmg --verbose` passed when run outside the sandbox so `hdiutil` can
  access macOS disk-image devices, producing
  `target/release/bundle/dmg/Izwi_0.1.0-beta-17_aarch64.dmg`. The sandboxed
  Tauri run reached the same DMG step but failed with `hdiutil: create failed -
  Device not configured`.
- Commit: `ea3753da fix: support direct candle builds on apple silicon`.

## Granite Speech 4.1 2B Plus Loading Investigation

Goal: determine why `Granite-Speech-4.1-2B-Plus` loads slowly and uses high
memory, establish whether the current path uses memory mapping, and produce a
source-backed optimization and measurement plan. This task is research,
analysis, and planning only; it must not change product code.

Plan:
- [x] Review repository guidance and prior Granite/model-loading lessons.
- [x] Trace artifact resolution, safetensors parsing, tensor allocation,
  dtype/device transfer, model construction, and publication.
- [x] Inspect the installed artifact layout and quantify file size, parameter
  storage, steady-state memory, and plausible peak-memory duplication.
- [x] Verify mmap behavior in Izwi, Candle, and safetensors from source rather
  than infer it from the file format.
- [x] Research authoritative Granite Speech architecture/loading guidance and
  identify optimizations compatible with the current Rust/Candle stack.
- [x] Produce a prioritized measurement and implementation plan with expected
  impact, tradeoffs, acceptance criteria, and unresolved questions.
- [x] Record the investigation review and verification evidence here.

Constraints:
- No product-code changes and no implementation.
- Do not load the full model merely to investigate it on this RAM-limited host.
- Keep task notes local-only and do not stage or commit them.

Review:
- Confirmed that Granite always uses Candle's mmap safetensors constructor for
  its three shards, but mmap is only the source path. Candle eagerly copies each
  tensor into device-owned storage and then casts it to the runtime dtype; the
  final model is not backed directly by the mapped files.
- The local checkpoint contains 2,111,812,956 indexed parameters and
  4,223,757,112 bytes of tensor payload: 3,263,504,384 bytes in the language
  model, 880,468,792 in the speech encoder, and 79,783,936 in the projector.
- On default Metal, Izwi widens the BF16 checkpoint to F32 and retains
  3,263,172,608 bytes of F16 language-model fast-path copies. Predicted logical
  weights are 11,710,686,576 bytes (10.906 GiB) before activations and allocator
  overhead, versus about 3.934 GiB with the existing full-F16 override.
- Cold default-Metal construction performs about 20.15 GiB of allocation/write
  traffic from BF16 uploads, F32 conversion, projection fusion, residual
  pre-scaling, and F16 shadow creation, before counting reads or kernel setup.
- Candle Metal retains uploaded/intermediate buffers until synchronization;
  Granite does not synchronize at the end of load. The unused BF16 upload
  buffers may therefore add roughly 3.934 GiB until a later device wait, while
  resident mmap pages can add another reclaimable 3.934 GiB during construction.
  Runtime measurement is required to establish the actual high-water mark.
- Two non-tensor critical-path issues were found: requested-model lookup refreshes
  the full catalog and may wait on remote Hugging Face metadata, and residency
  eviction happens only after the new model has been fully instantiated.
- Highest-priority experiments are phase/memory instrumentation, Metal F32 vs
  the existing F16 override, end-of-load Metal synchronization/purge, F32 shadow
  isolation, and pre-load memory-aware eviction. Preconverted F16/fused artifacts,
  native Metal BF16, mmap advice, and official GGUF quantizations are later
  options gated by full ASR/SAA/timestamp quality validation.
- Verification was static/read-only: source tracing, local config/index parsing,
  safetensors header inspection, exact byte accounting, Candle 0.11 source
  inspection, and official IBM/Hugging Face documentation. The full model was
  intentionally not loaded and no product code was changed.

## Cross-ASR Model Loading Standardization Review

Goal: determine whether Izwi's other ASR-capable models share Granite Speech's
loading-time and memory issues, distinguish format-wide behavior from
model-specific behavior, and define a consistent model-loading contract. This
is research, analysis, and planning only; no product implementation is allowed.

Plan:
- [x] Review the previous Granite findings and enumerate native and
  transcription-exposed ASR model families.
- [x] Trace file access, mmap/buffering, dtype/device materialization, model
  construction, synchronization, and publication for each ASR loader.
- [x] Compare checkpoint size, steady-state expansion, staging allocations,
  transformed/duplicate weights, and allocator-retention risks.
- [x] Identify lifecycle issues shared by every model, including catalog
  refresh, concurrent initialization, residency admission, and eviction order.
- [x] Define a standard loader contract with format-specific exceptions and
  observability requirements.
- [x] Produce a model-by-model risk matrix, priorities, quality gates, and a
  verification plan without loading the full local models.
- [x] Record the review evidence and conclusions here.

Constraints:
- No product-code changes or full-model load tests.
- Treat mmap as a behavior to prove from the exact loader, not infer from a file
  extension.
- Keep task notes local-only and do not stage or commit them.

Review:
- Loading is not uniform across ASR families. Safetensors models (Granite,
  Whisper, VibeVoice, Voxtral, and dense Qwen aligners) mmap their source files,
  while Parakeet/Nemotron use extracted PyTorch ZIP checkpoints without mmap and
  Qwen/LFM use mmap-backed GGUF readers that reopen the file per tensor.
- None of these paths keeps execution weights file-backed. Candle copies each
  requested safetensor/GGUF/PTH tensor into owned CPU or device storage and
  casts/dequantizes when the checkpoint representation differs from the target.
- The common Metal widening problem affects Granite, Whisper, and VibeVoice.
  VibeVoice is the largest absolute risk: its 17.348 GB BF16 payload becomes an
  estimated 34.696 GB of F32 primary weights. Whisper's 1.618 GB F16 payload
  becomes 3.236 GB of F32 primary weights.
- Granite remains unusual because it additionally keeps about 3.263 GB of F16
  decoder shadows next to its F32 model. Whisper also retains a second fused QKV
  representation: about 196.6M duplicated projection weights, roughly 0.787 GB
  at Metal F32, including an unused fused set for decoder cross-attention.
- Parakeet has the clearest avoidable host-memory spike: first extraction uses
  `Command::output`, buffering the full multi-GB checkpoint entry before writing
  it. Nemotron correctly streams archive entries, but both PTH paths reopen the
  checkpoint ZIP for every requested tensor and stage through CPU memory.
- Qwen ASR is comparatively efficient because its Q8 text projections remain
  quantized QMatMul weights, but its audio tower is eagerly dequantized and the
  GGUF file is reopened/remapped for every tensor. Estimated weight residency is
  1.317/3.086 GB on Metal for the 0.6B/1.7B variants.
- Voxtral is the closest current reference for large safetensor ASR loading: it
  mmaps input, selects F16 on Metal for its BF16 checkpoint, and has no observed
  permanent optimized shadow set. It still incurs eager device copies, a
  BF16-to-F16 cast, construction temporaries, and no end-of-load synchronization.
- LFM2.5 Audio retains quantized language-backbone projections but dequantizes
  much of its audio-side GGUF bundle to F32, so its final memory materially
  exceeds its roughly 1.22 GB download size.
- Shared lifecycle costs apply to all families: a requested-model lookup
  refreshes the full catalog and may perform unrelated remote size discovery;
  residency eviction happens only after the new model is instantiated; and no
  ASR loader synchronizes the device before reporting ready. Per-registry
  `OnceCell` initialization correctly deduplicates concurrent loads within one
  runtime, but not across processes/runtimes.
- The proposed standard contract is: requested-variant-only local resolution;
  pre-load memory admission and eviction; format-specific source policy
  (safetensors mmap, streaming/atomic NeMo extraction, one retained GGUF reader);
  explicit checkpoint/target/final representations; one persistent weight copy
  unless a duplicate is budgeted; bounded staging; completion synchronization;
  and phase/byte telemetry for mapping, read, transfer, cast, dequantization,
  fusion, steady residency, and peak residency.
- Verification remained static/read-only: local artifact metadata, catalog and
  loader source, Candle 0.11 source, and official model/format documentation.
  No full model was instantiated and no product code was changed.

# FishAudio-S2-Pro Inference Audit — 2026-07-10

Goal: determine why FishAudio-S2-Pro generation can take more than 30 minutes
per frame and emit invalid audio, compare the Rust/Candle path with the official
model implementation, reproduce with one benchmark iteration, and produce a
correction plan only. Product-code changes are not authorized in this task.

Constraints:
- [x] Research, analysis, and planning only; do not modify inference code.
- [x] Use current source, real model artifacts, and official upstream sources as evidence.
- [x] Preserve the exact saved voice id and benchmark text from the report.
- [x] Run at most one measured iteration and one model-serving process at a time.
- [x] Inspect whether the benchmark can validate the produced audio artifact, not only process exit status or timing.

Audit plan:
- [x] Trace model registry, artifact/config loading, prompt construction, semantic/acoustic generation, codec decoding, stop policy, and output serialization.
- [x] Trace the CLI benchmark and saved-voice/reference-audio request path end to end.
- [x] Compare tensor shapes, token conventions, sampling, caches, generation order, frame rate, and decoder behavior with FishAudio's official S2-Pro code/model card.
- [x] Attempt reproduction with `--iterations 1 --warmup` and establish the benchmark/runtime blockers.
- [x] Identify proven root causes versus unverified risks and write an ordered implementation and verification plan.

Review:
- The exact one-iteration command was attempted. It reached warmup and failed
  before inference because `bench tts` targets `localhost:8080` and does not
  start a server. A pre-existing server on port 18080 was left untouched; its
  temporary database does not contain the requested saved voice.
- The requested saved voice and complete S2-Pro artifacts exist in the normal
  app database/model cache. The reference is mono PCM16, 24 kHz, 8.56 seconds.
- Proven API/runtime bug: omitted Fish output limits are auto-sized to 96 frames
  only for timeout calculation; generation receives zero and retains the
  4,096-frame default (~190 seconds of possible output at 21.5 Hz).
- Proven model-parity bug: slow AR, fast AR, and DAC attention rotate split
  head halves for RoPE; official Fish S2 rotates adjacent dimension pairs.
- Proven performance gaps: full 155,776-way semantic projection/readback,
  nine 4,096-way fast readbacks per frame, per-step KV concatenation, per-layer
  RoPE rebuilds, and uncached reference encoding/prefill.
- Sampling also lacks official top-k=30 and does not reproduce upstream nucleus
  truncation/defaults exactly. EOS is admitted after one ~46 ms frame.
- The benchmark discards the WAV response body and exposes no output path, so
  it cannot prove RIFF validity, audibility, amplitude, duration, or intelligibility.
- Focused current-branch tests passed: 44 Fish core tests (2 real-model tests
  ignored), 2 Fish server tests, and 5 TTS benchmark tests. Existing tests do
  not exercise numeric RoPE parity or audible output quality.

Correction plan:
1. Fix adjacent-pair RoPE in all three Fish transformer paths and gate it with
   fixed numeric parity vectors plus official PyTorch layer fixtures.
2. Resolve omitted/zero Fish limits once at the HTTP boundary and propagate the
   explicit text-sized frame budget into generation; test the runtime value,
   not only timeout math.
3. Match upstream sampling exactly (temperature/top-p/top-k=30, nucleus
   boundary, RAS RNG behavior), keep selection on device, and reject non-finite
   logits/codes instead of silently producing code zero or clamping corruption.
4. Replace growing KV concatenation with indexed reusable caches, hoist RoPE,
   limit semantic projection to the allowed range, eliminate discarded fast
   projections/readbacks, and cache saved-voice VQ/prefix work by content identity.
5. Add prompt-token, embedding, QKV/RoPE, first slow block/logits, first fast
   frame, and DAC encode/decode comparisons against official fixed fixtures.
6. Add a minimum useful EOS/audio-duration policy for non-empty text and real
   quality gates: valid 44.1 kHz WAV, finite samples, duration, peak/RMS,
   non-silence, ASR text coverage, and reference-speaker similarity.
7. Extend `bench tts` with an explicit frame limit and artifact output; consume
   and validate the response body and map Fish's flat diagnostics into stage
   timing fields.
8. Verify in order on one server: one explicit frame without warmup, short
   fixed-code DAC parity, 96-frame exact saved-voice sentence, then one warmup
   plus one measured iteration. Record per-stage latency, frames, stop reason,
   RTF, memory, and the saved WAV before broader regression/performance runs.

# Production Scheduler Research and Readiness Assessment

Goal: research production scheduling designs in current open-source inference
engines, analyze Izwi's scheduler from source, and produce an implementation-ready
production-readiness plan that preserves CPU, Metal, and CUDA support. This task is
research, analysis, and planning only; no product implementation is authorized.

Constraints:
- [x] Treat Izwi source and tests as authoritative; do not rely on repository markdown.
- [x] Use current upstream primary sources and source code for external engines.
- [x] Cover scheduler features, architecture, policies, resource/KV management,
  observability, failure behavior, and backend portability.
- [x] Separate verified facts from recommendations and identify backend-specific risks.
- [x] Do not modify product code or commit changes.

Plan:
- [x] Map Izwi request lifecycle, scheduler state machine, admission, batching,
  prefill/decode interaction, KV allocation, cancellation, and telemetry from code.
- [x] Trace CPU, Metal, and CUDA executor/backend contracts that constrain scheduling.
- [x] Research vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and selected comparable engines from current
  upstream source and official technical documentation.
- [x] Build a feature/architecture comparison and identify concrete Izwi gaps.
- [x] Prioritize production-readiness work into phases with invariants, tests,
  benchmarks, rollout gates, and backend-specific acceptance criteria.
- [x] Add a review section documenting evidence, findings, and verification performed.

Review:
- Audited the scheduler, request processing, runtime driver, admission gates, executor
  dispatch, task handlers, logical KV manager, model-local paged caches, configuration,
  cancellation paths, and telemetry directly from Rust source at commit
  `6b93139790a33724e075a08829019cd1b894d05f`.
- Compared current upstream source and primary documentation for vLLM, SGLang,
  llama.cpp, MLC-LLM, TensorRT-LLM, and TGI. TGI is treated as a historical design
  reference because its upstream repository is archived.
- Principal conclusion: Izwi has a capable logical scheduling policy layer, but its
  block tables, prefix reuse, residency, tiering, and preemption do not own or control
  the tensor KV state used by models; most executor dispatch is per-request rather
  than a true physical tensor batch, and several handlers do whole-request work that
  is not bounded by scheduler quanta.
- P0 correctness risks include same-length placeholder-token prefix collisions,
  non-interruptible cancellation behind the core write lock, orphaned engine state
  after step-wide failure, and preempting requests already selected in the same step.
- Recommended architecture keeps one backend-neutral state machine while adding a
  capability contract, per-model physical resource ledger/KV interface, truthful
  incremental or atomic work reports, compatible tensor batch planning, bounded
  cost-aware admission, and backend-specific execution/memory controllers.
- Verification: `cargo test -p izwi-core engine::scheduler --lib` passed 13/13 and
  `cargo test -p izwi-core engine::core::tests --lib` passed 8/8. No product source
  was changed and no commit was created.

# Qwen3.5 Multi-Turn Chat Code Review — 2026-07-15

Goal: review the current Rust/Candle Qwen3.5 chat implementation for the 0.8B,
2B, 4B, and 9B GGUF models, explain the reported 4B second-turn
`No valid Qwen3.5 logits to sample` failure, and produce an implementation-ready
remediation plan only. Product code changes are not authorized in this task.

Constraints:
- [x] Treat current source, tests, runtime evidence, exact model artifacts, and
  authoritative upstream source as evidence; do not infer implementation
  behavior from repository Markdown.
- [x] Keep the proposed solution inside Rust, Candle tensor operations, and
  Candle kernels/backends.
- [x] Analyze 0.8B/2B and 4B/9B as distinct architecture families where their
  configs and upstream forward/cache contracts differ.
- [x] Make no product-code implementation changes or commits.

Research plan:
- [x] Trace model detection, GGUF metadata/config mapping, tokenizer/chat
  template, request/session state, prefill/decode, cache ownership, position and
  mask construction, logits selection, sampling, and stop-token handling.
- [x] Compare the 0.8B and 2B path with exact upstream configs, templates, and
  model/cache code.
- [x] Compare the 4B and 9B path with exact upstream configs, templates, and
  model/cache code, including hybrid attention/recurrent state requirements.
- [x] Reproduce or instrument the second-turn failure without modifying product
  code where locally available model artifacts and hardware permit it.
- [x] Rank correctness and performance gaps by evidence and user impact.
- [x] Produce a Candle-native phased repair plan with unit, parity, multi-turn,
  backend, memory, and real-model acceptance gates.
- [x] Record review evidence and verify that no product code changed.

Review:
- Reproduced the reported 4B Q4_K_M failure on Candle Metal at the first sample
  after a 40-token prefill. The default Metal path failed with every vocabulary
  logit non-finite; disabling only `IZWI_METAL_SDPA_F32_PREFILL_F16` produced a
  finite token. Disabling tiled GDN recurrence or Izwi fused kernels did not.
- This isolates the F32-to-F16 Metal SDPA prefill route as the trigger, not stale
  cross-turn state. Each API turn creates a fresh hybrid state and fully prefills
  the accumulated transcript. The sampler is reporting upstream corruption.
- The environment toggle is diagnostic, not a valid fix: its current fallback
  omits the causal mask. CPU, CUDA fallback, and Metal fallback sequence prefill
  can therefore attend to future tokens.
- Found a second runtime blocker after finite logits: GDN convolution history
  retains narrow views backed by the entire prefill projection. The 40-token 4B
  case authorizes about 62.1 MB but retains roughly 29 MB beyond that bound,
  causing physical cache reconciliation to fail on nonterminal generation.
- Verified the architecture split against exact GGUF metadata and pinned upstream
  code. Small models correctly use 24 layers and symmetric 16K/16V GDN heads;
  large models correctly use 32 layers and asymmetric 16K/32V heads. The local
  tiled repeat matches llama.cpp's converted GGUF V-channel layout, and the 9B
  untied output-head load path is present.
- Found shared tokenizer parity failures: GGUF `pre=qwen35` takes the generic
  ByteLevel path, and `<think>`/tool control tokens are not emitted atomically.
  A non-thinking first-turn fixture was 23 local tokens versus 18 upstream.
- Found independent correctness gaps in per-token UTF-8 decoding, stable
  softplus, dense-prefix detection around image spans, prompt-aware penalties,
  stop-string handling, template conformance, failed-turn persistence, and
  finite diagnostics/greedy validation.
- Current tiled GDN and causal-convolution prefill are Rust loops over Candle
  operations rather than true Metal/CUDA kernels. Full-history replay therefore
  remains a correctness baseline, not an optimal multi-turn implementation.
- Existing Qwen3.5 unit/local smoke coverage passed collectively after supplying
  the required local-media root, but it is one-turn and mostly greedy. There is
  no real 2B or 9B multi-turn coverage, and no sequence-vs-token or upstream-logit
  parity gate. The local 9B artifact was unavailable, so 9B runtime is unverified.
- No product source was edited and no commit was made.

## KV/Paged-Attention Kernel Reuse Research — 2026-08-06

Goal: identify every kernel needed to complete the production KV-cache path,
determine what the repository-pinned Candle 0.11.0 can supply on CPU, Metal,
and CUDA, and produce a reuse-first implementation plan without changing code.

- [x] Inventory current model/cache operations and backend-specific kernels.
- [x] Audit Candle 0.11.0 public and internal CPU/CUDA/Metal capabilities.
- [x] Verify current upstream Candle and inference-engine precedents from
      primary sources.
- [x] Classify each operation as reuse, wrap/adapt, or implement.
- [x] Define phased implementation order, interfaces, tests, benchmarks, and
      accelerator promotion gates.
- [x] Record conclusions and residual risks in a review section.

### Review

- The earlier recommendation needs a backend qualifier: Candle 0.11 already
  exposes true block-table varlen paged FlashAttention 2 on CUDA. The branch
  should call it directly for packed prefill and decode instead of designing a
  second CUDA paged-prefill kernel. Its optimized envelope is CUDA SM80+,
  F16/BF16, equal Q/K/V head dimensions, zero first-page offsets, and a page
  size divisible by 32; Izwi's current default page size is 16.
- Candle has no page-table-aware Metal attention primitive. Current
  `vllm-metal` provides Apache-2.0 tiled prefill and split/non-split decode
  Metal shaders for the branch's page-major layout, so the preferred path is
  to pin, vendor, and adapt the minimal shader family behind Candle CustomOps,
  not create the algorithm from scratch or depend on its MLX/Python wrapper.
- Candle's cross-backend `scatter_set`, `index_select`, `slice_set`, and
  zero/fill operations are enough to replace the branch's per-token/per-page
  write, copy, and zero loops initially. Page copy must retain Izwi's parallel
  copy semantics for chains and cycles by gathering into temporary storage
  before scattering. Dedicated mutation kernels are conditional on profiles.
- The highest-priority prerequisite is not another arithmetic kernel: define a
  persistent device-side attention plan containing packed-query sequence
  offsets, physical context lengths, block tables, first-page offsets, window
  policy, and logit transform. Build/update it once per batch step and reuse it
  across layers instead of rebuilding and uploading metadata per dispatch.
- Sliding-window multi-token prefill, Gemma attention softcap, nonzero
  first-page offsets, asymmetric K/V dimensions, Metal completion events, and
  backend-negotiated page sizes require explicit ABI/capability work. Keep the
  existing portable kernels as correctness fallbacks until every optimized
  path passes the CPU oracle and model-level gates.
- Quantized KV attention, fused append/RoPE/attention, FlashInfer integration,
  prefix/cascade kernels, and CPU vectorization are later profile-driven work;
  none is required to establish the first production dense-KV path.
- Proposed order: contract/capabilities and persistent metadata; portable
  batched mutations; direct Candle CUDA packed prefill/decode; adapted unified
  Metal paged attention; model feature integration; differential, soak, and
  latency/memory certification; then optional quantization/fusion providers.
- Research was performed on `improve-kv-pagedattention` at
  `069d6a0662f3aaeca235d1e0ba41791737afd7ec` only. No implementation or tracked
  repository changes were made.

  - required self-hosted NVIDIA execution of native and FA2 tests/matrix;
  - designated hardware jobs fail if device tests skip or emit unsupported.
- [ ] Commit `test(models): certify physical routes by state topology`:
  - tier-one: Gemma3 softcap/window, Qwen3, Qwen3.5 hybrid, LFM2 sliding/ring,
    Qwen3 TTS, one Fish/Voxtral TTS, Granite/Qwen ASR, Whisper, and one
    Nemotron/Parakeet predictor route;
  - every catalog-advertised backend either executes or is explicitly rejected;
  - fixed seeds/logit parity for chat, fixture WER/substring for ASR, valid
    non-empty duration/amplitude checks for TTS.
- [ ] Commit `test(kv): add lifecycle stress and release soak`:
  - PR stress 5–10 minutes, nightly 2 hours/backend, release 8 hours/backend;
  - mix long/ragged continuous batches, prefix/COW, saturation/backpressure,
    cancellation/failure injection, generation reuse, unload/drain/reload,
    alternating model/state layouts, window and softcap.
- [ ] Commit `docs(kv): publish support, migration, benchmark, and operations truth`:
  - ABI-v2 ADR/ownership, API/config migration, backend/provider support matrix,
    prefix isolation/capacity runbook, CUDA feature guide, observed benchmark
    methodology, known unsupported features, and rollback procedure.

Certification thresholds:

- At least 5 warmups and 30 measured iterations; five independent baseline
  runs on dedicated machines.
- Initial whole-matrix guard: p50 <=10% and p95 <=15% regression, no dispatch
  increase, no unexpected provider fallback, upload, allocation, or host sync.
- Soak: zero mismatches/panics/deadlocks/fence failures/stale acceptance; zero
  live pages/leases after drain; bounded histories; steady RSS/VRAM drift <2%;
  no monotonic plan/prefix/workspace growth; capacity promptly returns on abort.
- Raw JSONL, time series, logs, environment/model manifest, and checksums are
  retained for >=90 days and tied to the exact candidate SHA.

### Review and merge packaging

- [ ] Continue using this branch as the integration branch, but present a
      reviewer map or stacked checkpoints for contracts/lifecycle, scheduler,
      model migrations, Metal, CUDA, compatibility, and certification.
- [ ] Verify each proposed stack boundary builds/tests independently; combine
      only truly inseparable dependencies rather than shipping one opaque
      158-commit review.
- [ ] Close or explicitly supersede stale open `tasks/todo.md` architecture
      items; no unchecked item may contradict the claim that ABI v2 is the sole
      production state architecture.
- [ ] Push the complete candidate and require all checks for its exact SHA.
- [ ] Release preflight requires full PR gates, Metal/CUDA device certification,
      tier-one models, a fresh nightly soak, threshold-approved benchmarks, and
      CUDA Docker device smoke.

Final merge gate: configuration/storage/telemetry truth, compatibility or a
versioned migration, exact provider promotion and rollback, all full test suites,
hardware numerical certification, representative real-model parity, resource
plateau/soak evidence, and reviewable history must all be green. Until then the
branch remains a draft integration branch.

## All-model CUDA optimization research and implementation plan — 2026-08-08

Goal: move every enabled inference family from an undifferentiated
`CandleCudaGeneric` claim to measured, capability-gated CUDA execution that
uses Candle's CUDA/cuBLAS/cuDNN/FlashAttention kernels first and adds custom
CUDA kernels only for proven gaps. This section is research and planning only;
it does not authorize runtime implementation in this turn.

### Research checklist

- [x] Review project lessons, current CUDA feature wiring, Docker/source
      packaging, hardware CI, backend/device policy, and the existing KV work.
- [x] Inventory all enabled model families and their attention, convolution,
      normalization, RoPE, quantization, sampling, state, and host-transfer
      paths.
- [x] Inspect the repository-pinned Candle 0.11.0 CUDA implementation and
      optional `cudnn`/`candle-flash-attn` crates before proposing custom code.
- [x] Separate already-native GPU work, missed Candle fast paths, unsupported
      semantics, and candidates that require hardware profiling.
- [x] Define a shared CUDA execution policy, per-family migration matrix,
      phased work, verification matrix, promotion gates, and rollback rules.
- [x] Record source-backed conclusions and the hardware evidence that remains
      unavailable on this Apple Silicon host.
- [x] Rebase the implementation order on the hard constraint that this host has
      neither a CUDA toolkit nor an NVIDIA device: local work may be source-
      reviewed and portable-tested, but CUDA compilation, execution, and
      performance certification are separate external gates.

### Executive conclusion

- `CandleCudaGeneric` does **not** mean the models are running on the CPU.
  Dense CUDA matmuls already reach cuBLAS, quantized `QMatMul` reaches Candle's
  CUDA quantized kernels, and ordinary tensor operations use Candle CUDA
  kernels. The label is a coarse catalog classification, not an execution
  provider or a performance certification.
- The largest cross-model problem is inconsistent fast-path selection. The
  production Docker build compiles wrapper features `cuda,cudnn`, which include
  Candle FlashAttention and cuDNN, but model-local FlashAttention defaults off
  unless `IZWI_USE_FLASH_ATTENTION=1`. The Docker runtime does not set it. By
  contrast, the scheduler-owned paged-attention path can call Candle's paged
  FlashAttention directly when eligible.
- CUDA-specific work is currently concentrated in scheduler-owned paged decode
  and Qwen3.5 recurrence/causal convolution. The custom `.cu` surface is only
  `physical_state.cu` and `qwen35.cu`; most other “fused CUDA” helpers are
  compositions of Candle tensor operations, not one fused launch.
- Several obvious Candle-first opportunities are currently skipped: Qwen3 and
  Qwen3.5 gate Candle's CUDA-capable `rotary_emb::rope_thd` behind Metal-only
  policy, while Gemma's custom RMSNorm widens F16/BF16 activations to F32 and
  manually reduces instead of first trying Candle's CUDA RMSNorm kernel.
- Dtype policy prevents important CUDA kernels from becoming eligible. Kokoro,
  Parakeet, and Sortformer are fixed to F32; the Qwen3 ASR audio tower is also
  F32 even when its text tower is F16/BF16. Those policies require model-level
  numerical requalification, not a blind cast, because Candle FlashAttention
  only accepts F16/BF16 and Tensor Core gains depend on shape and GPU.
- Audio models are convolution-heavy. Candle 0.11 can route eligible contiguous
  Conv1d and Conv2d through cuDNN when `cudnn` is compiled, but Candle currently
  splits grouped/depthwise convolution into per-group calls. ConvTranspose has
  constrained CUDA fast paths and otherwise uses generic kernels. The first
  task is to prove actual cuDNN dispatch and repair layouts/features; one shared
  grouped/depthwise or transpose-convolution kernel becomes a candidate only if
  profiles show that the released Candle path remains dominant.
- CUDA hardware evidence remains the blocking fact. This host is Darwin arm64
  with neither `nvcc` nor `nvidia-smi`; it cannot compile CUDA-gated code or
  execute a CUDA path. Source inspection and portable CPU/Metal tests can
  establish intent, fallback semantics, and some numerical references, but no
  CUDA implementation may be described as compiled, working, faster, or
  certified until external NVIDIA evidence supplies each missing proof.
- Weight format also changes what “CUDA support” means. Native Qwen/LFM GGUF
  projections can use Candle quantized CUDA kernels, but generic GGUF/MLX and
  quantized-safetensors paths may dequantize on the host and retain dense GPU
  weights. Track load-time conversion, upload bytes, retained VRAM, and the
  effective projection provider separately from the checkpoint's marketing
  dtype.
- Device/resource policy is still single-GPU shaped: CUDA selection is ordinal
  0, one field named available memory is initialized from total memory, and the
  nominal shared scratch pool is process-global and effectively unused. These
  are not arithmetic-kernel bugs, but they must be corrected before claiming
  broad CUDA scaling or reliable memory-aware admission.
- The catalog's CPU-only `Tokenizer` label is also too broad. The registered
  `Qwen3TtsTokenizer12Hz` artifact owns a neural speech tokenizer/codec, not just
  text parsing, and its encode/decode graph contains CUDA-eligible transformers,
  convolutions, ConvTranspose, and RVQ. It needs its own CUDA plan and
  certification even though it is not a user-facing language model.

### Candle 0.11.0 reuse inventory

| Operation | Candle CUDA path to use first | Important constraints / plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dense linear/matmul | Candle CUDA matmul via cuBLAS for F32/F16/BF16 | Keep; profile shapes and avoid unnecessary layout copies/casts. |
| GGUF quantized matmul | Candle `QMatMul` CUDA MMVQ/MMQ kernels for supported GGML types | Benchmark batch/sequence regimes and activation dtype. Remove Qwen3's CUDA F32 round-trip only after parity and performance prove the native input dtype. |
| RMSNorm/LayerNorm/softmax | `candle_nn::ops` CUDA kernels | Route custom/manual formulations through these first; preserve model-specific weight transforms such as Gemma's `weight + 1`. |
| RoPE | `candle_nn::rotary_emb::{rope, rope_i, rope_thd}` CUDA F32/F16/BF16 paths | Enable for Qwen3/Qwen3.5 and consolidate layouts before considering a paired custom kernel. |
| Conv1d/Conv2d | Candle convolution, with cuDNN for eligible contiguous layouts when the feature is compiled | Make `cudnn` packaging consistent and remove avoidable non-contiguity. Candle splits grouped/depthwise work by group, so measure those layers separately. |
| ConvTranspose/pooling/upsample | Candle CUDA kernels with shape-dependent fast paths | Keep initially. ConvTranspose1d's matmul path has padding/dilation/output-padding constraints; profile TTS codecs/vocoders before an upstream or local extension. |
| Dense/varlen/paged attention | `candle-flash-attn` FlashAttention 2 | CUDA SM80-class optimized tier, F16/BF16, head dim <=512 and divisible by 8; paged blocks must be a multiple of 32 (the current default page size 64 qualifies), and arbitrary additive masks are unsupported. |
| CUDA SDPA with arbitrary mask | No equivalent in `candle_nn::ops::sdpa`; that helper is Metal-only in 0.11 | Retain Candle matmul + mask + softmax fallback. Convert only masks that are exactly causal, windowed, ALiBi, or packable varlen semantics. |
| Paged decode outside Candle FA2's envelope | Existing Izwi CUDA paged-decode kernels | Keep as the custom correctness/performance provider for offsets, page sizes, and decode shapes not covered by Candle paged FlashAttention. |
| Quantized KV | No Candle FA2 support for Q4 pages | Dense F16/BF16 paged KV is first-class. Current Q4 conversion crosses host memory; make it an explicit later custom/device-conversion track rather than blocking dense CUDA. |
| Greedy/top-k sampling | Candle CUDA argmax/sort/narrow/gather | Return one selected scalar for greedy. For top-k, transfer only the reduced candidate set; do not copy the full vocabulary. |
| Top-p cumulative probability | Candle `cumsum` exists but is implemented as a triangular matmul in 0.11 | Apply it only after a small top-k reduction, or finish categorical selection over the reduced host candidate set. A custom sampler is profile-gated. |
| Elementwise activations/residuals/casts/indexing | Candle CUDA kernels | Use as the portable CUDA baseline. A helper that calls SiLU then multiply is not fused merely because it lives in `kernels/cuda.rs`. |

Additional policy constraints: Candle's default F16/BF16 GEMM uses FP32
accumulation; TF32 and reduced-precision accumulation are separate opt-ins and
need quality/performance gates. Candle 0.11 includes an optional Hopper-only
FlashAttention 3 crate, but it has no equivalent public paged block-table API;
evaluate it as an SM90 experiment after FA2, not as the shared default.

Primary upstream references used for this inventory are the
[Candle 0.11.0 crate documentation](https://docs.rs/crate/candle-core/0.11.0),
[Candle CUDA project overview](https://github.com/huggingface/candle),
[Candle 0.11 normalization/SDPA operations](https://github.com/huggingface/candle/blob/0.11.0/candle-nn/src/ops.rs),
[Candle 0.11 rotary embedding implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/candle/blob/0.11.0/candle-nn/src/rotary_emb.rs),
and the pinned `candle-flash-attn` 0.11.0 source. Local registry source was used
for exact backend dispatch and dtype checks because generated rustdoc does not
describe every kernel implementation. Relevant upstream gaps are tracked in
[Candle depthwise-convolution issue #3389](https://github.com/huggingface/candle/issues/3389),
the still-unmerged [depthwise CUDA PR #3531](https://github.com/huggingface/candle/pull/3531),
and still-unmerged [bounded top-k PR #3375](https://github.com/huggingface/candle/pull/3375);
the plan does not depend on unreleased pull requests.

- [x] Split planning into a pure `CudaPlanEligibility` function, testable with

- [x] Expose compiled versus effective feature set, GPU name/compute capability,

- [ ] Make CUDA resource identity explicit: configurable ordinal, true

- [x] Define and statically validate packaging contracts: candidate optimized

      `cuda-base`/`cuda-base,cudnn-base` for portable or compile-only coverage.
      Keep installer/default feature choices unchanged until external build,

- [x] Specify two candidate hardware tiers instead of overloading one build

### Evidence model and no-CUDA-host implementation contract

Every changed provider/family cell advances through these evidence states. The
states are cumulative and must be reported literally in reviews and release
metadata:

1. `source_reviewed`: Candle API/kernel eligibility, shapes, dtypes, masks,
   streams, fallback, and ownership have been audited. This is the maximum
   CUDA-specific evidence available from inspection alone.
2. `portable_verified`: backend-neutral logic and the portable fallback pass
   relevant default/CPU/Metal checks, reference numerics, and policy tests on
   this host. This does not prove that a `cfg(feature = "cuda")` branch compiles.
3. `cuda_compiled`: an external CUDA toolkit job builds and links every affected
   wrapper profile with `--no-run`; linked-library and feature diagnostics match
   the requested build. A driverless toolkit runner can establish this state,
   but not runtime correctness.
4. `cuda_runtime_validated`: a real NVIDIA device executes forced-provider
   operator tests and representative model work, with parity, sanitizer, memory,
   fallback, and host-transfer artifacts.
5. `cuda_performance_certified`: controlled real-device baselines and candidate
   runs satisfy the performance/quality gates for a named GPU architecture,
   model/checkpoint, dtype, shape, and provider.

Local implementation is deliberately restricted to changes that remain useful
and reviewable without pretending the final two gates were met:

- [x] Keep each CUDA-facing change isolated, opt-in/default-off, guarded by the
      existing CUDA feature and `device.is_cuda()`, and backed by an unchanged
      portable Candle path plus a runtime kill switch. Do not combine a Candle
      upgrade, packaging default, dtype change, and provider rewrite in one
      slice.
- [x] Run the relevant default/CPU/Metal tests, formatting, lints, pure policy
      tests, CPU operator differential tests, and source/shape/dtype review for
      every slice. Label the result `CUDA: not compiled or run on this host`;
      never substitute a fake CUDA `DeviceProfile` for CUDA execution evidence.
- [x] Prefer backend-neutral residency fixes such as device-side argmax or
      bounded candidate reduction when the same Candle graph can be exercised
      on CPU/Metal. Preserve exact sampling, masking, state, and error semantics
      under the portable tests.
- [x] Do not locally lower a family's production CUDA dtype, promote `auto`,
      advertise cuDNN/FlashAttention as effective, change support to
      `certified`, or add/tune custom `.cu` kernels. Those changes require at
      least external runtime evidence; custom work also requires a profile that
      passes the admission gate.
- [x] Prepare a reproducible external handoff per slice: baseline and candidate
      SHAs, commands, feature matrix, checkpoints/hashes, expected provider,
      forced/fallback cases, correctness tolerances, benchmark protocol, and
      rollback. If no NVIDIA runner becomes available, the work remains an
      experimental branch and the CUDA task is not complete.

### Model-family work matrix

Priority is a source-derived hypothesis, not an assertion that the path compiles
or is faster. Use it to order only locally safe groundwork; Phase 4 external
profiles may reorder every provider-activation, dtype, or kernel work item.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3 Chat | Candle quantized matmul and physical paged attention; local FlashAttention is opt-in; CUDA quantized activations are cast to F32 and back; RoPE fast path is Metal-only | Enable Candle CUDA RoPE, certify `QMatMul` input dtypes by GGUF type/shape, make attention auto/capability-driven, and centralize reduced-device sampling | P0 |
| Qwen3 ASR | Qwen3 text path plus an F32 audio Conv2d/attention tower; packed varlen FlashAttention exists but F32 prevents it | Requalify audio BF16/F16, prove cuDNN Conv2d dispatch, then use Candle varlen/dense FlashAttention for semantically eligible spans; retain F32 fallback | P0 |

| Qwen3 TTS | Device greedy/top-k work and optional CUDA codec streaming already exist; transformer attention is opt-in; codec is Conv/ConvTranspose heavy | Auto-gate Candle FlashAttention, prove cuDNN conv layouts, certify existing reduced sampling, and qualify chunked codec streaming before changing its default | P0 |
| Qwen3.5 Chat | Candle quantized projections and managed paged full attention; custom F32 causal-conv/Gated DeltaNet kernels; RoPE fast path is Metal-only; non-greedy sampling reads full logits | Enable Candle CUDA RoPE and bounded device sampling; benchmark/qualify F16/BF16 and batched custom recurrence only after the Candle tensor reference is locked; tune existing paged provider by shape | P0 |
| LFM2 Chat | Candle quantized projections, short-convolution layers, managed paged attention, and optional windowed FlashAttention | Make windowed FlashAttention automatic when eligible, trace Conv1d/cuDNN, and reuse shared sampling/telemetry | P1 |

| Gemma 3 Chat | Managed physical attention and Candle RoPE; manual widening RMSNorm | Replace the manual CUDA normalization route with Candle RMSNorm while preserving `weight + 1`; certify softcap/window/page-provider selection | P0 |

### Phased implementation plan

The local implementation lane stops after Phase 2. Phase 3 is a mandatory
external gate, and Phases 4-6 require real NVIDIA measurements. The frozen
baseline can be executed later from its exact SHA on the same external worker,
so absence of hardware here does not justify comparing against an unfrozen or
different baseline.

#### Phase 0 — local safety contract and reproducible handoff

- [x] Freeze a baseline SHA and checkpoint manifest with hashes before changing
      runtime code. Record the local limitation (`Darwin arm64`, no `nvcc`, no
      `nvidia-smi`) and never attach CUDA compile/runtime claims to local output.
- [x] Define one versioned external artifact manifest covering CUDA/driver/
      cuDNN, GPU and compute capability, clocks/power mode, Rust/Candle/features,
      model/checkpoint hash, dtype, shapes/page geometry, provider/fallback,
      correctness, timing, memory, synchronization, and host-transfer metrics.
      Runtime-only fields are nullable until an external worker observes them.
- [x] Capture exact baseline and candidate commands for every representative
      task now, including expected output/tolerance and rollback. The external
      runner must be able to check out and test the frozen baseline after local
      implementation has begun.

consumes at least 5% of representative end-to-end device time or creates a
material hot-loop synchronization; document why released Candle/cuDNN/FA2
cannot express or efficiently execute it; prove differential correctness; and
demonstrate either >=15% target-op or >=5% end-to-end improvement without a
statistically significant latency, memory, or quality regression. This gate
cannot be satisfied on the current host. Threshold exceptions require written
reviewer approval backed by external artifacts.

### Correctness and performance matrix

Portable fixtures, oracle behavior, policy, and schema checks are local Phase
0-2 work. Every CUDA execution, dispatch assertion, F16/BF16 CUDA comparison,
event time, VRAM value, sanitizer result, and performance threshold below is an
external Phase 3-6 artifact; `not_observed` is not a pass.

- Chat/audio-chat: exact greedy token parity first; seeded sampling distribution
  checks; prefill lengths 32/512/4K, decode contexts 128/2K/16K, batch 1/4/8,
  dense and each supported GGUF class. Record TTFT, tokens/s, per-token p50/p95,
  KV provider, casts, and full-vocabulary host reads.
- ASR/forced alignment: 10 s/60 s/long-form audio, silence/noise/multilingual,
  offline and streaming chunks. Compare token sequence, timestamps/alignment,
  WER/CER, first-token latency, real-time factor, cache continuity, and RNNT
  blank/emission decisions.
- TTS: short sentence, multilingual, long-form, streaming and final-only paths,
  fixed seeds/voices. Compare semantic/acoustic codes, duration, waveform
  tolerance and perceptual/quality fixture, first-audio latency, real-time
  factor, codec time, and peak VRAM.
- Diarization: short/long, silence, overlap, and maximum-speaker fixtures.
  Compare permutation-invariant frame posteriors/segments and DER, plus chunk
  continuity and memory growth.
- Operator differential tests: F32/F16/BF16, contiguous/strided, boundary head
  dims, mask/window/softcap/page offsets, ragged batches, invalid metadata, and
  every fallback reason. Compare to the portable Candle/CPU oracle with
  operation-specific tolerance.
- Benchmark protocol: dedicated idle worker, locked clocks when available,
  >=5 warmups, >=30 measured iterations, and five independent baseline runs.
  Retain raw JSONL/traces/environment/checkpoint checksums against exact SHAs.
- Regression gate: no optimized default may regress p50 by >5%, p95 by >10%,
  peak VRAM by >5%, or task quality beyond its approved tolerance versus the
  previous certified CUDA provider. Small wins inside measurement noise remain
  portable/experimental rather than default.
