## CUDA/KV follow-up performance assessment (2026-08-08)

- [x] Re-audit the landed CUDA default, kernel routing, host-transfer removal,
      long-context policy, and physical KV changes from current source.
- [x] Identify the remaining shared CUDA and KV-cache bottlenecks, avoiding
      duplicate recommendations for already-landed work.
- [x] Rank the work by expected latency/throughput/VRAM benefit and implementation
      risk, with explicit NVIDIA-only acceptance measurements.
- [x] Document the review outcome and the recommended logical commit sequence.

### Review

- The most urgent follow-up is paged-arena materialization: CUDA model-maximum
  contexts currently resolve paged groups as `Fixed`, and the accelerator arena
  allocates full K and V tensors for every layer at load. Add admission-barrier
  slab growth before increasing kernel scope.
- The largest decode-loop overhead visible from source is metadata: native CUDA
  paged decode rebuilds host block tables and synchronously clones the complete
  metadata vector to the device in every custom-op call. Lower one batch plan
  once, retain it on device, and update only changed rows/pages.
- Candle FlashAttention remains the preferred paged prefill provider inside its
  supported envelope. The fallback currently expands each causal prefill query
  into paged decode metadata; add a native CUDA varlen/windowed fallback only
  after measuring unsupported Flash cells.
- Kernel work should next qualify Candle/cuDNN primitives, then fill shared CUDA
  gaps (QK RMSNorm, paired RoPE, short convolution). Several CUDA helpers named
  fused still issue multiple Candle operations, while CUDA block fusion is
  explicitly disabled.
- Later work is GPU-specific provider/page/partition tuning, device-side
  stochastic sampling, quantized KV, CUDA graph capture, and broader continuous
  batching. Each requires real NVIDIA numerical, latency, and VRAM evidence.

# Research Portable CPU/Metal Context Auto-Fit — 2026-08-12

Goal: design a model- and machine-general context-selection policy analogous
to llama.cpp `--fit`, using shorter fitted contexts on CPU/Metal while
preserving current CUDA context semantics.

Research checklist:
- [x] Verify current llama.cpp CPU/Metal fit inputs, context provenance, safety
      margin, minimum context, and failure/recovery behavior from source.
- [x] Trace Izwi context provenance and every managed/invocation state consumer.
- [x] Define a deterministic shared-memory fit equation covering weights, state,
      invocation multiplicity, compute workspace, and operator budgets.
- [x] Specify explicit-vs-auto context behavior, diagnostics, fallback order,
      logical commits, and cross-backend verification.

Review:
- llama.cpp's useful contract is provenance-aware fitting: only unset context is
  reduced, the default floor is 4,096 tokens, and a 1 GiB target margin is kept.
  Its CPU path uses total RAM, while Metal uses recommended working-set
  headroom; its current UMA accounting and final-candidate validation remain
  heuristic, so those details should not be copied unchanged.
- Izwi already resolves a shorter configured context for CPU/Metal and native
  context for CUDA. The immediate defect is that non-CUDA managed-state loading
  discards that logical reach and eagerly allocates the full 1,024-page arena.
  The complete portable fix must both honor the resolved context everywhere and
  replace the provenance-losing numeric default with per-model Auto fitting.
- The proposed fitter uses one shared CPU/Metal memory envelope, exact model,
  state, invocation, concurrency, and execution-workspace plans, a configurable
  safety reserve, and an exact page-aware candidate search. Explicit context is
  validated but never silently reduced; CUDA bypasses the portable fitter.
- Capacity elasticity must be explicitly authored by state domains rather than
  inferred from clocks. This covers custom Qwen3 TTS state, dual-clock Fish S2,
  fixed recurrent/ring/cross-attention state, and duplicate capability pools.
- No product files were changed. The two existing pure planner/production-cost
  regressions used during the investigation passed; implementation and complete
  verification remain a separate phase.

Implementation checklist:
- [x] Commit backend-neutral managed logical reach so CPU/Metal fixed arenas are
      sized to the loaded effective context while CUDA remains growable.
- [x] Replace provenance-losing numeric defaults with an Auto/Explicit context
      policy, retaining backward-compatible positive numeric configuration.
- [x] Author explicit elastic capacity bindings for context-sized state and
      migrate every retained/invocation topology without changing fixed clocks.
- [x] Add a pure shared-memory planner that sums exact resident state,
      invocation multiplicity, execution workspace, and a configurable reserve.
- [x] Resolve and seal one effective context per model generation; consume it
      in managed/invocation allocation, prefix policy, and request/output limits.
- [x] Make failed portable planning authoritative before Ready publication and
      synchronize Metal state before publishing a generation.
- [x] Verify deterministic budget matrices, representative model topologies,
      request boundaries, CPU/Metal compilation, and unchanged CUDA contracts.
- [x] Commit each independently reviewable vertical slice and record SHAs and
      exact verification evidence in this review.

Implementation review:
- Managed CPU/Metal arenas now use the fitted loaded-model reach. The Qwen3
  4B/8B production geometry regression proves a 4,096-token context allocates
  64 pages / 576 MiB instead of 1,024 pages / 9 GiB.
- Missing context is Auto, legacy positive numerics remain Explicit, and the
  resolved value is published per loaded generation and used by chat, ASR, and
  adaptive TTS request/output boundaries. Explicit contexts are not silently
  reduced; CUDA retains its native-context and growable-arena behavior.
- Invocation state uses authored DecoderContext bindings. Fixed encoder,
  codebook, ring, recurrent, and tensor domains are not inferred from their
  clocks or shortened accidentally. Exact slot and capability multiplicity is
  included in portable fitting.
- Planning uses the stable shared CPU/Metal capacity domain, subtracts tracked
  residency, retains explicit operator budgets, and keeps a configurable 1 GiB

# Audit Portable Model-Load Regressions — 2026-08-12

Goal: explain the Qwen3 ASR missing-context failure and Parakeet Metal OOM,
identify every model exposed to the same failure classes, and design a
model-general correction without changing production code in this phase.

Research checklist:
- [x] Trace Qwen3 ASR context metadata from GGUF/config loading through its
      retained and invocation capacity contracts.
- [x] Quantify Parakeet model/state allocations and locate the command-buffer
      synchronization point that reports the Metal OOM.
- [x] Inventory all model families for optional/missing context metadata,
      fixed eager tensor/static state, and loads not covered by context fitting.
- [x] Separate corrupted/unsupported artifacts from planner regressions and
      true model-too-large failures using exact byte formulas.
- [x] Specify logical implementation commits and deterministic plus hardware
      regression coverage while preserving CUDA behavior.

Review:
- The catalog Qwen3-ASR GGUF physically omits both context keys accepted by the
  loader. The official 0.6B and 1.7B text configs declare 65,536 tokens, so the
  failure is an artifact/provenance integration defect, not bad user input.
- Qwen3 ASR also exposes a second latent defect: portable fitting sizes its
  retained cache first, then reuses that context for a separate offline
  invocation cache without fitting their aggregate. At 4,096 tokens each cache
  is 448 MiB; native 65,536 would be 7 GiB each.
- Parakeet has only 12,800 bytes of invocation state per scalar slot. Its OOM
  therefore comes from queued F32 model-weight materialization or existing
  Metal pressure and is merely surfaced by the invocation arena's first global
  synchronization. A preceding failed load can leave queued Metal work until
  that same barrier.
- The portable fitter returns immediately for fixed-only Parakeet, Nemotron,
  and Sortformer state. Model residency uses catalog total-inference estimates
  as if they were exact model bytes (Parakeet is charged 12 GiB), while the
  shared-memory advisory authority cannot trigger memory-based LRU eviction.
- The remediation must resolve artifact capacity provenance, plan one aggregate
  generation before any device allocation, derive model residency from tensor
  inventories, preflight fixed-only state, synchronize before publication, and
  quarantine a Metal backend after a command-buffer OOM. CUDA admission remains
  unchanged.

# Production Inference Readiness Audit — 2026-08-23

Status: research, analysis, and planning only; no product-code changes authorized.

Goal: identify and rank the five highest-impact gaps that prevent real clients
from safely operating Izwi as a production inference engine, using current
source, tests, deployment assets, and executable evidence rather than roadmap
claims.

Research checklist:
- [x] Map public inference routes, model/runtime architecture, scheduling,
      resource management, and deployment topology.
- [x] Audit correctness, model capability truth, concurrency, cancellation,
      memory safety, and throughput behavior in the inference runtime.
- [x] Audit authentication, tenancy, quotas, input limits, failure semantics,
      API compatibility, and service lifecycle behavior at the HTTP boundary.
- [x] Audit metrics, tracing, health/readiness, configuration, persistence,
      packaging, CI, soak/load tests, and hardware certification evidence.
- [x] Reproduce or statically prove the most consequential gaps, distinguish
      blockers from improvements, and rank the top five by client impact.
- [x] Produce a phased remediation plan with acceptance criteria and record the
      exact evidence reviewed below.

Review:
- Scope: current `improve-kv-pagedattention` worktree at `a3bb751e`; source,
  tests, deployment assets, CI definitions, benchmark gates, and documented
  compatibility contracts were reviewed. No production code was changed.
- Existing foundations are substantial: managed KV/session fencing, transaction
  rollback and cleanup, bounded stream channels, continuous decode batching for
  five chat families, guarded CUDA memory admission, SQLite WAL, durable batch
  leases, Prometheus telemetry, backend compilation/device workflows, and
  graceful SIGTERM handling. These were not reported as missing features.
- Ranked blocker 1: the shipped binary installs anonymous/allow-all/no-op auth,
  policy, audit, governance, and quota hooks. Routes expose the data and model
  administration planes together, quota evaluation is never called, persisted
  objects are not owner/tenant scoped, and the server defaults to `0.0.0.0`.
  A real multi-client deployment therefore has no enforceable security, tenant,
  administrative, usage, or cost boundary.
- Ranked blocker 2: physical backend work is deliberately serialized. Native
  continuous batching is limited to five chat families; Qwen TTS, realtime ASR,
  and the scalar fallback advertise no native batching, the static tensor batch
  executor is not implemented, and inter-request parallelism defaults to one.
  Long audio/prefill operations can head-of-line block unrelated clients, with
  no release-gated concurrency SLO proving acceptable C4/C8/C16 behavior.
- Ranked blocker 3: overload, deadline, and fault containment are incomplete.
  HTTP admission semaphores wait without queue bounds or deadlines; configured
  request timeouts are not propagated to chat/Responses/OpenAI ASR runtime
  contexts; blocking native work detaches at timeout but keeps its singleton
  execution permit; deterministic engine-step errors retry indefinitely while
  readiness can remain green. A burst or one wedged operation can exhaust
  connections/memory or stall every client instead of returning a bounded 429,
  503, or timeout.
- Ranked blocker 4: CPU and Metal resource admission is advisory unless the
  operator supplies an explicit memory budget. Without one, ledger domains use
  `u64::MAX` and planning ignores live available memory. Co-located/containerized
  deployments can swap, allocation-fail, or be killed by the OS instead of
  rejecting work before model/context allocation; CUDA is more strictly guarded.
- Ranked blocker 5: the shipped deployment is neither durable nor reproducible.
  The image advertises a config file that `izwi-server` does not read; Compose
  mounts `/app/data` while default SQLite/media resolve elsewhere; Responses and
  agent sessions are process-local; all replicas use the same batch worker ID;
  readiness can be green with no loaded model and `/v1/models` advertises catalog
  models rather than immediately servable ones. In addition, only one model
  variant is revision pinned and manifests contain no content hashes, so a fixed
  server release does not identify the inference bytes it executes.
- Phase 0 acceptance: protect every non-probe route; implement API-key/OIDC auth,
  admin RBAC, immutable tenant ownership, object-scoped queries, quota/rate
  enforcement, audit events, and adversarial cross-tenant tests. Default to
  loopback or require an explicit insecure remote opt-in.
- Phase 1 acceptance: create one absolute deadline before body work/admission,
  bound global and tenant queues, return structured 429/503 plus `Retry-After`,
  propagate cancellation through model load/preprocess/execute/stream delivery,
  add native-call watchdog isolation, classify step failures, and prove a bad or
  noisy request cannot stall unrelated work.
- Phase 2 acceptance: enforce cgroup/live-headroom-aware CPU/Metal budgets and
  implement native multi-row execution for priority chat, ASR, and TTS paths.
  Gate releases on C1/C4/C8/C16 throughput, p95/p99 TTFT/TPOT/end-to-end latency,
  accelerator utilization, RSS/VRAM, OOM, cancellation, and hours-long soak
  thresholds per supported model/backend/hardware profile.
- Phase 3 acceptance: make the stock container load and strictly validate its
  resolved config, persist SQLite/media on the advertised volume, use unique
  replica identities, support shared durable state where retrieval is claimed,
  report readiness only after required models are loaded and warmed, and pass
  two-replica recreate/failover/rolling-upgrade/backup-restore tests.
- Phase 4 acceptance: pin every primary and auxiliary model repository to an
  immutable revision; verify SHA-256 and size on download and load; publish a
  signed artifact bill of materials and exact-image SBOM/provenance; retain
  accuracy gates (WER/CER, DER/JER, alignment, TTS intelligibility/similarity,
  chat task quality) plus performance/fault evidence against the exact release.

# Plan — Remove the Physical Inference Serialization Bottleneck — 2026-08-23

Status: production-safe execution substrate implemented; CPU Whisper is the
first concurrent certificate, while Metal/CUDA and unsupported native-static
families remain deliberately fail-closed pending hardware/model evidence.

## Outcome and design decision

The target is not unrestricted parallel model calls. It is a bounded,
contract-driven execution broker that can keep multiple independent client
requests making progress while preserving one logical state writer and exact
session serialization. Throughput should come first from compatible native
tensor batches, continuous or chunk-level interleaving at proven safe points,
and bounded host-side overlap. Multiple accelerator launches may overlap only
after a specific adapter/backend/hardware combination proves that its model
state, streams, allocator, workspace, and cache ownership are independent.

Do not begin by deleting `Engine::step_gate`, increasing semaphore counts, or
turning the serial batch loop into `join_all`. Chat, TTS, and ASR currently
remove exact session state from executor maps during a forward, while cleanup
interprets a missing entry as confirmed release. The global gate currently
prevents that race. Explicit in-flight state ownership is therefore a hard
prerequisite to every concurrency change below.

The steady-state flow will be:

`scheduler/direct producers -> exact batch lanes -> deadline-aware cohort
formation -> weighted execution-group broker -> backend lane -> fenced result
-> serialized core commit`

The first production version will still permit only one physical accelerator
launch per execution group. It removes request-wide serialization by forming
real native batches, interleaving resumable work, independently committing
finished dispatches, and overlapping bounded CPU preparation/post-processing.
CPU row-parallel inference can be enabled earlier for adapters that prove
reentrancy. CUDA multi-stream overlap is a later optimization; Metal stays at
one physical launch until independently certified.

## Evidence and constraints

- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/mod.rs`: `step_gate` spans prepare, execute, and
  commit, and also protects abort and lifecycle operations.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/runtime/coordinator.rs`: an engine step acquires the
  complete backend execution budget rather than a single dispatch lease.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/core.rs`: batch formation deliberately retains
  one physical launch and rolls back/defer all other assemblies.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/execution_group.rs`: physical batches are awaited
  serially on every backend.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/executor.rs`: default CPU, CUDA, and Metal
  inter-request parallelism is one; Metal is clamped to one.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/runtime/adapters/loaded.rs`: native continuous batching
  exists for five chat families, but Qwen TTS, realtime ASR, and scalar
  fallbacks are exclusive or width one.
- `crates/izwi-core/src/engine/executor.rs`: the production static-batch branch
  accepts the TTS shape but returns that no loaded physical implementation is
  registered. The test-only static adapter is not evidence of model-level B>1.
- `handler_chat.rs`, `handler_tts.rs`, and `handler_asr.rs` temporarily remove
  state during forward; `UnifiedExecutor::cleanup_session` treats absence as a
  successful release.
- Existing `StageDescriptor`, `ExecutionProfile`, `BatchLaneKey`, `PlanId`,
  cache reservations, stream fences, and `FailureScope`/`HealthImpact` types
  provide most of the contract vocabulary. The missing layer is an independent,
  safely owned physical dispatch transaction and an execution-group broker.

## Protected invariants

- [ ] Exactly one active `PlanId`/quantum may mutate an exact `SessionKey`.
- [ ] A result commits only against its exact batch, plan, session epoch, model
      instance/load generation, adapter ABI, and cache reservation.
- [ ] Managed KV, model leases, invocation slots, workspace, and backend permits
      remain owned until physical completion, including error, panic, timeout,
      cancellation, or a dropped caller future.
- [ ] Only `NotStarted` work can be replayed or rerouted. `Started` or
      `ProducedOutput` work must never be silently retried.
- [ ] Stream progress is committed before delivery, remains monotonic per
      session, cannot be overtaken by the final event, and stays byte-bounded.
- [ ] Same-session state mutation, realtime input push/finish order, model
      load/drain/unload, and stages without a declared safe point stay serial.
- [ ] Direct runtime work and scheduler work share one finite, fair physical
      capacity policy; neither can bypass or starve the other.
- [ ] Existing CPU/Metal model-load admission policy is unchanged by this plan.

## Work packages and dependencies

### WP0 — Establish contract truth and a reproducible baseline

- [ ] Generate a checked support matrix for every enabled model family,
      capability, dtype, and backend: `Exclusive`, independent row-parallel,
      native `Static`, or native `Continuous`; record its safe point, shape and
      padding rules, maximum physical width, workspace, state ownership, and
      whether streaming is incremental or final-output chunking.
- [ ] Fail closed: an unknown or incomplete loaded-adapter contract is
      execution-group exclusive. Configuration may lower a sealed limit but
      never expand it.
- [ ] Separate the following capacity axes in configuration and telemetry:
      tensor batch width, scalar row fan-out, inter-batch physical concurrency,
      CPU intra-op threads, invocation slots, and transient workspace.
- [ ] Add baseline metrics before behavior changes: lane depth/bytes, cohort
      formation delay, permit wait, dispatch kind and width, fill/padding ratio,
      active dispatches, workspace current/high-water, head-of-line deferrals,
      cancellation phase/latency, abandoned compute, scalar-fallback reason,
      TTFT, TPOT, and end-to-end latency.
- [ ] Capture exact-SHA and immutable-model-artifact baselines at C1/C4/C8/C16
      for chat, TTS, ASR, and mixed traffic on the intended CPU, Metal, and CUDA
      hardware profiles.

Exit gate: the matrix, metrics, workloads, thresholds, and artifact identities
are checked in; no GA route silently falls back to scalar execution without a
bounded reason metric and an explicit policy.

### WP1 — Make executor state safe while a model call is in flight

Dependency: WP0 contract types and metrics. This must land before overlap.

- [ ] Replace removable session-map entries with an explicit slot lifecycle,
      such as `Ready(State) | InFlight { generation, cleanup_requested }`, for
      chat, TTS, ASR, and every equivalent mutable adapter state.
- [ ] Introduce an RAII state lease that owns the checked-out state and must
      restore, finalize, or poison the exact slot on success, error, panic, task
      cancellation, or executor drop.
- [ ] Replace boolean cleanup confirmation with a typed result such as
      `Released | BusyInFlight | Unconfirmed`; make cleanup idempotent.
- [ ] Add a core in-flight registry keyed by `BatchId` plus exact row fences.
      Cleanup, abort, unload, cache release, and quarantine clearing must consult
      both core and executor ownership.
- [ ] Enforce existing `FailureScope` and `HealthImpact`: an unhealthy execution
      group stops new dispatches, fails or drains scoped waiters, affects
      readiness, and requires explicit recovery.
- [ ] Add deterministic barrier tests for cleanup-during-forward,
      cancellation, unload/reload, stale completion, panic/drop, duplicate
      completion, and exact zero lease/cache/workspace residue.

Exit gate: every active physical call remains visible and owned for its entire
lifetime; cleanup cannot report success for in-flight state.

### WP2 — Ticketize prepare/execute/commit without changing serial behavior

Dependency: WP1.

- [ ] Introduce `PreparedPhysicalDispatch`/`DispatchTxn` containing the
      monotonic dispatch sequence, `BatchId`, complete `PhysicalBatch`, exact
      row plans, model/adapter/load-generation fences, immutable request
      snapshots and leases, managed-cache reservations, progress barrier,
      deadline/cancellation handles, launch policy, required units, invocation
      slots, and workspace demand.
- [ ] Give each ticket an RAII rollback path so a failed submit or dropped task
      cannot strand scheduler plans, KV reservations, or stream fences.
- [ ] Mark every submitted quantum in flight, including decode. Repeated
      scheduling must not construct a second plan for an active session.
- [ ] Split whole-step commit into per-dispatch commit and a separate terminal
      outbox drain. Independent sessions may commit in completion order while
      all core mutations remain under the single logical writer.
- [ ] Remove the one-assembly truncation and phase barrier only in an observe
      mode that computes proposed dispatches but still executes one at a time.
- [ ] Prove serial parity for token IDs, output hashes, progress ordering, cache
      receipts, scheduler fairness, cancellation, and lifecycle behavior.

Exit gate: serial mode uses independent tickets and produces byte-for-byte or
declared numerical-equivalent behavior with zero leaked transactions.

### WP3 — Add one bounded, weighted execution-group broker

Dependency: WP2. Physical launch concurrency remains one in this package.

- [ ] Replace step-wide coordinator acquisition with a per-ticket lease whose
      units reflect its sealed launch contract: a native tensor batch normally
      consumes one launch unit, row-parallel scalar execution consumes its row
      units, and group-exclusive work consumes all units.
- [ ] Route engine inference and direct TTS/ASR/realtime/diarization/alignment
      stages through the same bounded admission policy.
- [ ] Preserve scheduler weighted fairness and add workload-class-aware
      deficit/aging for direct stages so an exclusive waiter cannot be bypassed
      indefinitely.
- [ ] Use existing exact `BatchLaneKey` compatibility and implement
      `max_formation_delay` with earliest-deadline slack. Interactive and
      realtime traffic starts at zero or a very small delay; no cohort may wait
      past its request deadline.
- [ ] Acquire permits before workspace and device entry; retain coordinator,
      invocation, workspace, model, and KV ownership until actual completion.
- [ ] Use separate bounded pools for feature extraction, tokenization,
      decoding, encoding, and I/O so host work can overlap the single device
      lane without exhausting memory or starving model execution.
- [ ] Convert worker panic or channel loss into a synthetic, fully fenced batch
      failure; a task may not disappear without a completion record.

Exit gate: all physical work uses one broker; serial accelerator output remains
identical, host/device idle gaps decrease, and queue/fairness/resource metrics
stay within their declared bounds.

### WP4 — Enable certified CPU concurrency and native static batches

Dependency: WP3 plus a passing contract/correctness certificate per adapter.

- [ ] Enable CPU independent-row execution only for adapters that prove
      reentrant per-row state. Auto-cap row fan-out so
      `inter_op_parallelism * model_intra_op_threads` does not exceed the
      container/cgroup CPU allocation. Whisper is a candidate because its
      current contract permits independent CPU rows while rejecting native
      tensor batching.
- [ ] Keep Metal and CUDA scalar fallback at width one in this package.
- [ ] Replace the central, dormant static-TTS branch with a model-owned physical
      stage executor registration. A loaded adapter may publish `Static` only
      when its actual model kernels accept and correctly split B>1 tensors.
- [ ] Select the first static family only after a B>1 spike proves parity and
      useful gain. Prefer atomic non-streaming TTS with a true batch dimension
      or an ASR encoder. Do not reactivate Qwen TTS or Whisper native batching
      while their present batch-size-one/reject contracts remain true.
- [ ] Implement exact cohort keys for model instance/ABI/backend/dtype/options/
      state schema plus modality shape buckets, padding masks and ceilings.
- [ ] Return per-row output, error, state, usage, and cancellation. After device
      entry, a failed physical batch must not silently re-execute scalar rows.
- [ ] ASR batches must bucket duration/frame count, carry real attention masks,
      split timestamps correctly, and bound padding. TTS cohorts must match
      voice/reference/codec/sample-rate and preserve voice isolation.

Exit gate: CPU overlap and the first static family pass their independent
correctness, memory, latency, and goodput gates; uncertified routes remain
exclusive with no public capability overclaim.

### WP5 — Make long-running modality work preemptible at semantic safe points

Dependency: WP3; each model-family change is independently certifiable.

- [ ] Protect the existing five-family continuous chat decode path and add
      deadline-aware cohort formation. Add chunked/static prefill only for a
      family that proves resumability, position accounting, and KV correctness.
- [ ] Refactor Qwen3 TTS toward continuous token/frame batching only after
      talker, predictor, tokenizer, KV, and codec state are isolated per row and
      the full model owns a real B>1 path.
- [ ] Route Kokoro's existing chunk yields through the broker with a bounded
      chunk quantum. Classify whole-utterance-then-final-chunk TTS families as
      long atomic/background work rather than low-latency streaming.
- [ ] Batch ASR encoders first. Make long-form ASR yield between bounded chunks;
      continuous decoder batching waits for proven per-row decoder state.
- [ ] Keep realtime ASR push/finish order exclusive initially. Any later packet
      microbatching may occur only at an input safe point with deadline slack
      and must never drop audio.
- [ ] Represent diarization/alignment pipelines as durable stage DAGs. Host
      branches may overlap; device launches on the same group remain serial,
      while branches on distinct execution groups may run concurrently with
      combined reservation and real cancellation.
- [ ] Add a temporal streaming test that blocks generation after the first
      committed delta and proves the client receives that delta before the
      model is allowed to finish.

Exit gate: long jobs yield at declared safe points or are isolated as atomic
background work; interactive traffic has a bounded head-of-line delay.

### WP6 — Optional CUDA physical-launch overlap and multi-device lanes

Dependency: WPs 1–5 and evidence that native batching/interleaving is
insufficient. This is not a GA prerequisite for resolving the blocker.

- [ ] Add a launch policy distinct from row batchability:
      `ExecutionGroupExclusive | ModelExclusive | Concurrent { max_inflight,
      units_per_dispatch }`.
- [ ] Implement explicit CUDA streams/events and prove allocator, scratch
      workspace, model mutation, invocation slots, and managed-cache ownership
      are isolated. Start with `max_inflight = 2` for one allowlisted family.
- [ ] Require separate certification for prefill/decode overlap and cross-model
      overlap; neither follows from ordinary row batchability.
- [ ] Give each physical device its own broker. Multi-device DAG branches may
      overlap only when all device and host reservations are acquired safely.
- [ ] Keep Metal group-exclusive until a separate backend-specific certificate
      demonstrates safe overlap; use native batching and host/device pipelining
      for Metal throughput in the meantime.

Exit gate: a device timeline proves real physical overlap, output/caches remain
correct under reverse-order completion and injected faults, and the result beats
native-serial goodput without violating memory or tail-latency budgets.

### WP7 — Rollout, certification, and removal of the global gate

Dependency: WP1–WP5 for general availability; WP6 only for concurrent CUDA.

- [ ] Ship independent controls:
      `native_batching_mode = off|shadow|on`,
      `physical_execution_mode = serial|shadow|concurrent`, and
      `max_physical_batches_in_flight`, defaulting to one. An emergency serial
      override wins over every adapter certificate.
- [ ] Attribute gains with four benchmark cells: scalar-serial, native-serial,
      scalar-parallel, and native-parallel. Do not call native batching a
      concurrency win or vice versa.
- [ ] Bind each allowlist certificate to git SHA, binary/image digest,
      Cargo.lock/toolchain, model repository/revision/hash, adapter ABI, dtype,
      complete settings, workload hash/seed, exact hardware, driver, and OS.
- [ ] Roll out per model/backend/hardware profile: off -> shadow -> canary ->
      partial -> default. Never enable a broad backend such as all CUDA devices
      from one model certificate.
- [ ] On rollback, stop new concurrent submissions, drain at physical safe
      points, force serial, then disable native batching if needed. Replay only
      work proven `NotStarted`.
- [ ] Migrate abort, cleanup, synchronization, cache lifecycle, shutdown, and
      unload to the in-flight registry. Delete `step_gate` only after every
      caller has an explicit lifecycle/drain mechanism and serial mode no
      longer depends on it.
- [ ] Retain the serial implementation and kill switch for at least two
      releases after the final family becomes default-on.

Exit gate: certified profiles are default-on, uncertified profiles fail closed
to serial execution, rollback is rehearsed, and no lifecycle path relies on a
request-wide inference mutex.

## Verification and promotion gates

### Deterministic correctness and fault tests

- [ ] At capacity two, two disjoint tickets reach a barrier executor before
      release; serial mode admits exactly one. Same-session work never overlaps.
- [ ] Complete B before A and prove B can commit/deliver while A stays valid;
      both plans, cache reservations, permits, slots, and workspaces drain to
      zero afterward.
- [ ] Cleanup during chat/TTS/ASR forward returns `BusyInFlight`; unload marks a
      model draining, rejects new tickets, waits for exact old-generation work,
      synchronizes, and only then frees state.
- [ ] Queued cancellation never calls the model. Running cancellation holds all
      resources until the model call actually ends. Paused-time tests distinguish
      dispatch-wait deadlines from model-execution deadlines.
- [ ] Reverse-order completion, duplicate/stale results, row failure,
      execution-group-fatal failure, OOM, task panic, progress-channel closure,
      and dropped caller futures preserve exact fencing and leak nothing.
- [ ] Row cancellation or failure cannot alter sibling output/state. A stream
      delivery failure affects only its exact session.
- [ ] Invocation-slot exhaustion defers rather than surfacing as model failure;
      coordinator and workspace high-water marks never exceed configured caps.
- [ ] Direct and engine work share capacity without starvation; weighted
      classes retain service under mixed chat/audio load.

### Real-model correctness

- [ ] Compare scalar and batched logits with predeclared dtype-specific
      tolerances; require exact greedy tokens and fixed per-request RNG streams
      for stochastic parity. Retain token IDs and output hashes as artifacts.
- [ ] TTS gates include intelligibility, speaker/voice isolation, duration and
      codec correctness; no row may borrow another row's reference state.
- [ ] ASR gates include no more than 0.2 percentage-point WER regression,
      timestamp p95 drift no greater than 40 ms, and padding no greater than 25%
      for the certified workload.
- [ ] Streaming tests prove monotonic per-row chunks and genuine first-delta
      delivery before completion, not post-hoc chunking of a final output.

### Performance and resource gates

- [ ] Run C1/C4/C8/C16 for every benchmark cell in a fresh process, with a
      synchronized arrival barrier, at least three repetitions, and at least 30
      measured completions after warmup. Include uniform, ragged, membership
      churn, cancellation/deadline, blocked-stream, injected-fault, load/unload,
      and mixed-modality workloads.
- [ ] At C1, candidate p95/p99 TTFT and end-to-end latency are no worse than
      1.05x serial and throughput is at least 0.98x.
- [ ] At C4/C8/C16, default-on requires at least 1.10x aggregate goodput over
      the relevant prior mode, p99 no worse than 1.10x, and the worst admitted
      row no worse than 1.25x its cohort median. A family that misses the gain
      remains serial rather than adding complexity without client benefit.
- [ ] Chat C8 additionally targets native width greater than one on at least 50%
      of eligible launches and at least 25% throughput gain over width one.
- [ ] The first TTS and ASR native paths each require at least 20% throughput
      gain; TTS p95 may regress no more than 20%, subject to its quality gates.
- [ ] Peak RSS/VRAM/workspace stays within the declared profile budget and no
      more than 1.15x the matched baseline. After soak, residual growth is at

## Recommended implementation slices

1. WP0 plus the contract/telemetry portion of WP1: no behavior change.
2. Complete WP1 and its deterministic race/lifecycle suite.
3. WP2 ticketization in strict serial mode and prove parity.
4. WP3 broker with one accelerator launch plus host overlap and formation delay.
5. WP4 CPU row concurrency and one real native-static model family.
6. WP5 model-family safe-point work, independently shipped by modality.
7. WP7 staged enablement; undertake WP6 only if measured demand justifies it.

Implementation approval checkpoint: review and approve this architecture and
the WP0/WP1 slice before changing runtime behavior.

## Plan review

- This plan addresses blocker 2 without broadening into the separate auth,
  general ingress/deadline, memory-admission, or deployment-durability blockers.
  It uses execution deadlines, fairness, cancellation, and bounded queues only
  where required to make physical dispatch safe for real clients.
- It preserves the working continuous chat path and deliberately refuses to
  advertise static/native batching until an enabled model implementation—not a
  test adapter or descriptor alone—executes real B>1 tensors.
- The shortest safe client-visible win is: explicit in-flight ownership,
  independent dispatch tickets, a shared broker with one device launch,
  certified CPU row parallelism, then one real static ASR or TTS family.
- Implementation landed as logical commits from `130d092f` through
  `bb3c8366`: contract axes and rollout controls, bounded telemetry, executor
  in-flight ownership, sealed launch certification, exact dispatch tickets,
  one fair broker shared by engine/direct work, bounded CPU row parallelism,
  and policy-aware concurrent execution with stable result order.
- Serial remains the default and emergency fallback. Shadow owns multiple
  exact candidates but launches them serially. Concurrent mode overlaps only
  sealed compatible tickets; group-exclusive work, Metal, CUDA, TTS native
  static claims, and unknown profiles remain serialized.
- Verification: `cargo test -p izwi-core --lib -- --quiet` passed 1,996 tests
  with 7 environment/model-dependent tests ignored. Focused tests cover FIFO
  weighted admission, shared direct/engine capacity, peak concurrent activity,
  exclusive serialization, row-unit caps, reverse completion ordering,
  stale/duplicate completions, and exact incremental-progress fences.
- Remaining promotion work is evidence-gated rather than silently enabled:
  real-hardware C1/C4/C8/C16 benchmarks and soak certificates, a genuine
  model-owned B>1 static implementation, modality safe-point expansions, and
  optional CUDA stream overlap. The global lifecycle gate is retained until
  independent per-dispatch commit/drain replaces its final lifecycle role.

### Review result

- Promotion is blocked: `cargo check -p izwi-cli --tests` fails because both new
  runtime fields are missing from CLI configuration projections/fixtures.
- Serial mode is not an authoritative physical rollback switch. Scalar row
  workers can still fan out, and all CPU scalar adapters receive independent
  width rather than only the certified Whisper route.
- The shared broker enforces a global weighted capacity but not the concurrent
  policy's per-model limit across engine and direct calls.
- Engine work reserves workspace before it owns execution capacity; deadline
  and whole-envelope cancellation are also not rechecked after permit grant.
- Concurrent execution still has a whole-step ordered commit barrier, so a fast
  independent ticket cannot deliver or drain before an earlier slow ticket.
- Group-exclusive compatibility is currently engine-wide, preventing the
  intended cross-execution-group overlap.
- Spawned physical launch tasks are not structurally owned if the runner future
  is dropped, and task panics are converted to non-poisoning row failures.
- Shadow mode does not evaluate the concurrent planner, several declared
  fallback/defer metrics have no production callers, and reported effective
  capacity does not describe the shared broker or direct work.
- The CPU Whisper allowlist is a static tuple backed by synthetic tests; the
  exact-release real-model parity, resource, benchmark, and soak certificate
  required by the plan does not exist yet.

Verification evidence: the prior core library run passed 1,996 tests (7

prepared-order return. The CLI check failed with two E0063 errors, so a

### Primitive review

- Preparation has a distinct work identity and state; it cannot match decoder
  prefill.
- Native dispatch requires an exact loaded generation, exact preparation
  selector, execution-group domain, native/batchable certification, bounded
  width and known workspace, and retains every row lease through completion.
- The minimum row deadline fences the whole physical batch.
- Admission handoff rejects cloned leases, removes preparation queue/lane
  eligibility while retaining its resource reservation in a drain-visible
  bridge, then atomically adopts that reservation into a fresh observed
  execution admission without relabelling. Failed admissions return the live
  bridge for ordered artifact-then-reservation release.
- Preparation rows use coordinator-issued seals bound to the exact job and
  loaded adapter/stage; callers cannot self-assert identity.
- Cross-request batch formation and row cancellation/artifact delivery remain
  Qwen integration work; this slice supplies the authenticated dispatch and
  lifecycle primitives only.

## Retained static-attention sidecar prerequisite — 2026-08-25

### Retained static-attention review

- Static initialization is immutable and one-shot. A transaction consumes a
  free physical slot and atomically promotes it at commit; it never dirties an
  already published reader. Therefore committed plus active staging slots are
  exactly bounded by sequence capacity, without a hidden second allocation.
- CPU distinct-memory batching validates the complete canonical row partition
  and every retained identity before invoking any row. Metal/CUDA deliberately
  reject this new batch API until an exact multi-memory kernel is published.
- No Whisper adapter/contract or chat route was changed in this prerequisite.
- Review correction: staging holds the authenticated state map through the
  arena write, so abort/reuse cannot create a physical-slot ABA. Closing is
  checked at begin linearization, not only sequence registration.
- Review correction: exact materialized bytes are recorded before owner
  publication, and failure drops the runtime/lease without generation advance.
- Review correction: allocation selects and authenticates one retained static
  domain/group from a full mixed paged plan while retaining the full contract
  and resolved-plan identity.

# Plan — Remove Vendored Candle Metal Kernels — 2026-09-01

Scope: research, analysis, and planning only. Identify the commit and rationale
that introduced `third_party/candle-metal-kernels-0.11.0`, map its complete
build/runtime dependency surface, evaluate non-vendored alternatives, and
produce a verified migration/removal plan. Do not change dependency manifests,
source code, lockfiles, or the `third_party/` tree in this task.

- [x] Trace the introducing commit and reconstruct its technical intent.
- [x] Map every manifest, lockfile, build, CI, and runtime consumer.
- [x] Evaluate upstream, registry, Git, and local-generation alternatives.

      `third_party/` in a follow-up task.

## Review

- Introduced by `3d20ce1c277e55d7bb06ca76998698ff7bc89948`
  (`fix(metal): preserve pre-macOS 15 device support`). The only semantic delta
  from published `candle-metal-kernels 0.11.0` is an Objective-C class
  availability guard before constructing the macOS-15-only residency-set
  descriptor; the fallback keeps Metal device creation working on Izwi's
  supported macOS 12-14 releases.
- The global path patch affects Cargo resolution on every platform. It forced
  both CPU and CUDA Docker builders to copy a Metal-only dependency, while the
  lockfile lost its registry source/checksum. Izwi does not directly consume
  the patched residency API; Candle invokes it while creating a Metal device.
- Published `0.11.0` remains the latest crate and upstream `main` still lacks
  the guard. Reverting directly to crates.io would therefore restore the
  pre-macOS-15 panic.
- A Candle fork is explicitly rejected. There is no Cargo-native way to apply
  this source patch while consuming the unchanged official crate. The selected
  design is official crates.io `0.11.0`, CPU fallback on macOS 12-14, and Metal
  acceleration only on macOS 15+.
- The follow-up must gate Metal before every device-construction route, retain
  application support on macOS 12-14, remove the root path patch and both Docker
  copies, regenerate registry provenance in `Cargo.lock`, delete `third_party/`,
  and update the documented backend contract.
- Verification must prove that macOS 12-14 selects CPU without attempting Metal
  construction, macOS 15+ still executes real Metal work, CPU/CUDA locked builds
  remain clean, and exactly one official registry-sourced kernels crate resolves.

## Implementation review

- No NVIDIA GPU or NVCC is available on this macOS host. CUDA-conditional Rust
  checks use isolated temporary PTX declarations and do not validate CUDA source,
  linking, numerics, speed or loading time. Real-device checks fail closed when
  `IZWI_REQUIRE_CUDA_TEST_DEVICE=1`; production source contains no such stubs.

  wins. The explicit provider uses F16/BF16 MMA, not native FP8 instructions.
- Graph capture uses bounded safe regions and may defer first-use work; both
  Ready and first-request latency are measured. Mutable source tiles are
  rehashed, so warm derived-cache loads still read source bytes.
- The 40 tokens/s and faster-load goals remain unmeasured acceptance gates.

## 2026-09-09 — Local media publish under confined Docker seccomp

- [x] Reproduce the long-TTS persistence failure at the exact tempfile publish boundary.
- [x] Preserve atomic no-clobber publication while falling back narrowly when renameat2 is denied.
- [x] Add regression coverage for the permission-denied fallback and destination collision.
- [x] Run focused server tests, formatting, Clippy/diff hygiene, and document the result.

Plan: keep the normal `NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber` path. When the kernel
returns permission denied for its `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` attempt, retry
with a same-filesystem hard link, which retains no-clobber semantics, then let
the temporary owner unlink its original name. Do not weaken the container
seccomp profile or replace no-clobber publication with overwrite-capable rename.

Review: the failure originates in `NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber`, whose Linux
implementation uses `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` and returns Docker/seccomp's
permission denial without attempting its hard-link fallback. Local media publish
now retries only permission-denied failures with a same-filesystem hard link and
preserves no-clobber behavior. Both new regression tests and the existing streamed
file-upload regression passed; server Clippy passed for all targets with warnings
denied, rustfmt passed, and `git diff --check` is clean. The stopped EC2 GPU instance
was not restarted, so no paid-instance deployment or end-to-end CUDA generation
was performed.

- The Phase 2 gate found and closed one control-plane identity gap: query and
  cancel now fence request, attempt, worker incarnation, deployment, and model
  generation, and cancellation distinguishes requested from execution-stopping.
  The updated protocol/client tests and server check passed.
- Phase 2 implementation should use the existing tiny, real LFM2.5 CPU GGUF
  fixture after extracting it into owning test support, then add an opaque
  runtime admitted-invocation handle. It must not acknowledge before coordinator
  admission or release capacity before the handle confirms teardown. A separate
  gateway state/router/startup branch is required; making `AppState.runtime`
  optional or constructing a fake runtime was rejected.
- Phase 2 is complete. The standalone worker verifies its artifact manifest,
  loads and warms before binding, uses the existing CPU runtime/scheduler, and
  holds authoritative capacity through confirmed teardown. Its plaintext
  private listener is loopback-only. Drain/admission serialization, finite
  attempt retention, lost-ack duplicate handling, disconnect cancellation and
  fail-closed unconfirmed teardown are covered by 11 worker tests.
- Gateway mode branches before runtime, persistence, preload, batch, or CUDA
  delegation initialization and exposes only the migrated chat route, probes,
  docs, and filtered OpenAPI. Public JSON and SSE preserve the existing response
  encoders; gateway admission is retained through an SSE body's lifetime.
- Real CPU evidence is one subprocess worker serving a generated tiny supported
  LFM2 GGUF through the in-process hardware-independent public gateway router.
  Both OpenAI-compatible JSON and SSE completed with usage. This is real CPU
  process-separation evidence, not Metal/CUDA, multi-device, performance, or
  production-readiness evidence.
- Phase 3 strict assignment commits `36a6f4a4`, `9cb40101`, and `5fee8c41`
  separate local backend preferences from production worker assignments. The
  supervisor validates a bounded, deny-unknown node schema against an injected
  inventory and executable catalog, clears/allowlists each child environment,
  maps CUDA visibility by UUID before startup, and provides exclusive resource
  plus shared generation fences. Managed workers acquire those fences before
  runtime construction, verify CPU/Metal/CUDA memory-budget environment pairs,
  and call the no-fallback runtime constructor. CUDA host memory now has an
  independent runtime cap in addition to device memory. CPU affinity is
  explicitly reported as advisory on builds that do not enforce it.
- Phase 3 checks so far: 17 supervisor tests passed; five strict core assignment
  tests passed; the strict-assignment validation and canonical CUDA UUID tests
  passed; the worker assignment mapping test and CUDA host/device cap test
  passed; and the one-subprocess tiny-LFM CPU HTTP/gateway test passed in 5.50s.
  No Metal/CUDA feature compilation or accelerator execution has been claimed.
- Phase 3 lifecycle supervision adds shell-free child launch with a parent-owned
  control pipe, exact descriptor/status readiness fencing, monotonic incarnation
  status, bounded deterministic restart backoff/quarantine, and cooperative
  drain followed by cancellation, TERM, and KILL deadlines. Managed workers
  stop admission on parent-pipe EOF and keep invocation capacity until execution
  actually tears down. The supervisor suite passed 23 tests; the worker drain
  cancellation regression and worker binary assignment test each passed.
- Phase 4 registry primitives are bounded by configured worker, deployment, and
  local-dispatch ceilings. Approved incarnations start unready, observations use
  receiver-monotonic freshness and strictly increasing status sequences, and
  selection filters exact deployment/capability/backend constraints before a
  deterministic capacity-weighted choice. Local dispatch guards reconcile only
  after a newer status sequence; the worker remains authoritative for admission.
  Eleven focused registry tests passed. Route/startup integration and concurrent
  worker admission tests remain in P4.3-P4.6.
- Phase 3 staged loading reuses core load-peak/resident memory reservations and
  serializes runtime construction, model load, and warm-up through one node-wide
  lease. Managed workers verify every lock path from their exact assignment,
  then release only the transient load lease before binding Ready. Supervisor
  configuration and resource locks reject duplicate exclusive accelerator
  assignments both within and across supervisor processes. Twenty-five
  supervisor tests and the worker binary assignment test passed.
- Native terminal packaging now includes the gateway-capable server, a CPU
  worker on Linux/Windows or Metal-capable worker on macOS, and a bounded node
  config example. Synthetic tar/zip acceptance and missing-worker/config
  rejection passed, as did the packaged-config parser test. P3.6 remains open:
  the supervisor is still library-only, actual release builds/Windows checks
  were not run, and no accelerator execution or performance evidence exists.
- A registry-backed chat dispatcher now selects exactly once, pins the selected
  incarnation/deployment/generation into the invocation, reserves local load
  before POST, and retains its guard through normal or streaming forwarding.
  A stale-load test proved an authoritative worker capacity rejection is not
  retried on the second eligible worker; a two-worker test proved deterministic
  balancing. Public gateway startup/state wiring remains open, so P4.3/P4.4 are
  not yet marked complete.
- Phase 4 topology examples use the bounded node schema for one CPU worker, one
  Metal worker, and three independently assigned CUDA workers. Four parser and
  topology assertions passed. Placeholder device IDs, budgets, paths and model
  revisions are explicitly non-runnable and provide no accelerator evidence.
- The node supervisor now has a CPU-only executable that resolves bounded
  environment-backed credentials, validates an operator-supplied CPU inventory,
  serially launches exact assignments, monitors exits, applies bounded restart
  quarantine, and drains children on signals. Its complete package suite passed
  32 tests. Metal/CUDA command-line inventory remains fail-closed and P3.6 stays
  open until native archives actually carry and smoke-check the supervisor.
- Native terminal archives now require the supervisor alongside the gateway,
  worker, bounded config example, CLI and desktop binary. POSIX shell syntax,
  release YAML parsing, and synthetic tar/zip acceptance plus missing-artifact
  rejection passed. The documented matrix keeps Windows/release-build and all
  real accelerator evidence explicitly unverified.
- The public gateway can now build a bounded registry from explicit loopback
  endpoints, poll fresh status, route JSON/SSE chat once, and reapprove only a
  matching authenticated replacement incarnation while fencing the old one.
  Worker-authoritative atomic capacity across two independent client views,
  no-retry rejection, public JSON/SSE routing, startup bounds and replacement
  identity/generation/capacity tests passed. Plaintext client endpoints are
  restricted to numeric loopback; remote TLS remains a later phase.
- The deterministic HTTP harness now distinguishes a lost acknowledgement from
  a disconnect after accepted and from a disconnect after partial output. Its
  nine-test transport suite passed: unknown acceptance was not replayed,
  authoritative capacity stayed held through confirmed cancellation teardown,
  and partial output was never fabricated as success. Circuit breaking and a
  provably pre-send alternate-dispatch path remain open in P5.4.

## P5.1a review

- Public gateway startup resolves its key through a bounded `env:VARIABLE`
  reference (default `env:IZWI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`); no public-secret CLI option
  exists. The one configured key maps to one server-authored principal, tenant,
  and fixed `inference` role/scope. Caller identity headers are discarded before
  the enterprise policy hook, which remains an additional deny/fail-closed layer.

  disabling it does not inherit the Tauri allowlist.
- New gateway 401/403/413/429/503 helpers use the existing bounded OpenAI-style
  JSON envelope. The 1 MiB default chat body cap is configurable from 1 KiB to
  32 MiB and is installed before `Json` extraction. Request IDs are restricted
  to 128 safe ASCII bytes; invalid values receive a generated UUID and 400.
- Production startup rejects enabled wildcard/empty CORS allowlists and public
  plaintext binds unless `IZWI_GATEWAY_TRUSTED_INGRESS_TLS=1` acknowledges an
  external TLS ingress. Loopback plaintext remains supported.
- Static evidence only in this workstream: direct `rustfmt` on owned leaf files
  and `git diff --check` passed. Parent integration ran
  `cargo test -p izwi-server gateway_ --lib -- --test-threads=1`: 20 passed,
  0 failed. Committed as `e700a1ae`.

  header trust, or full Phase 5 route/stream hardening.

## P6.3a review

- Existing keys are scoped only by operation/key, are inserted after graph
  creation, are not used for replay/conflict, and reads ignore expiry. Retention
  and row count are unbounded; the transcription digest also omits audio bytes.
- Existing strengths include `NamedTempFile`, media-ingest compensation,
  artifact tombstones, attempt-token publication fencing, and Fish PCM replay
  fencing. Gaps include post-ingest graph/object leaks, no generic orphan GC,
  deletion order that can lose the provider key, no startup temp sweep, and
  losing-attempt output cleanup.
- Next order: add a tenant+operation+key durable reservation/commit/replay
  contract with canonical digest, expiry and hard bounds; integrate routes;
  then add a cleanup ledger, losing-attempt cleanup and bounded startup sweep.
  P6.3 remains open.

# P6.3g — Reserved provider writes for opaque artifacts — 2026-09-13

- [x] Add an opt-in versioned provider write/recovery contract without changing legacy writes.
- [x] Persist bounded write reservations before provider I/O and consume them atomically with artifact metadata.

## P6.3g decisions

- Reserved writes carry a provider-enforced expiry. Recovery occurs only after
  that deadline, so a successful provider `NotFound` must also prove a late
  commit cannot appear for the same write ID.
- A separate table avoids weakening the existing tombstone-only cleanup
  table's SQLite check and join fences. Both ledgers share the same bounded
  maintenance call and wall-clock deadline.
- Legacy `MediaStorageProvider::put` remains intact for routes not yet migrated.
  This slice does not claim speech/media crash recovery or losing-attempt cleanup.

# P6.3g/P6.5b — Reserved provider-write recovery foundation — 2026-09-13

- [x] Add an opt-in provider capability with a bounded server write ID and
  cleanup-by-write-ID semantics that fence future publication.
- [x] Implement the contract for local storage without changing legacy provider writes.
- [x] Persist bounded pre-write reservations and claim expired cleanup with exact tokens.
- [x] Publish ArtifactStore metadata only while the reservation is still owned.
- [x] Recover crash-orphaned writes after restart and retry provider failures with bounded backoff.

  metadata/key mismatch, bounded cleanup, and schema compatibility.
- [x] Review, run serial focused checks, commit, and clean the workspace.

## P6.3g/P6.5b decisions

- A returned storage key is insufficient: it does not exist before provider
  acceptance, which is the crash window being closed. The provider contract is
  keyed by a pre-write UUID. Successful/NotFound cleanup must also fence future
  completion for that UUID; otherwise a delayed remote write could reappear.
- ArtifactStore rejects providers without this opt-in capability before sending
  bytes. Existing legacy media paths retain their current provider contract in
  this slice. Media-ingest/speech adoption and exact-attempt losing-output
  settlement are intentionally separate follow-up commits.
- Lease expiry or stale heartbeat alone never authorizes deletion. Recovery
  claims only expired write reservations, and publication must atomically prove
  the reservation remains reserved under its exact token.

## P6.3g/P6.5b review

- The opt-in v1 provider envelope binds an exact UUID, expiry, original bounded
  request metadata, declared length, and digest. Local storage serializes each
  write/recovery through one of 256 persistent lock shards and keeps no
  untracked sidecar; canonical MIME types retain their read-time identity.
- The durable reservation ledger is capped at 65,536 rows, cleanup claims at 64,
  provider calls at 30/5 seconds, and errors/keys/input fields at fixed limits.
  Publication consumes the exact stored reservation in the media-row transaction.
- Artifact tests passed 17/17, persistence tests 14/14, runtime-store tests 46/46,

# P6.2f/P6.3h — Exact stage-output ownership contract — 2026-09-13

- [x] Bound retained stage output references and require canonical unique UUIDs.
- [x] Complete a stage only when every referenced artifact is an output/debug
  row owned by the exact job, stage, attempt count, and attempt token.

## P6.2f/P6.3h decisions

- The durable store is authoritative even if an executor constructs
  `StageExecutionOutcome` directly. Validation belongs inside the same
  completion transaction after the exact active lease wins its update.
- This establishes the ownership invariant needed by a later held/disarmable
  losing-output cleanup ledger. It does not itself delete any artifact.
- `StageExecutionOutcome` is a public Rust type, but its output vector is now
  private and it no longer implements unconstrained `Deserialize`. Callers use
  `empty` or the checked `try_new` constructor. This intentional source/API
  tightening prevents bypassing the bounded typed contract; the store remains
  independently authoritative for exact ownership.

## P6.2f/P6.3h review

- Completion retains at most 64 canonical, unique UUID references. The current
  attempt must own every referenced output/intermediate/debug artifact by exact
  job, stage, attempt count, and token inside the completion transaction.
- SQLite uses the existing immediate write transaction. PostgreSQL and MySQL
  additionally lock each accepted artifact row before committing completion.

  filename, content type, metadata entry count, keys, values, and aggregate

  request exist before the durable fence without changing provider behavior.
- The envelope is an internal versioned JSON record. Version 1 retains at most
  8 KiB, 16 metadata entries, 128-byte keys, 1 KiB values, and 4 KiB aggregate
  metadata. Built-in namespaces are fixed; `Other` is capped at 128 bytes.
- Existing duplicated columns remain publication and legacy-recovery fences.
  They are checked against the persisted request rather than trusted as a
  substitute for it.
- A strict internal V1 request DTO rejects unknown outer and nested fields.
  Database reads and cleanup selection apply backend-specific byte-length SQL
  predicates before materializing envelope text: SQLite counts BLOB bytes;
  PostgreSQL/MySQL use `OCTET_LENGTH`.
- Unknown legacy and oversized rows remain durable and excluded from provider
  I/O. A bounded malformed row is transactionally moved back to cleanup-pending
  with a one-hour retry and bounded error, so it cannot roll back or starve valid
  rows in the same fixed-size maintenance batch.

## P6.1g/P6.3i review

- New ArtifactStore provider I/O begins only after the exact request envelope
  and write fence commit together. A crash/reopen test proves recovery with a
  built-in namespace and extra metadata, which the historical reconstruction
  could not reproduce.
- Serial tests passed: batch runtime store 51/51, ArtifactStore 17/17, SQLite
  schema/migration 2/2, provider-managed schema contract 2/2, and focused
  envelope/legacy/poison-row tests 1/1 each. `cargo check -p izwi-server`,
  direct rustfmt, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The first independent review found nested strictness, pre-materialization byte
  bounds, and cleanup starvation blockers. All three were fixed; independent
  re-review was clear.

# Plan — Production Serving Finding & Gap Remediation — 2026-09-19

Scope: implement the 4 code-level findings and gaps identified during the comprehensive
architecture and correctness review against IZWI_PRODUCTION_SERVING_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md:
1. Fix tenant concurrency lease leak in gateway_tenant_concurrency.rs on worker restart or timeout.
2. Align MockWorker duplicate attempt conflict semantics with the real worker (unretryable HTTP 409).
3. Bound invocation remaining time and prevent deadline Instant overflow.
4. Add randomized tie-breaking in capacity scoring when worker scores are equal.

- [x] Fix 1: Release tenant concurrency leases on worker restart (HTTP 409 CONFLICT) or orphan reconcile timeout.
- [x] Fix 2: Align MockWorker duplicate attempt handling to return unretryable HTTP 409 conflict status.
- [x] Fix 3: Enforce MAX_REMAINING_TIME_MS in InvocationRequest and use checked_add for deadline calculation.
- [x] Fix 4: Add randomized tie-breaking to capacity-weighted worker selection when scores are identical.
- [x] Verification: run test suites across all affected crates, clippy, formatting, and boundary checks.

## Remediation Review — 2026-09-19

- **Commit 1 (`2e85b1c1`):** `fix(serving): release tenant concurrency leases on worker restart or unreachable timeout`
  - Recognizes `HttpStatus` with `StatusCode::CONFLICT` (409) in `reconcile_until_stopped` as proof that the worker incarnation restarted and old execution has stopped, releasing the tenant concurrency lease.
  - Adds `MAX_RECONCILE_TIMEOUT` (60s in production, 100ms in tests) to reclaim orphan leases when worker is permanently unreachable, eliminating permanent tenant lockout under worker crash cycles.
  - Adds unit tests for both incarnation conflict and orphan timeout lease reclamation.
- **Commit 2 (`58e6c50a`):** `fix(serving): align mock worker duplicate attempt conflict status with production worker`
  - Replaces `MockWorker`'s return of `RejectionCode::CapacityExhausted` for duplicate attempts with raw HTTP 409 conflict text (`"attempt is already owned; acceptance is unknown, query or cancel it"`), matching `izwi-serving-worker` exactly.
  - Adds contract test proving duplicate attempts receive an unretryable HTTP 409 conflict.
- **Commit 3 (`60345414`):** `fix(serving): bound invocation remaining time and prevent deadline overflow`
  - Adds `MAX_REMAINING_TIME_MS = 86_400_000` (24h) in `izwi-serving-protocol` and validates it in `InvocationRequest::validate()`.
  - Replaces unchecked `+ Duration` with `Instant::now().checked_add(...)` in `WorkerClient::invoke`, preventing panics on malformed input.
  - Adds unit tests in `types.rs`.
- **Commit 4 (`137805ca`):** `feat(serving): add randomized tie-breaking to capacity scoring`
  - Adds `randomized_tie_breaking` option to `WorkerRegistryConfig` (defaults to false for deterministic test reproducibility).
  - When enabled, uses random tie-breaking (`uuid::Uuid::new_v4().as_bytes()[0] % 2 == 0`) when candidate score equals selected score, satisfying Plan Section 7.2.
  - Adds unit test proving equal workers distribute selections under randomized tie-breaking.
- **Verification:** All tests passed (izwi-serving-protocol: 16/16, izwi-serving-client: 5/5 lib + 23/23 http_contract, izwi-serving-supervisor: 42/42, izwi-serving-worker: 17/17, izwi-server gateway: 67/67, worker_registry: 21/21, check-serving-boundary passed, python benchmarks passed).

# DS1.2b — managed tensor-snapshot publication + attach-by-fork — 2026-09-23 (part 5)

Plan (from DS1_CONV_STATE_SPIKE_ANALYSIS.md requirement 2 + the DS1.2b handoff):
wire the managed cache so hybrid contracts that declare
`PrefixPolicy::CommittedSnapshots` publish committed tensor snapshots keyed by
the shared paged page-chain digest, and attaching invocations fork them
(DS1.1 prototype recipe: read -> begin -> stage_replace -> commit at the fork
cursor). DINV-02 tenant salt + model generation binding is inherited because
the snapshot key IS the page-chain digest (namespace fingerprint binds salt,
model revision, plan). Default stays off (declarations only exist behind
`enable_prefix_caching`).

Key design decisions:
- Snapshot key = digest of the last paged prefix page whose end equals the
  snapshot cursor. Tensor reuse can therefore never exceed or diverge from
  paged reuse; a miss truncates the paged match back to the nearest
  snapshot-backed boundary (sound partial reuse).
- Publish only when the fresh first-chunk commit cursor is interval-aligned
  (cursor % interval_steps == 0) and pages were accepted through that cursor.
- Strict gate `tensor_snapshot_prefix_policy`: exactly one paged-attention
  domain (CommittedPages), every tensor domain CommittedSnapshots with one
  shared interval, all in exactly one consistency group, no append/ring
  domains. Anything else stays admission-inert (MTP variant included).
- Legacy (AllDomains) transaction mode only; clocked/selected requests never
  publish or attach. Legacy commit already forces tensor cursor == paged
  accepted cursor, which the model derives from `physical_kv.context_len()`,
  so the fork needs zero model/handler changes.
- Scheduler alignment: first prefill chunk (num_computed == 0) of an
  Incremental-prefill request whose sealed contract passes the gate is clamped
  down to the interval boundary via a new ExecutionProfile field. This makes
  published snapshots reachable by longer-prompt attachers (system prompt /
  history reuse). Identical-length siblings would need zero-ingest prefill
  authority (unchanged-prefix fence) - deliberately deferred.
- Snapshot index bounds derived, no new config: entries <= arena sequence
  capacity, bytes <= authorized tensor envelope; LRU eviction on insert.

  gate (exactly one paged-attention domain with CommittedPages, every tensor
  domain CommittedSnapshots with one shared interval, one consistency group)
  + bounded LRU `TensorStateSnapshotIndex` (entries <= arena sequence
  capacity, bytes <= authorized tensor envelope, idempotent republish,
  cursor-conflict rejection).
- Snapshot keys are the paged page-chain digests at the snapshot boundary, so
  DINV-02 tenant salt + model generation binding is inherited from the

- managed.rs: sharing surface derived at bind (interval must sit on the
  resolved page grid); `finalize` publishes after the legacy tensor commit
  when the accepted cursor is the aligned boundary of accepted pages;
  `prepare_inner` reconciles the paged match by walking back to the nearest
  snapshot-backed boundary (zero reuse fallback when the session cannot fork)
  and forks via the DS1.1 recipe (read -> begin -> stage_replace -> commit at
  the fork cursor) on a fresh sequence, with full rollback on failure.
  Fork-seed transaction ids descend from u64::MAX, plan-id txns ascend.
- The post-lookup clamp only engages when nothing attached; pages the lookup
  matched but the reconcile dropped are excluded from re-publication (one
  digest must keep exactly one block binding). Saltless managers keep their
  exact pre-DS1.2b behavior (clamp gated on namespace presence).

  contract with tensor domains, closing the 9c8dc83a hybrid-attach hazard

- Scheduler: `ExecutionProfile::managed_snapshot_prefill_interval` from the
  sealed contract gate; metadata carries it; first prefill chunk
